Abandoned databanks contain detailed plans to invade [arc_site_planet.GetName] and process the population in "pain farms" to tenderize their flesh before they are consumed.

ancrel.107.junk.desc.zh: “外星信号”的源头找到了，然而这并不是什么潜伏者的外星入侵，实际上信号来自于一个远古的勘探标记，这应该是由某个自动探测装置在[From.Planet.GetName]探测出一条有价值的小矿脉后所设置的。这个标记已经受损，只能发出断断续续的微弱信号。
ancrel.107.junk.desc.en: The source of the "alien signal" has been discovered, but rather than being any sinister alien invasion force the signal originates from an ancient survey marker which was apparently set by an automated probe which had discovered a minor vein of valuable resources on [From.Planet.GetName]. The marker is damaged and transmits only intermittently and very faintly.

ancrel.107.nothing.desc.zh: 对[From.Planet.GetName]的彻查表明这里与外星生命没有任何联系。要么这里从来没有什么外星人的信号发出，要么就是某种原因使得这里没能留下任何痕迹。不管事实究竟如何，对[From.Planet.GetName]的调查还显示这里蕴含有一些矿藏。
ancrel.107.nothing.desc.en: A thorough investigation of [From.Planet.GetName] has revealed absolutely nothing related to aliens. Either there was never any alien signal originating here, or whatever caused it left without leaving any traces. However, the close inspection of [From.Planet.GetName] has revealed some minerals.

ancrel.108.desc.zh: 我们发现了被精炼过的矿物，虽然进一步研究亟待展开，但是我们初步认为这是一个巨型战场遗址。看起来，其中一方进行了轨道空降并与星球上的防御军发生了交火。进攻方为什么没有进行轨道轰炸？最后的胜利者究竟是谁？一切都悬而未决。
ancrel.108.desc.en: The refined material has been uncovered, and while further study is needed, our initial impression is that this is the remains of a vast battle site. It appears that one side descended from orbit and was engaged by planetbound defenders. Why there was no orbital bombardment and who the victor was remains unclear.

ancrel.109.desc.zh: 我们得出结论，来自“毁灭者”，即一族高维游牧民的军队入侵了[From.Planet.GetName]，入侵时此行星属于“抵抗组织”，一个由数个不同物种组成的联盟。通过零散的记录，我们认定这场战争主要是在星系的其他部分进行，而[From.Planet.GetName]是抵抗组织寄希望于在“毁灭者”的魔爪之外建立一个秘密殖民地的尝试。这场战役和战争整体的结果仍不得而知，但对战争机器残骸的研究已经获得了一些有价值的信息。
ancrel.109.desc.en: We have concluded that forces from "The Destroyers", a race of extra-dimensional nomads, invaded [From.Planet.GetName], which at the time belonged to "Those-who-resist", a coalition of several different species. From scattered records we believe that that the war was mostly fought elsewhere in the galaxy and [From.Planet.GetName] was an attempt by Those-who-resist to establish a secret colony outside the reach of The Destroyers. The outcome of this battle and the larger war remains unknown, but study of the wrecked war machines has yielded some valuable information.

ancrel.11.desc.zh: 不像先前的泽珞族星球，[From.Planet.GetName]明显是一颗核心星球，地表上存有数座城市以及大量的大小定居点。此处又同其他殖民地一样空荡，没有任何灾难亦或是死亡的迹象，这些居民的命运无从知晓。我们已经检测到数个水晶档案库的存在，将准备进行调查。
ancrel.11.desc.en: Unlike the previous Zroni worlds, [From.Planet.GetName] was clearly a core world, with several cities of varying size covering the surface. Like the others it now sits empty, showing no signs of disaster or death; the fate of its population is unknown. Several Archive crystals have been detected, and will need to be investigated.

ancrel.11000.a.zh: 那么其他层里又为我们隐藏着什么呢？
ancrel.11000.a.en: What do the other layers have in store for us?

ancrel.11000.desc.zh:
这座废墟看起来至少有成百上千年那么陈旧了。起初它看起来只是一个大型露天建筑，不过随着对外部结构发掘的深入，我们很快发现这只是一座城市中被废弃的贫民窟。有一座巨大的大门阻挡了我们深入城市的去路，我们的科学家猜想这个社会分为了数个阶层，而建筑的每一层分别居住着这座城市一个阶层的人。

我们的科学家很快就在这座地下废墟破碎的混凝土地面下发现了外星人的遗骸。然而在找到第一具遗骸过后，我们很快发现贫民窟里到处都是遗骸，有的横尸街头，有的死在家中，有的从天花板上高高地悬挂下来。虽然不知道是谁干的，但真的是一副相当令人反胃的场景。
ancrel.11000.desc.en:
The ruins seem to be centuries, if not millennia, old. At first it seems to be only a large open-air dome, but as we are excavating the outermost parts we quickly find ourselves in what appears to be the derelict slums of a city. As a large gate blocks our progress deeper into the city, our scientists speculate that it is split into a hierarchy, each layer holding one class of the people of the city.

It does not take long before one of our scientists finds alien remains in subterranean ruins under the broken concrete floor. After the first corpse is found, however, we start finding remains all over the slums, be it in the streets, in what would have been their homes, or hanging from the most remote parts of the ceiling. It is unclear what killed them, but it is a grisly sight.

ancrel.11005.desc.zh:
第一个圈子似乎是由流浪汉和贫民们摇摇欲坠的窝棚组成，而第二个圈子则与[Root.GetAdj]市政规划观念有很多一致之处。

我们发现了几个我们的科学家认为曾经是集市的开放广场，但因为年深日久，所有东西都早已腐朽到无法辨认它可能是什么的地步。

之后不久，我们也开始在圆顶的这一部分发现值得注意的遗迹。此处居民尸骸遍地，其死亡方式似乎与他们那些穷邻居差不多。
ancrel.11005.desc.en:
Whereas the first circle seemingly consisted of the ramshackle dwellings of the outcast and destitute, this second circle has more in common with the [Root.GetAdj] notion of proper urban planning.

We find several open squares our scientists assume used to be marketplaces, though anything from back then has long since decayed to the point where it is impossible to make out what it might have been.

It does not take long before we start finding unusual remains in this part of the dome too. They seem to have perished in much the same way as their poorer neighbors, and we find the dead strewn all over.

ancrel.11010.a.zh: 我们的科学家随时准备探索最后一层。
ancrel.11010.a.en: Our scientists stand ready to check the final layer.

ancrel.11010.desc.zh:
当进入第三层的大门最终打开后，我们的科学家们——带着对下一步的发现的好奇——鱼贯而入，而这里很快被确认为是该穹顶古建筑中的一个更富有的区域。我们可就此对从这座城市可能获得的发现做出更积极的期望。

进入这一层后不久，我们中的一个人突然转身，野蛮地袭击了一位同事。当该袭击者被制服时，受害者已经死在地上。此后，那位发疯的科学家一直胡言乱语，我们完全无法理解他们身上到底发生了什么。

这一层比前两层都小，很可能是我们到达圆顶中心之前的最后一层。只剩下一扇门了。
ancrel.11010.desc.en:
When the gate into the third layer finally opens, our scientists - curious about what they will find next - flood into what is soon identified as a yet wealthier region of the old dome. At this point we can make confident assumptions about what to expect from this city.

Shortly after we enter the layer, one of our people suddenly turns around and savagely attacks a colleague. The victim is already dead on the ground by the time the unexpected assailant is restrained. In the aftermath we are completely unable to get anything sensible out of the crazed scientist, and get no better understanding of what happened to them.

This layer is significantly smaller than either of the previous two, and it is most likely the final one before we reach the center of the dome. Only one gate remains.

ancrel.11015.a.zh: 让我们修一下这台机器，看看能发现什么。
ancrel.11015.a.en: Let us tinker with this machine and see what we can find.

ancrel.11015.desc.zh:
当最后一扇门开启时，强烈的灵能波冲击着我们的科学家。他们中的大多数在剧烈的痛苦中崩溃了，最终只有少数人进入了这一层。

这一层似乎是一座大寺庙，中间有一个巨大的祭台或祭坛。墙上到处都是描绘不同恒星系的巨大图表，一个重复的图表似乎围绕着[Root.System.GetName]本身。

幸存为数不多的的几位科学家向中央靠拢，他们发现这实际上是一台打造成古老祭坛形式的雄伟机器。
ancrel.11015.desc.en:
As soon as the final gate opens up, waves of intense psionic energy wash upon our scientists. Most of them collapse in apparent agony, leaving only a few to make their way into the actual layer itself.

It seems to be a large temple, with a massive dais or altar in the middle of it. All across the walls there are huge diagrams of different star systems, and a repeated one seems to center on [Root.System.GetName] itself.

Making their way closer to the middle, the few scientists that remain find that it is in fact an imposing machine fashioned in the form of an old altar.

ancrel.11020.a.zh: 拆了这台机器，以免造成更多的伤害！
ancrel.11020.a.en: Rip the machine apart before it can cause any more harm!

ancrel.11020.desc.zh: 当修理工作开始时，他们突然被一种共同的幻觉所困扰——一个正被挖出并解封的存在，尖啸着发出命令。尖啸越发刺耳，一个生物撕开[From.System.GetName]星系的景象在他们的脑海中反复上演。几位科学家不省人事，无法应对这种持续折磨他们身体疼痛。
ancrel.11020.desc.en: As they start tinkering with the machine, they are suddenly beset by a shared auditory hallucination - a screaming command by something to be unearthed, unshackled. Visions of a creature ripping apart the [From.System.GetName] system plays repeatedly in their heads as the creature's demands grow shriller. Several scientists fall unconscious, unable to deal with the unabating torrents of pain that rack their bodies.

ancrel.11020.tt.en: An $NAME_Eldritch_Horror$ will be released in the [eldritch_location.GetName] system.

ancrel.11025.a.zh: 啊，伟大的存在！来拥抱你迷途的羊群吧！
ancrel.11025.a.en: O Great One! Embrace your wayward flock!

ancrel.11025.a.tt.en: [Root.GetName] will rebuild their starbase in the [eldritch_location.GetName] system.

ancrel.11025.b.en: It was a mistake to release you.

ancrel.11025.desc.zh:
终于……

凡人，跪下！在我面前卑躬屈膝，我将赐予你佑护和智慧。

若敢不从，我将为你带来终结！
ancrel.11025.desc.en:
FINALLY...

BOW DOWN MORTALS, GROVEL BEFORE ME, AND I SHALL GRANT YOU PROTECTION AND WISDOM.

OPPOSE ME, AND I SHALL BE YOUR END!

ancrel.11027.a.zh: 一切将如您所愿，伟大的存在。
ancrel.11027.a.en: It will be as you wish, Great One.

ancrel.11027.desc.zh:
尔等既选择了智慧之路。
一切将如其之所应为。
ancrel.11027.desc.en:
SO YOU HAVE CHOSEN THE PATH OF WISDOM.
EVERYTHING IS AS IT SHOULD BE.

ancrel.11035.desc.zh: 我们与我们穿越[eldritch_location.GetName]星系的舰队失去了联系。随后，我们又收到了其中恒星坍缩和一切毁灭的消息。
ancrel.11035.desc.en: We have lost all contact with our fleet as it was traveling through the [eldritch_location.GetName] system. Shortly afterwards, we receive news about the collapse of the star and the destruction of everything around it.

ancrel.12.desc.zh:
大多数能读取的记录都着重记载了战争的过程。我们得出的结论是，人们的想愿会影响特定主题记录的“强度”，这使得大多数人关心的问题会被着重记载。并不出人意料，战争的过程在每个人的脑海中都有.

大多数泽珞族人站在福音派一方，然而，尽管福音派拥有大量的支持者，他们的局面却非常不利。升格派完全不考虑对星系产生的影响，从而可以肆无忌惮的施展他们的灵能力量，而福音派则受限于他们能从自身获取的力量的多少。

起初，这场战争似乎呈一边倒，但是福音派的一位英雄取得了一个可怕而又至关重要的发现，这使得局势变得扑朔迷离。
ancrel.12.desc.en:
Most of the accessible records focus on the course of the war. Our working theory is that the mood of the population influences the "strength" of the record about a subject, meaning the most thought-about issues are recorded with greater prominence. Unsurprisingly, the course of the war was on everyone's mind.

The majority of the Zroni sided with the Saviors, but while they had an advantage in numbers they bore one significant disadvantage: heedless of their effects on the galaxy, the Divine were free to use their full Psionic might; meanwhile the Saviors were limited to whatever power could be drawn from their own bodies.

At first the war seemed hopeless, but eventually a hero amongst the Saviors would make a terrible - yet vital - discovery.

ancrel.12000.desc.zh: [Root.Leader.GetName]与一组研究人员登上了空间站，并设法恢复了某些部分的供电。似乎在 [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]进入太空之前仅仅几个世纪就已经有人居住了。乍一看，它似乎是一个武装空间站，占其大部分体积的超大大炮证明了这一点。然而，其余大部分区域似乎都专门设计为研究设施，这表明该武器很可能是高度实验性的。
ancrel.12000.desc.en: [Root.Leader.GetName] has boarded the station with a team of researchers and managed to restore power to some sections. It appears that it was inhabited mere centuries before [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] took to space. At first sight, it appears to have been a weapons station, as evidenced by the exceptionally large cannon that takes up the majority of its volume. However, most of the remaining sections seem to have been dedicated to research facilities, indicating that the weapon was likely highly experimental.

ancrel.12005.desc.zh:
[Root.Leader.GetName]不禁注意到，即便考虑到空间站的年龄，其明显未损坏的系统绝大部分似乎以过高的频率出现故障。

在无数次重新激活它们后，团队的计算技术人员发出痛苦的尖叫：“这是啥？为啥？咋整？！”一时间，痛苦和怀疑的声音有增无减，[Root.Leader.GetSheHe]摇了摇[Root.Leader.GetHerHis]的头，宣布失败。“似乎整个设施都是用导管胶带糊在一起的，”[Root.Leader.GetSheHe]说。“我很震惊这玩意儿曾经能用。”
ancrel.12005.desc.en:
[Root.Leader.GetName] can't help but notice that an abnormally large number of apparently undamaged systems in the station seem to be failing with excessive frequency, even allowing for their age.

Upon reactivating them for the umpteenth time, agonized screams are heard from the team's comp tech: "What? Why? How?!" The stream of distressed and incredulous noises continues unabated for some time before [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] shakes [Root.Leader.GetHerHis] head, defeated. "It seems this entire facility was cobbled together with duct tape," [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] says. "I'm surprised it ever worked."

ancrel.12005.desc.gestalt.zh:
我们注意到，这个空间站上大量看似完好的系统似乎都在发生灾难性故障，其频率远超预期——即便考虑到它们的年代也是如此。

在几次艰难的系统重启尝试后，我们的一名维修工[root.GetIndividualNamePlural]发生了严重崩溃："超出理性参数范围，"它开始不停重复这句话。这种状态持续了一段时间，最终[root.GetIndividualName]被迫完全放弃了尝试，让我们不得不得出结论：这个设施的程序设计根本不具备可用性。我们甚至无法理解这个设施曾经是如何正常运转的。
ancrel.12005.desc.gestalt.en:
We note that a large number of apparently undamaged systems aboard this station seem to be suffering catastrophic failures, far more frequently than expected - even allowing for their age.

Following several arduous attempts to reactivate these systems, one of our repair [root.GetIndividualNamePlural] suffered a critical meltdown: "Context exceeds parameters of reason," it began bleating. This continued for some time before the [root.GetIndividualName] was forced to abandoned the attempt altogether, resigning us to a conclusion that the facility programming is not fit for purpose. We cannot fathom how this facility ever functioned properly.

ancrel.12010.desc.zh: 尽管过程经常中断，[Root.Leader.GetName]已在破译该空间站的用途方面取得重大进展。日志表明，它的创造者“鲁达里”一直在与一个被称为“波格-莫里”灭杀种族进行长期斗争——一场他们即将输掉的战争。为了在绝望的最后一搏中扭转局势，一群激进的鲁达里政治家得出结论，保证他们生存的唯一方法是彻底消灭敌人。由于无法通过常规手段击败波格-莫里舰队，他们资助了一个绝密项目，旨在制造一种能够利用恒星的力量在跨恒星系空间发射的激光武器。然而，虽然他们可以在这个问题上投入大量资源，但该项目成立地较为仓促，并且不断有危险发生——无论是被敌人还是被他们自己政府内不愿屈服于此类措施的派系。
ancrel.12010.desc.en: Despite the frequent outages, [Root.Leader.GetName] has been able to make significant progress in deciphering the purpose of the station. Logs indicate that its creators, the "Rudari," had been engaged in a long struggle with a genocidal race known as the "Pogg-Mory" - a war they were losing. In a desperate last-ditch effort to turn the tide, a radical group of Rudari politicians concluded that the only way to guarantee their survival was through the total annihilation of the enemy. Unable to defeat the Pogg-Mory fleet by conventional means, they funded a top secret project to build a laser weapon capable of firing across interstellar space by harnessing the power of a star. However, it appears that while they could throw considerable resources at the problem, the project was hastily set up and in constant danger of discovery - either by the enemy or by factions within their own government unwilling to stoop to such measures.

ancrel.12015.desc.zh:
[Root.Leader.GetName]发现了鲁达里首席科学官的个人日志，这些日志看起来是一连串对该项目看起来不可能的要求以及迅速下降的质量和安全标准的抱怨。“没有时间测试任何东西，”最后一篇文章中写道。“这是我族人的最后一搏，敌人已经察觉到了我们。我们必须希望到此为止了。他们来了。”

日志表明由于该武器在那不久之后进行测试，所有记录都将停止于此。有证据表明，超级武器仅仅是成功摧毁了空间站。鲁达里似乎将其位置的秘密带到了他们的坟墓中——阻止我们找到他们的遗族。

空间站程序和总体状况都不足以让我们冒险尝试重新启动它并完成这个项目。然而，“死亡激光”中使用的一些创新概念为我们自己的武器专家提供了宝贵的见解。
ancrel.12015.desc.en:
[Root.Leader.GetName] has uncovered the Rudari Chief Science Officer's personal logs, which read as a litany of complaints about the seemingly impossible demands of the project and their rapidly falling quality and safety standards. "There is no time to test anything," reads one of the last entries. "This is the last gambit of my people, and the enemy has our scent. We must hope that this is enough. They are coming."

The logs indicate that the weapon was due to be tested soon after, at which point all records cease. Evidence suggests that the superweapon succeeded only in destroying the station. The Rudari seemingly took the secret of its location to their graves - allowing us to find its remains undisturbed.

Neither the programming nor the general condition of the station are good enough for us to risk trying to reactivate it and complete the project. However, some of the innovative concepts used in the "Death Laser" have provided our own weapons specialists with valuable insights.

ancrel.12020.desc.zh:
我们发现了明显的迹象，迹象表明[From.Planet.GetName]曾经人口稠密。然而，尽管不知道是什么摧毁了他们文明，摧毁都做得非常彻底：几乎没有发现有用的遗骸。

我们的扫描仪在地表深处探测到几个可能曾经支持生命的大洞。也许我们会在那里有更多的运气。
ancrel.12020.desc.en:
We have discovered clear signs that [From.Planet.GetName] was once densely populated. However, whatever destroyed their civilization did a very thorough job of it: very few useful remains have been found.

Our scanners have detected several large cavities deep below the surface that may once have supported life. Perhaps we will have more luck there.

ancrel.12025.desc.zh: 我们对[From.Planet.GetName]上的洞穴系统的挖掘发现了保存完好、规模宏大的地下高科技社会遗迹。许多废墟的状况出奇的好，我们设法找到了[Owner.GetResearchers]所描述的加密数据水晶“图书馆”。希望这些可以对这里发生的事情有所了解。
ancrel.12025.desc.en: Our excavation of the cave systems on [From.Planet.GetName] has found well-preserved remnants of an underground, high technology society built on a vast scale. Many of the ruins are in surprisingly good condition, and we have managed to find what our [Owner.GetResearchers] are describing as a "library" of encrypted data crystals. Hopefully, these can shed some light on what happened here.

ancrel.12030.desc.lithoid.zh: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不怀疑这些遗骸是我们失踪的[Owner.GetTeamMember]的遗骸，但他们对究竟是什么杀死了他们感到困惑——这个过程似乎相当地迅速。他们敦促我们在接下来的调查中保持谨慎。
ancrel.12030.desc.lithoid.en: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$ Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to what exactly killed them - the process seems to have been fairly instantaneous. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.

ancrel.12030.desc.machine.zh: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不怀疑这些遗骸是我们失踪的[Owner.GetTeamMember]的遗骸，但他们对他们的单元如何如此迅速地腐蚀感到困惑。他们敦促我们在接下来的调查中保持谨慎。
ancrel.12030.desc.machine.en: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$ Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to how their unit corroded away quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.

ancrel.12030.desc.normal.zh: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不怀疑这些遗骸是我们失踪的[Owner.GetTeamMember]的遗骸，但他们对尸体如何如此迅速地分解感到困惑。他们敦促我们在接下来的调查中保持谨慎。
ancrel.12030.desc.normal.en: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$ Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled about how the body decayed quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.

ancrel.12035.desc.zh:
我们解析来自[From.Planet.GetName]洞穴中的数据水晶时，拼凑出了一个陷入困境的星球的景象。

这个星球曾经是一个繁荣的文明的中心，被称为伊兰尼基金会。在那个文明的后期，伊兰尼人越来越倾向于囤积知识，而不关心物质问题，比如生育。结果，他们的人口迅速减少。他们的领袖对他们不断减少的人数感到震惊，他们试图找到永生的技术解决方案。在这一点上，记录变得越来越稀少——尽管它似乎早于迫使他们进入地下的某种灾难——目前尚不清楚他们的努力有什么结果。
ancrel.12035.desc.en:
As we interpret the data crystals from the caves on [From.Planet.GetName], we begin piecing together a picture of a troubled planet.

The planet was once the center of a prosperous civilization known as the Ilanii Foundation. During that civilization's latter years, the Ilanii turned more and more to the hoarding of knowledge instead of more material matters such as procreation. As a result, their population fell rapidly. Alarmed by their dwindling numbers, their leaders attempted to find a technological solution for immortality. Records become scarcer around this point - though it appears to predate whatever cataclysm forced them underground - and it is not clear yet what results their efforts yielded.

ancrel.12040.A.zh: 这种有机微生物将成为一种很好的武器。
ancrel.12040.A.en: This microorganism will make a fine weapon.

ancrel.12040.B.zh: 隔离这个星球，只允许谨慎的研究。
ancrel.12040.B.en: Quarantine the planet, allowing only careful study.

ancrel.12040.c.evopred.zh: 什么都吃的微生物？你们的远房亲戚来咯。
ancrel.12040.c.evopred.en: All-Devouring Microorganism? Meet a your macro match.

ancrel.12040.desc.curators.zh: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ 从此以后，他们将生活在小飞地中，并致力于保存他们文明中失落的知识，最终演变成现代[curator_enclave_country.GetName] 的祖先之一。
ancrel.12040.desc.curators.en: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization, eventually morphing into one of the ancestors of the modern [curator_enclave_country.GetName].

ancrel.12040.desc.meet_curators.zh: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$从今以后，他们将生活在小飞地中，致力于保护他们文明中失落的知识。我们不知道他们的最终命运，但其中一块数据水晶表明他们正前往[curator_poi.GetName] 恒星系。
ancrel.12040.desc.meet_curators.en: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization. Their ultimate fate is unknown to us, but one of the data crystals indicates they were headed for the [curator_poi.GetName] system.

ancrel.12040.desc.no_curators.zh: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ 他们的最终命运遗失在历史的长河中，但似乎他们曾打算将他们毕生奉献于保存他们文明失落的知识中。
ancrel.12040.desc.no_curators.en: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ Their ultimate fate is lost to time, but it seems they intended to dedicate the remainder of their existence to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization.

ancrel.12060.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]恒星系笼罩着诡异的光芒。[Root.GetName]突然出现在星系的某个区域，我们确信这里此前数代人甚至数千年间从未被星系文明造访过。

但等一下，我们的传感器发现了一个能量信号！该信号主要集中在星系中的第一颗行星上，这颗行星似乎不太可能支持生命，毕竟它距离中子星如此接近。但好像还有其他信号正在移动。它们直奔[Root.GetName]而去，武器随时准备开火！
ancrel.12060.desc.en:
An eerie glow lies over the [From.GetName] system. The [Root.GetName] has emerged in a sector of the galaxy surely not visited by any galactic civilization for generations - for millennia... if ever.

But wait - our sensors are reporting energy signatures! Most are concentrated on the first planet of the system, an unlikely candidate for life, considering its proximity to a neutron star. But there are others, mobile ones. They are careening towards the [Root.GetName], weapons charged!

ancrel.12065.desc.zh: 我们已经击败了[fromfrom.System.GetName]的防御者。这个恒星系里的景象真是光怪陆离：固态物质几乎不存在，即便是小行星带都残破不堪，就像是被人彻底地开采枯竭了一般。一系列巨型装置按照特定的间距环绕着行星，而信号显示的那一颗孤零零的行星也许是人为制造的。其中释放出了强大的能量信号。如果有什么线索的话一定能在那里找到。
ancrel.12065.desc.en: We have defeated the defenders of [fromfrom.System.GetName]. The system is a curious sight: there is very little solid matter remaining in it - even its asteroid belts have a bedraggled look, as if they have been extensively mined. A series of large installations placed at regular intervals around the star, and there is a single planet that our readings suggest may be artificial in origin. Intense energy signals have been detected emanating from it. If answers are to be found, they will be there.

ancrel.12070.desc.zh:
目前为止，我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]所能推断的是，这个被他们乌鸦嘴般称为“观测终端”的行星上从未有过生命的存在。但其上并不缺活动迹象。地表上有稠密的建筑物，大量人造建筑鳞次栉比地排列在荒芜的基岩上，这些规整的阵列几乎覆盖了行星四分之三的地表。数以亿计的无人机正在对其进行维护，执行的任务从简单的清扫到运行高度复杂的装配线皆包含在内。

然而它们的真正作用目前尚不明确。我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]准备派遣一支队伍下到地表以进行进一步调查。
ancrel.12070.desc.en:
As far as our [Owner.GetResearchers] can tell, there has never been life on the planet they have ominously dubbed the "Observation Terminal". But there is no shortage of activity. The surface is densely built up, massive artificial structures placed upon the bare bedrock in neat, orderly rows that cover almost three quarters of the planet. Billions of mechanical drones maintain them, performing tasks ranging from menial clean-up to running highly-complex assembly lines.

Their exact purpose remains, however, unclear. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are preparing to send a team to the surface to investigate further.

ancrel.12075.desc.zh:
这些机器人对我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]毫不关心，即使从它们的身边路过也继续执行着各自的命令。与这些无人机的一切沟通尝试都失败了，即便是尝试打断他们的工作也毫无收获，这些无人机毫不躲闪直接强行冲撞挡路的[Owner.GetResearchers]，造成了严重的损伤。

打那以后，我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]转而将目光放在操控这些无人机的程序上。通过分析拦截到的信号，我们推断其中有一个主宰一切的系统在操控这些无人机。然而，对其进行解码非常困难，可能很难再有进一步的发现了。
ancrel.12075.desc.en:
As our [Owner.GetResearchers] pass amongst them, the drones on the planet ignore their presence and continue going about their tasks. All efforts to communicate with the drones have failed, and even attempts to disrupt them produced no reactions - the drones simply rode roughshod over the interfering [Owner.GetResearchers], causing serious injury.

Since then, our [Owner.GetResearchers] have shifted their focus to the programs steering the drones. Analysis of intercepted signals suggests there is an overarching system steering them. However, the encryption it uses is extremely sophisticated, and it has proven hard to find out more.

ancrel.12080.desc.zh: 尽管我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]已经难以进一步深入调查这颗行星，但还有一支队伍还在继续研究散布在整个恒星系中的物体阵列。总共约有超过一万个这样的物体，它们大部分是长圆柱体外形的装置，似乎仍在运行，持续不断地向行星发送信号。鉴于它们的形状以及它们似乎无一例外地指向我们星系中的各个点的事实，我们无可避免地得出这是一个出奇巨大的传感器阵列的结论。但它会是由谁建造的呢？
ancrel.12080.desc.en: While our [Owner.GetResearchers] have been unable to make further progress investigating the planet, a team has been investigating the array of objects spread across the system. There are over ten thousand of them, all told. Most of them are long and cylindrical devices that still seem to be operating - they are transmitting a signal towards the planet. Given their shape and the fact that they seem to be without exception pointed towards various points in our galaxy, we cannot escape the conclusion that this is an absurdly huge sensor array. But who could have built it?

ancrel.12085.desc.zh: 在一次大胆的行动中，我们的[Owner.GetResearchers]趁着附近没有其他无人机存在时，成功地向一处无人机主机的接入终端植入了窃听装置。该入侵目前还没有被发现，我们对其的印象是这是一个高度复杂的系统，甚至可能远超我们的网络，但完全没有考虑到自卫的需求。毫无疑问他们认为这些防御舰队的武力吓止就已经非常充分了。尽管如此，我们入侵的这个系统庞大得难以置信，甚至庞大这个词用来描述这个涵盖整颗行星的系统来说都有些苍白无力，所以我们需要一些时间来获取更多信息。
ancrel.12085.desc.en: In a daring move, our [Owner.GetResearchers] managed to implant spyware into an access terminal to the drones' mainframe in a moment while no drones were nearby. The intrusion does not appear to have been detected yet. Our impression is of a highly sophisticated system - beyond even our own networks, probably - but one which did not anticipate the need to protect itself. No doubt the physical deterrence of the defense fleet was deemed sufficient. Nevertheless, the systems we are infiltrating are vast - a term which seems a gross understatement for this planetary system - so it will take some time to find out more.

ancrel.12090.A.zh: 我们可以将这一整颗星球整合进我们自己的操作系统。
ancrel.12090.A.en: We can integrate the world into our own operating system.

ancrel.12090.B.zh: 让它们继续，我们可以提取他们的数据。
ancrel.12090.B.en: Let them continue - we can siphon off their readings.

ancrel.12090.C.zh: 将这些无人机分发到我们的各个殖民地。
ancrel.12090.C.en: Distribute the drones to our colonies.

ancrel.12090.C.machine.tooltip.zh: 8K£pop£ 机器人口将被分配到我们的各个殖民地上。
ancrel.12090.C.machine.tooltip.en: 8K £pop£ Machine Pops are distributed to our colonies.

ancrel.12090.C.mechanical.tooltip.zh: 8K£pop£ 机械人口将被分配到我们的各个殖民地上。
ancrel.12090.C.mechanical.tooltip.en: 8K £pop£ Mechanical Pops are distributed to our colonies.

ancrel.12090.D.zh: 但这可是一个巨大的合金库啊！
ancrel.12090.D.en: But this is just an enormous alloy mine!

ancrel.12090.E.zh: 这个运作良好的网络可以为我们所用。
ancrel.12090.E.en: A well-organized network such as this could serve us well.

ancrel.12090.E.tooltip.zh: [From.Planet.System.GetName]星系将由一个机械智能国家管辖，该国家会成为我们的附庸国。他们的首都，[From.Planet.GetName]，将成为一颗带有8K£pop£机器人口的机械星球。
ancrel.12090.E.tooltip.en: The [From.Planet.System.GetName] system will be placed under the control of a Machine Intelligence that will be our subject. Their capital, [From.Planet.GetName], will be a Machine World with 8K £pop£ Machine Pops.

ancrel.12090.desc.zh:
位于$NAME_Ultima_Vigilis$的自动化系统似乎比我们所能想象的还要古老。我们黑入这个系统取得了数据，可是其中并没有能够帮助我们确认其建造者身份或最终意图的信息。关于系统的建造者，我们唯一可以确定的事情就是他们至少在12亿年前就已经来到了这里，在建造完系统并将其设定为监测整个星系的观测站后就离开了。

值得一提的是，经历如此漫长的岁月后，这个系统仍在运作。遍布整个系统的装置阵列实际上是高度精密的传感器，它们会向该星球发送实时数据，而在星球上的中央处理系统则会将这些数据转化为无人机可以保存并长期存储的数据。由于受到存储空间与物资短缺的影响，他们似乎下决心改进了数据压缩技术。这个星球上的巨型结构自称其存储了自建造以来的所有观测数据，不过我们却无法证实这一点，毕竟这些数据被过度压缩，已经超出我们的解压能力了。

令人不安的是，尽管发送频率下降，但其依旧在向外界广播“重点”数据流。不过都过了这么久了，应该也没人在监听了吧？不管怎样，我们已经准备好程序接管这些无人机，只要有胆量，我们马上就可以根据我们自己的设想改造这个系统。
ancrel.12090.desc.en:
It seems the automated systems in $NAME_Ultima_Vigilis$ are older than we can imagine. The data systems we have hacked do not give us any clues as to the identity or ultimate intentions of its creators, but the one thing we have managed to ascertain is that they arrived no less than 1.2 billion years ago, and departed soon after setting up the system as an observation post to surveil our entire galaxy.

Remarkably, the system is still operating even after all these years: the array of installations spread across the system are, it turns out, highly sophisticated sensors. They send a live feed to the planet, where the central operating system processes it into information the drones can save and store. Spurred on by shortages of space and matter, it appears that they have improved their data compression techniques with determination: the massive structures on the planet purport to contain the sum of all observations ever recorded. However, we cannot test this assertion, since the data is compressed well beyond our ability to decompress it.

Disturbingly, a reduced stream of "highlights" is still being broadcast into empty space. But surely no one is still listening, after all this time? Regardless, our programs are poised to take control of the drones. We may now shape the system to our imagination - if we dare.

ancrel.12095.desc.zh:
“你们一点也不顾念——”

传输数据流乱码了一段时间，无法输出有效信息。

“你们难道没有想过有人正在接受那个你漫不经心就切断掉的数据流？行吧，既然你们已经证明自己是一群危险而具有攻击性的害虫……那么是时候叫害虫防治过来了。准备好迎接末日吧。”
ancrel.12095.desc.en:
"You inconsiderate-"

The transmission feed is garbled for a time, and no sense can be made of the noises heard.

"Did you never consider that someone might be watching that signal feed you so carelessly cut off? Well, since you have proven yourselves to be dangerously aggressive vermin... it's time to call the PEST CONTROL. Prepare to face your doom."

ancrel.12095.tooltip.zh: 不久后可能会发生某些糟糕的事情……

ancrel.13.a.zh: 这些灰尘……竟然是……泽珞族！

ancrel.13.desc.zh:
水晶告诉我们，曾经有一个疯狂的泽珞族研究员，致力于研究一种链式反应理论，将灵能使用在身体内部并在受控的灵能链式反应中燃烧掉自己的身体，这种理论是如此的离经叛道，其同侪一致拒绝予以接受。根据他最后的遗言，他崇高牺牲后残存的灰烬经过检测被确认为一种难以置信的强大灵能源，其富含的能量等同于他一生的灵能潜势总和，而且可以直接为另一位灵能者所用。

这个水晶最后也指给了我们泽珞族母星的位置！
ancrel.13.desc.en:
The crystal tells us how a rogue Zroni researcher - working on a theory which his peers refused to believe - turned his power inwards, consuming his own body in a contained Psionic chain-reaction. Following his last instructions, the dusty residue of his supreme sacrifice was tested and confirmed to be an incredibly potent source of Psionic energy. It was essentially the sum total Psionic potential of his life, rendered instantly usable by another Psion.

The crystal finally pointed us towards the location of the Zroni homeworld!

ancrel.13000.desc.zh: 在勾陈一的最后一个侵略者倒下后，我们的舰船在返回港口之前完成了对恒星系的最后一次扫描，并发现了一些奇怪的东西。在勾陈一 II 的星球上，我们的传感器显示有重金属被排列成了人造结构。有趣的是，这些构造中中似乎只有一个漂浮在行星海洋上，而其余的则在海面以下。我们怀疑这是外星生命的杰作。
ancrel.13000.desc.en: After the last of the aggressors in Polaris fell, our ships completed a final scan of the system before heading back to port and discovered something curious. On the world of Polaris II, heavy metals are arranged in artificial structures on our sensors. Interestingly only one of these formations appears to be floating on the planetary ocean while the rest are below the surface. We suspect this is the work of alien life.

ancrel.13005.desc.zh:
漂浮的冰山本身内置了一个巨大的黑色长方体，由与上方太空舰队残骸相同的合金制成。我们的冰川专家表示，尽管据称“很难用外星大气来判断”，冰山形成依然可以追溯到至少一千年前。结构内部的扫描显示有相当多的生物读数，因此不建议使用破坏性工具。

团队将不得不穿越冰冻的悬崖，到达似乎是建筑物入口的地方。
ancrel.13005.desc.en:
Built into the floating iceberg itself is a hulking black cuboid made out of the same alloys as the wreckage of the space fleet above. Our glacial specialists state that analysis of the iceberg dates its formation to least a thousand years ago, though it's supposedly "hard to tell with alien atmospheres". Scans of the interior of the structure show quite a few biological readings, therefore using disruptive tools is inadvisable.

The team will have to traverse the frozen cliffs to what appears to be an entrance into the building.

ancrel.13010.desc.zh: 我们在[From.Planet.GetName]的设施入口处建立了大本营。我们已经发现了一些看起来像是刻在建筑物墙壁上的文字。现在我们将开始在不会损坏里面任何东西的情况下打开这扇门的漫长而艰巨的过程。与此同时，我们的异种语言学家尝试翻译铭文中已失传的外星语言。
ancrel.13010.desc.en: We have set up base camp at the supposed entrance to the facility here on [From.Planet.GetName]. Already we have discovered something that looks like writing inscribed on the walls of the building. Now we will begin the long and arduous process of opening this door without damaging whatever is inside. At the same time, our xeno-linguists attempt to translate the dead alien language of the inscriptions.

ancrel.13015.desc.zh: 是时候了，我们已经准备好解封黑色结构，根据墙上铭文的初步翻译，它被称为“避难所”。这个避难所的创造者勾陈一星人将其作为保护财宝安全的最后手段。当我们打开门时，迎接我们的是——根据我们的传感器的数据——一种类似于外界空气的受控大气，只是二氧化碳要少得多。
ancrel.13015.desc.en: The time was upon us, and we stood ready to unseal the black structure, dubbed "The Vault" according to preliminary translations of the wall inscriptions. The creators of this vault, the Polarians, made it as a last resort to keep their treasures safe. As we opened the doors, we were greeted by - according to our sensors - a controlled atmosphere similar to the air outside, just with quite a bit less carbon dioxide.

ancrel.13020.a.zh: 把这些样本发送给我们的科学家。
ancrel.13020.a.en: Send these samples to our scientists.

ancrel.13020.b.evopred.zh: 不仅编目了而且还便于克隆？这个地库简直是为我们建的。
ancrel.13020.b.evopred.en: Cataloged and ready for cloning? This vault was made for us.

ancrel.13020.desc.zh:
远古种子！植物胚胎——那是勾陈一星人藏在这个金库里的宝藏。进一步的翻译告诉我们，这些外星人怪异地不断用过量二氧化碳填充他们的大气层。一旦气候发生不可逆转的变化，这个星球的古代居民就会收集他们所能找到的所有不能在新环境下生存的植物物质，并将它们全部冻结在这里。

那时，整个星球都会被冰覆盖；现在，只剩下这片孤独的小冰山了。然而，他们的努力不会白费——拿到星球上的整个植物生态的编目和分类，将极大地帮助我们的科学家研究未来的生物问题。
ancrel.13020.desc.en:
Ancient seeds! Plant embryos - that was the treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the plant matter they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole plant ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our scientists in researching future biological matters.

ancrel.13025.desc.zh:
有机微生物！所有有害和有益的细菌。所有真核生物和原核生物。所有这些都在高级存储设施中标记和分类：这是勾陈一星人藏在这个金库中的巨大财富。进一步的翻译告诉我们，这些外星人怪异地不断用过量二氧化碳填充他们的大气层。一旦大气发生了不可逆转的变化，这个星球的古代居民就会收集他们所能找到的所有不能在新环境下生存的微生物，并将它们全部冻结在这里。

那时，整个星球都会被冰覆盖；现在，只剩下这片孤独的小冰山了。然而，他们的努力不会白费——拿到星球的整个微生物生态的编目和分类，将极大地帮助我们的[Root.Owner.getscientistplural]开发新星球以及改造殖民地。
ancrel.13025.desc.en:
Microorganisms! Every harmful and helpful bacterium. Every eukaryote and prokaryote. All in an advanced storage facility labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole microbial ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our [Root.Owner.getscientistplural] develop new and improved colonies for new worlds.

ancrel.13025.desc.machine.zh:
有机微生物。所有有害和有益的细菌，所有真核生物和原核生物。标记和编目：这是勾陈一星人藏在这个金库中的宝藏。进一步的翻译告诉我们，这些外星人怪异地不断用过量二氧化碳填充他们的大气层。一旦大气发生了不可逆转的变化，这个星球的古代居民就会收集他们所能找到的所有不能在新环境下生存的微生物，并将它们全部冻结在这里。

那时，整个星球都会被冰覆盖；现在，剩下的就是这座孤独的小冰山。然而，感谢他们的努力——预先分类的生物将使提取相关信息变得更加容易。
ancrel.13025.desc.machine.en:
Microorganisms. Every harmful and helpful bacterium, every eukaryote and prokaryote. Labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small, lonely iceberg. However, their efforts are appreciated- pre-sorted biologicals will make it easier to extract relevant information.

ancrel.13030.desc.zh: 大前天晚上，首席考古学家[From.Leader.GetName]报告说看到了令人不安的景象，并且一直被关在自己的房间里直到现在。他们认为是我们这里的某种东西引发的……
ancrel.13030.desc.en: Three nights ago, chief archaeologist [From.Leader.GetName] reported having a disturbing vision and has been shut away in their quarters until now. They believed the source to be whatever is down here with us...

ancrel.13100.desc.zh:
在[From.Planet.GetName]上发现了充满蘑菇的巨大峡谷，这就是答案的开始。原来水在这些蘑菇里面。它们似乎扩张到了星球表面的很大一部分，并且都与同一个菌丝体相连，因此从技术上讲，它算是一个单一的有机体，也是我们见过的最大的有机体之一。该团队的一些成员将这种巨大的真菌称为“巨大蘑菇”。

看起来蘑菇已经过基因改造，并完全接管了曾经存在于这里的生态系统。它们肆无忌惮地加速生长，以至于它们吸收了这里存在的大部分水。随后，它们进入了一种干枯的休眠状态，在这种状态下，大部分真菌仍然活着，水遍布整个生物体。
ancrel.13100.desc.en:
The discovery on [From.Planet.GetName] of vast canyons filled with mushrooms provided us with the beginning of an answer. The water is inside the mushrooms. They seem to span a large part of the surface of the world, all connected to the same mycelium, which technically makes it a single organism, and one of the biggest we've ever seen. Some of the members of the team dubbed this humongous fungus the 'Fumongus'.

It looks like the mushrooms have been genetically altered and have completely taken over the ecosystem that once existed here. Their unbridled and accelerated growth was such that they absorbed most of the water that was present here. They subsequently entered a sort of dried-up dormant state in which most of the fungus is still alive, with water spread out across the whole organism.

ancrel.13105.desc.zh:
在坐落在[From.Planet.GetName]峡谷中的菌丝森林的深处，我们发现了某种地堡，早已被蘑菇摧垮。该团队认为，它是由对这里的蘑菇进行基因改造的那个物种建造的。

地堡的大部分已经倒塌，其中的许多设备可能已经损坏无法修复，但我们已经确定了一些可能装有可利用材料的密封房间。值得注意的是，这里没有发现外星人遗骸。也许他们放弃了这个地方，也或者全部被当地野生动物所吸收了。
ancrel.13105.desc.en:
Deep in the heart of the mycelial forests nestled in the canyons of [From.Planet.GetName] we discovered some sort of bunker, long overrun by mushrooms. The team believes that it was built by the same species that genetically altered the mushrooms here. 

Large sections of the bunker have collapsed and a lot of the equipment within it is likely broken beyond repair, but we have identified some sealed rooms that might hold exploitable material. Notably, no alien remains have been found here. Maybe they abandoned the place, or else didn't leave behind any body parts that weren't absorbed by the local wildlife.

ancrel.13110.desc.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上的地堡用于保护计算设备，其中一些似乎直接连接到菌丝体。值得庆幸的是，我们设法重新激活了几个终端和数据库。

破解加密和解密所使用的语言需要时间，团队已要求派我们的几位顶级[Root.Owner.GetLinguists]来帮忙。
ancrel.13110.desc.en:
The bunker on [From.Planet.GetName] was used to protect computing equipment, some of which appears to be directly connected to the mycelium. Thankfully, we managed to reactivate several terminals and databanks.

Breaking the encryption and deciphering the language used will take time, and the team has requested that several of our top [Root.Owner.GetLinguists] be sent here to help.

ancrel.13115.desc.zh:
我们从[From.Planet.GetName]地堡中的数据库中找到了有价值的信息。数据库告诉我们，这是一种监听哨站。显然，外星人找到了一种方法来解释通过菌丝体传播的信号并将它们转化为可操作的情报。

我们不明白这怎么实现的，但该团队现在将尝试从附近的冰小行星带运水过来再次“唤醒”巨大蘑菇，看看如果它有传输数据的话，传输的是什么样的数据。
ancrel.13115.desc.en:
We have recovered valuable information from the databanks found in the bunker on [From.Planet.GetName]. The databanks tell us that this was a sort of listening post. Apparently, the aliens found a way to interpret the signals coursing through the mycelium and convert them into actionable intel.

We do not understand how this might have been possible, but the team will now try to bring water from nearby ice asteroids to 'awaken' the Fumongus again and see what kind data it transmits, if any.

ancrel.13120.desc.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上的蘑菇又开始繁茂了。在其他几艘飞船的帮助下，我们不得不将几颗冰小行星拖入轨道，然后将其中的大块降落到行星上的各个地方进行融化。这是一个漫长的过程，但它终于开始有结果了。

有了这个，计算机开始吐出看起来非常随机的小块数据，直到我们从母星上分辨出信号。与[Root.Owner.Capital.GetName]的团队进行了一系列合作实验，唯一可能的结论是蘑菇对其他星球上发生的事情的有有限的了解。虽然我们检索到的数据尚不可利用，但预计继续尝试恢复蘑菇会给我们带来更多结果。
ancrel.13120.desc.en:
The mushrooms on [From.Planet.GetName] are starting to flourish again. With the help of several other ships, we had to tow several icy asteroids into orbit before bringing down chunks of them to various places on the planet to melt. It has been long process, but it is finally beginning to bear fruit.

With this, the computers began to spit out small bits of data that seemed pretty random until we recognized activity from our home. In cooperation with teams on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName], a series of experiments has been conducted and the only possible conclusion is that the mushroom has some limited awareness of what happens on other planets. While the data we have retrieved is not exploitable just yet, continued efforts to restore the mushrooms are expected to give us more results.

ancrel.13130.a.zh: 偏执的傻瓜。我们该使用它。

ancrel.13130.desc.zh:
$ancrel.13135.intro$

然而，关于菌丝网络，我们仍然知之甚少。$ancrel.13135.mid$ 但是还有谁可以访问这个网络呢？有很多数据我们无法与这个星系中的恒星系相关联。我们更悲观的 [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] 认为我们可能不是唯一在倾听的人，通过重新激活网络，我们只是向使用它的所有人展示了我们自己。

鉴于我们仍然不了解巨大蘑菇，以及之前接触过它的物种，最好不要管它。
ancrel.13130.desc.en:
$ancrel.13135.intro$

And yet, there is still so much we don't know about the mycelial network.  $ancrel.13135.mid$ But who else may have access to this network? There is a lot of data that we were not able to correlate to systems in this galaxy. Our more pessimistic [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] argue we might not be the only ones listening, and that by reactivating the network we just revealed ourselves to anyone using it.

Given all we still don't know about the Fumongus, or about the previous species that tapped into it, it might be best to just leave it alone..

ancrel.13135.a.evopred.zh: 能监听还能汇报。也许我们也可以学学类似的事情。
ancrel.13135.a.evopred.en: Monitor and report. Perhaps we can learn something similar.

ancrel.13135.desc.zh:
$ancrel.13135.intro$

仍然存在一些谜团，毕竟我们仍然不确定蘑菇是如何设法从星系其他地方收集这么多数据的。$ancrel.13135.mid$

随着网络再次运行，剩下的唯一决议就是是否将其用于监视。
ancrel.13135.desc.en:
$ancrel.13135.intro$

Some mysteries remain, as we are still not sure how the mushroom manages to collect that much data from the rest of the galaxy. $ancrel.13135.mid$

With the network working again, the only decision left to make is whether to use it for surveillance, or not.

ancrel.14001.desc.zh: 当我们打开这艘外星人星舰的气阀门时，等待在另一边的是一片修罗地狱。我们初步调查发现，这里简直就是一片残杀现场。在检查支离破碎的船员尸体之后，我们很确定他们生前正互相撕扯对方的四肢。我们可以转身就走……但那样我们就永远没法发现这场悲剧是怎么发生的了。
ancrel.14001.desc.en: When we opened the airlock of the alien starship, putrefaction and decay awaited us on the other side. Our preliminary investigation has uncovered a scene of carnage. After examining the mutilated bodies of the crew, we are certain they tore each other limb from limb. We could just leave... but then we'd never know why this tragedy happened.

ancrel.14002.desc.zh: 随着进一步的发掘，我们找到了这艘船的科学实验室。微弱的能量布满这片区域，泛出轻柔的紫外光。一片凌乱的紫色灌木正在厚重的孢子云。看来，这艘船的医生利用实验室和通风闸将一片有毒的云雾排放到了飞船的每一个角落。
ancrel.14002.desc.en: Digging deeper, we have uncovered the ship's science lab. Minimal power saturates the scene in ultraviolent illumination. A riot of purple shrubbery is releasing thick clouds of spores. The ship's doctor used a laboratory and ventilation shafts to flood the ship with an intoxicating mist.

ancrel.14003.b.zh: 运行诊断程序，并开始修复。

ancrel.14003.desc.zh: 我们认为自己能免疫这片有毒云雾带来的危害。如果我们能让飞船的引擎运作起来，我们就能启动这艘船并将其送回母星研究。这需要时间，但这座精密的药学实验室能为我们帝国的士兵们提供有用的生物增强剂。
ancrel.14003.desc.en: We think we are immune to the full effects of the intoxicating mist. If we can get the ship's engines online, we can launch the ship and send it back home for study. This will take time, but the elaborate pharmaceutical laboratory may provide useful biochemical augmentation for our empire's soldiers.

ancrel.14004.a.zh: 抓住已经陷入“极乐”的工程师。

ancrel.14004.desc.zh: 我们愚蠢地以为我们能够免疫这片云雾，但是我们的工程师们已经陷入了销魂极乐的状态。他们在飞船的过道跳舞，大声地唱歌。我们需要时间对空气进行净化，抓住这帮子工程师，然后才能发动飞船。这些耽搁会花费我们的时间。
ancrel.14004.desc.en: We foolishly thought we were immune to the mist, but our engineers are experiencing a state of rapturous bliss. They dance in the ship's corridors, singing atonally. We will need to clear the atmosphere and capture our engineers before we can launch the ship. This delay will cost us time.

ancrel.14005.desc.zh: 我们愚蠢地以为自己能够免疫这片云雾，但是我们的科学家们已经在经受心理狂躁的苦果。在飞船的每一个角落都有打斗发生。我们需要时间对空气进行净化，镇压住这群云雾的受害者，然后才能发动飞船。这些耽搁会花费我们的时间。
ancrel.14005.desc.en: We foolishly thought that we were immune to the mist, but our scientists are experiencing fits of psychotic rage. Fighting has broken out shipwide. We will need to clear the atmosphere and subdue the mist's victims before we can launch the ship. This delay will cost us time.

ancrel.14006.a.zh: 好好利用这个令人惊叹的科技。

ancrel.14006.a.tooltip.zh: 胜利在等着！我们的士兵应该愿意冒这个风险。
ancrel.14006.a.tooltip.en: Victory awaits! Our soldiers should be willing to take this risk.

ancrel.14006.b.tooltip.zh: 有些秘密我们还是别知道为好。
ancrel.14006.b.tooltip.en: There are some secrets we were not meant to know.

ancrel.14006.desc.zh: 我们起飞了！尽管很危险，但外星人飞船的有毒迷雾确实能够增强我们帝国士兵的战斗力和忠诚心。然而，问题还是存在：我们应该让自己的士兵去接触这种有害的物质吗？或者我们从这场悲剧的错误中学得教训，放弃这一切？
ancrel.14006.desc.en: We have liftoff! Though dangerous, the alien ship's intoxicating mist could augment the effectiveness and loyalty of our empire's soldiers. However, the question remains: should we subject our own soldiers to this hazardous substance? Or should we say no and learn from their tragic mistakes?

ancrel.14100.desc.zh:
我们实在是很难说[From.Planet.GetName]到底算不算作一个行星：初步钻探发现的是一层又一层的生物组织。据估计，总共需要2,435,463只缇扬奇尸体才能产生此等规模的行星质量（误差范围5.3%）。即使我们假设地核是一块岩石，尸体只是堆叠在上面，涉及到的样本数量依然是无比庞大的。

是某人或者某种事物将缇扬奇带到这里让它们死去，还是说它们只是顺其自然地来到这里度过最后的时光，然后死去？
ancrel.14100.desc.en:
It's hard to determine if [From.Planet.GetName] is even a planet: preliminary drilling has only revealed strata upon strata of biological tissue. According to estimations, it would take 2,435,463 Tiyanki bodies to produce a planetary mass of this size (with a margin of error equal to 5.3%). Even assuming the existence of a rocky core upon which the corpses are layered, the number of specimens involved is still significant.

Did someone or something bring the Tiyanki here to die, or are they naturally drawn to this place as their final hour draws near?

ancrel.14100.necro.desc.zh: $ancrel.14100.desc$最重要的是：为什么我们的死灵法师不能复活它们？为什么这堆死去的肉体拒绝我们，就好像已经有其他存在在控制它们一样？
ancrel.14100.necro.desc.en: $ancrel.14100.desc$ Most crucially: why are our Necromancers unable to revive them? Why does this dead flesh reject us, as if already controlled by another entity?

ancrel.14200.desc.zh:
遍布[From.Planet.GetName]地表的死亡缇扬奇的那种不寻常……的活动，似乎是它们再生能力的一种副作用：即使技术上已经判定为死亡，它们的尸体仍旧在不断地重组再生。这个恒星系拥有着非比寻常般丰富的营养物质，尤其是缇扬奇游荡的那个气态巨行星。或许这解释了为什么我们之前从未观察到这样的行为。

然而，这个发现并没有解释为什么这些死去的生物像是在被某种单一思维控制一样蠕动，不断地伸出触手，吞食新近降落到这个行星上的尸体。

我们希望进一步的挖掘能够揭示这个地方，或这个生命……的内在运作规律，带给我们新的见解。我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]还在就术语和分类问题无法达成一致。
ancrel.14200.desc.en:
The unusual... liveliness of the dead Tiyanki covering the surface of [From.Planet.GetName] seems to be a byproduct of their regenerative capabilities: even if technically dead, the bodies are still reassembling themselves. This system is unusually rich in nourishing substances typically found in the gas giants where Tiyanki graze. Perhaps that explains why this behavior hasn't been observed before.

This discovery does not explain why the dead seem to move as if controlled by a single mind, extending their tentacles to encroach upon the new carcasses falling on the planet.

Further excavations will hopefully reveal new insights on the inner workings of this... place. Or being. Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] are still divided on the exact nomenclature.

ancrel.14300.desc.zh: 我们的挖掘队发掘到了一个复杂的隧道网络，从[From.Planet.GetName]的地表一直延伸到地下深处。化学分析确认迷宫的墙体是由压实的缇扬奇组织构成，尽管其年代甚至超过了我们的帝国，但肉质还散发着温热，甚至几乎没有腐败。看上去就像是这些尸体自己聚合到了一起，重构其形态建立了这个地方……但是为什么？
ancrel.14300.desc.en: Our excavations unearthed a complex network of tunnels extending under the surface of [From.Planet.GetName]. Chemical analysis confirms the walls are entirely composed of highly compressed Tiyanki tissue, the flesh still warm and hardly decomposed despite rivaling the age of our empire. It's as if the corpses were fused together, reshaped and modified to form this place... But why?

ancrel.14400.desc.zh:
在对[From.Planet.GetName]的地下隧道网络进行测绘的时候，我们[Owner.GetScientistPlural]突然意识到，这个隧道网络同一只缇扬奇的血管系统极其相似——但是其规模达到了行星级别。

那些搏动的墙壁散发着轻微的温暖，随着探险队逐渐接近行星的核心，墙壁的温度也在慢慢提升——在核心处，我们的扫描仪捕捉到了一个微弱的生命信号。
ancrel.14400.desc.en:
After mapping the extensive underground network of [From.Planet.GetName], our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] realized the tunnels closely match the structure of the Tiyanki vascular system - but on a planetary scale.

The pulsating walls emanate a soft warmth, the temperature slowly increasing as the expedition approached the planet core - where our scanners have picked up a faint life signal.

ancrel.14400.matriarch.desc.zh:
在对[From.Planet.GetName]的地下隧道网络进行测绘的时候，我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]突然意识到，这个隧道网络同一只缇扬奇的血管系统极其相似——但是其规模跟我们之前遇到的那只在星辰间游荡的缇扬奇族母差不多。

那些搏动的墙壁散发着轻微的温暖，随着探险队逐渐接近行星的核心，墙壁的温度也在慢慢提升——在核心处，我们的扫描仪捕捉到了一个微弱的生命信号。
ancrel.14400.matriarch.desc.en:
After mapping the extensive underground network of [From.Planet.GetName], our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] realized the tunnels closely match the structure of the Tiyanki vascular system - but on a scale comparable to that of the Tiyanki Matriarch we encountered while roaming the stars.

The pulsating walls emanate a soft warmth, the temperature slowly increasing as the expedition approached the planet core - where our scanners have picked up a faint life signal.

ancrel.14510.b.zh: 在不伤害它的前提下监视其生长。
ancrel.14510.b.en: Monitor its growth without harming it.

ancrel.14510.c.zh: 让这个神圣的生命体在和平中成长吧。
ancrel.14510.c.en: Let this sacred life-form growth in peace.

ancrel.14510.d.zh: 策展人肯定愿意为这个标本付个好价钱。
ancrel.14510.d.en: The Curators will pay a good price for this specimen.

ancrel.14510.desc.zh:
在一个庞大的地下穴室中，一只缇扬奇竖立地站着，钟型的脑袋微微地摇晃着，它细线一样的触手舒展开来，连接着穴室的外墙。看上去它成为了某种控制单元，不断操纵、指引着这个行星级别墓地的生长。

我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]没法断定什么种类的生物会从如此恐怖的过程中诞生，但是当它苏醒的时候，有一件事是很明确的：它会成为远比普通的缇扬奇要大得多，也恐怖得多的存在。
ancrel.14510.desc.en:
In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell-shaped head swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread across the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appears to be some sort of command unit, controlling and directing the growth of this planet-sized graveyard.

Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] are unable to determine what kind of creature will arise from this grim process, and when it will awaken, but one thing is for sure: it will be something far, far more vast and terrible than an ordinary Tiyanki.

ancrel.14510.matriarch.desc.zh:
在一个庞大的地下穴室中，一只缇扬奇竖立地站着，钟型的脑袋微微地摇晃着，它细线一样的触手舒展开来，连接着穴室的外墙。看上去它成为了某种控制单元，不断操纵、指引着这个行星级别墓地的生长。

我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]没法断定这个过程什么时候会完成，但是相信一旦这只生物苏醒，它会成为远比普通的缇扬奇要大得多，也恐怖得多的存在：这只生物值得我们视作一只新的缇扬奇族母。
ancrel.14510.matriarch.desc.en:
In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell-shaped head swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread across the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appears to be some sort of command unit, controlling and directing the growth of this planet-sized graveyard.

Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] don't know when the process will be concluded, but believe once the creature awakens, it will be something far, far more vast and terrible than an ordinary Tiyanki: something worthy of being called a new Tiyanki Matriarch.

ancrel.14520.desc.zh: 在一个庞大的地下穴室中，一只缇扬奇竖立地站着，钟型的脑袋微微地摇晃着，它细线一样的触手舒展开来，连接着穴室的外墙。看上去它成为了某种控制单元，不断操纵、指引着这个行星级别墓地的生长。但是这个生物现在已经死了，被我们用来前往这个地方的挖掘设备毁灭了。核心周边的外壳变得苍白而易碎，整个地方经历了第二次死亡。
ancrel.14520.desc.en: In a vast underground chamber, a Tiyanki stands upright, bell swaying lightly, its wiry tentacles spread on the floor to connect with the outer walls of the chamber. It appeared to be some sort of control unit, controlling and directing the growth of the grave mound. But the creature is now dead, destroyed by the mining equipment we used to get access to this same place. The shells around the core are pallid and brittle; soon, this whole place will die a second death.

ancrel.14910.b.evopred.zh: 获取生物质的一种有趣途径。
ancrel.14910.b.evopred.en: An intriguing way to acquire biomatter.

ancrel.14910.desc.zh:
我们探险队的一名成员在探索隧道的时候突然消失了。搜寻小队花了好几天时间试图定位[Owner.GetScientist]，结果发现这人被一堵墙给包裹住，身体被触手死死地缠住。

把[Owner.GetScientist]解救出来花费了不少时间和精力。[Owner.GetScientist]并不只是被简单地缠住了：这堵墙正试图在分子层面将[Owner.GetScientist]融合，使其成为墙体表面的一部分。

现在[Owner.GetScientist]的状态稳定了下来，但此人拒绝离开我们的科研船——即使是在那里，也在用极度怀疑的状态死死地盯着墙壁，生怕还会有下一次袭击。
ancrel.14910.desc.en:
A member of our expedition team disappeared while exploring a tunnel. The retrieval squad spent days trying to locate the [Owner.GetScientist], only to find them partly encased in a wall, body tightly wrapped in tentacles.

Freeing the [Owner.GetScientist] took considerable time and effort. The [Owner.GetScientist] was not simply tied: the wall was trying to fuse with the [Owner.GetScientist] at a molecular level, turning them into a part of the surface.

The [Owner.GetScientist] is now in stable condition, but refuses to leave our science ship - and even there, they keep watching the walls with extreme suspicion as though fearing another attack.

ancrel.15.desc.zh:
泽珞星已经被灵能风暴彻底摧毁，看上去只在某些时间才能和宇宙其他空间处于同一位面。无论发生过多么可怕的灾难，泽珞族应该自我们脚下的星球起源。

就像先前发现的殖民地一样，泽珞星依旧空无一人。但是周围的空间中充斥着水晶信号，由于存在如此多的干扰信号，这里的大气又非常诡异，搜寻有用信息可能要花费一定的时间。
ancrel.15.desc.en:
Zron is wracked by storms of psionic energy, and appears to only be partially in phase with the rest of the universe. Whatever calamity befell the Zroni seems to have originated here.

Like all the previous colonies, it is devoid of Zroni but is teeming with crystalline signals. Given this much signal noise - on top of the strange atmospheric conditions - it may take some time for us to locate any useful information.

ancrel.15000.desc.zh:
由于[From.Planet.GetName]的林冠非常茂密难以穿透，从空中对穿越丛林便捷路线的搜索几乎一无所获。林冠之下生机勃勃：有无附肢的掠食者、耷拉脸的灵长类和成群的吸血昆虫。森林的土层非常肥沃，而恶臭的水洼让探索团队难以前行。不仅如此，还有某些东西，不知道是茂密的植被还是未知的电磁干扰，使仪器设备经常发生故障。

项目领队相信他们还是能够在树木间找到通路，只是进程可能会非常缓慢。
ancrel.15000.desc.en:
Given the impenetrable canopy on [From.Planet.GetName], aerial surveys have proven useless in determining a convenient route through the jungle. Below, the undergrowth teems with life: limbless predators; droop-faced primates; swarms of hematophagous insects. The forest floor is loamy, and pools of fetid water have caused the team significant delays. What's more, something - either the density of the foliage or an as yet undefined electrical interference - has prevented much of their equipment from functioning properly.

The project's lead believes they should still be able to forge a path through the trees, though progress is likely to be slow.

ancrel.15001.desc.zh:
对土壤的分析显示，[From.Planet.GetName]在过去的一百个公转周期内进行过一场令人惊奇的气候转变。和今天植被茂密的景象大不相同，这颗星球曾经荒芜又遍地岩石。项目领队相信这些巨大的植物本身就是原因：共振显像扫描发现，它们的树汁中存在灵能。这些能量从地下水中被植被巨大的根系抽出，并经由类似光合作用的过程逐渐散布到整个行星的大气中。这很可能就是团队仪器设备出故障的原因。

有趣的是，月光似乎能促进灵能扩散。在晴朗的夜晚，甚至空气看起来都在震颤，这个现象在团队接近目的地的过程中越来越强烈。这一景象我们前所未见。
ancrel.15001.desc.en:
A soil analysis reveals that [From.Planet.GetName] has undergone a startling climatological transformation within its last 100 cycles. Far from the lush jungle world that exists today, the planet was once rocky and barren. The project lead believes the great trees themselves are responsible: a resonance imaging scan detected the presence of psionic energy within their sap. Pulled from groundwater by the trees' vast root systems, this energy is eventually diffused throughout the planet's atmosphere in a process akin to photosynthesis. It is highly likely that this is the cause of the team's malfunctioning equipment.

Interestingly, the presence of moonlight appears to accelerate the psionic diffusion. On clear nights, the air itself seems to vibrate, a phenomenon that has only grown in intensity as the team nears its destination. This is unlike anything we've ever seen before.

ancrel.15002.desc.zh:
在终于抵达他们寻找的坐标后，考古团队发现了一条隐藏在林冠下蜿蜒崎岖的河谷。河水从圆环形的洞口奔流而出，显然，这条河一定发源自某个庞大的地下泉。一条数千年前在岩壁上开凿出来的摇摇欲坠的阶梯将团队带向了一个地下隧道。

洞穴的墙壁和顶上密密麻麻地涂写着一些潦草的象形文字，其中最引人注目的是一个圆形的类人脸的符号。我们的翻译算法成功地解码了许多这类符号，其中这一符号指代这颗星球的卫星。

在洞穴中，灵能的存在已经爆表了。不幸的是，道路的尽头被一处数世纪历史的塌方所封堵，只要稍给一些时间，探险队应该可以设法通过。
ancrel.15002.desc.en:
At last reaching their tracked coordinates, the archaeology team discovered a winding river valley hidden beneath the canopy. Rushing forth from a circular cave-mouth, the river apparently stems from some massive, underground spring. A precarious stairway, carved from the rocks several thousand years ago, delivered the team to a subterranean tunnel.

The cave's walls and ceiling are covered in a compact scrawl of ideographs, the most prominent of which is a round, humanoid face. Our translation algorithms have succeeded in decoding much of the symbology, and this particular image likely represents the planet's moon.

Within the cave, the presence of psionic energy is off the charts. Unfortunately, the path ahead was blocked by a cave-in several centuries ago, but given time, the expedition should be able to find a way through.

ancrel.15003.b.zh: 我们必须揭秘这个力量的源泉。
ancrel.15003.b.en: We must uncover the source of this power.

ancrel.15003.desc.zh: [From.Planet.GetName]上的科学团队发来了一封喜报！成功进入洞穴下层后，他们最终抵达了一个开阔的、半球形的石室。在这里，河道围绕着一座小小的岛屿流淌，小岛的中央是一块稀有晶体构成的石笋。这座石笋是由数百万年的水滴逐渐形成的，而它似乎就是整颗行星奇异灵能的源头。研究团队发现了宗教仪式的痕迹，还有若干仪式性的人造小祭器散布在石笋支柱的周围。除此之外，多相位扫描还在支柱的地基中发现了一个圆形的物体。一旦挖掘出来，这个物体有很大希望能够提供一些关于这个神秘地方的本质的线索。
ancrel.15003.desc.en: A note of triumph from our science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! After successfully reaching the lower levels of the cave, they at last arrived in a wide, hemispherical chamber. There, the river parts around a small island, at the center of which is a stalagmite of rare crystals. Formed drop-by-drop over the course of several millennia, the pillar appears to be the source of the planet's strange, psionic energy. The team has discovered evidence of religious ritual, as well as several small artifacts of ceremonial significance scattered around the pillar. What's more, a multiphasic scan revealed a round object embedded in the pillar's base. Hopes are high that, once removed, this artifact will shed some light on the true nature of this mysterious place.

ancrel.15004.desc.zh:
在[From.Planet.GetName]的科学团队有了新的突破！他们小心地将晶体支柱完整地挖掘了出来。其中保存着一个古老的、类人的面具。它的里侧写着一些象形文字，指明这件文物的名字叫做“造化之面具”。这些字符可能会意自这颗行星的卫星所具有的转变性的力量，即随着月相的变化操控潮涨潮落。

面具本身则具有难以置信的灵能性质，很有可能就是这颗行星发生快速气候变化的原因。无论是谁培养了那座晶体支柱，以及谁精心种植了那些复杂的林冠地图，他们很显然都是出自崇拜并保护这件文物的目的。团队提出的理论是，如果运用得当，这个面具可以协助我们的帝国转变整颗行星。
ancrel.15004.desc.en:
A breakthrough from the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! Their careful excavation of the crystal pillar is complete. Preserved within was an ancient, humanoid mask. Ideographs on the reverse side refer to the artifact as The Mask of Transformation. This is likely a reference to the transformative power of the planet's moon, controlling the tides as it transitions from one phase to the next.

The Mask itself possesses incredible psionic properties, and is likely responsible for the rapid climatological transformation of the planet. Whoever fostered the crystal pillar and planted the elaborate map of trees in the forest above clearly intended to honor and protect this artifact. The team theorizes that, if properly used, the Mask may enable our empire to transform entire worlds.

ancrel.15005.desc.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上传来了坏消息，我们的科研团队没能成功地把那件文物从晶体石笋中取出。可能出于操作过于暴力，团队把这座支柱彻底砸碎了。更糟糕的是，其中的文物被损坏到无法辨认，而整间石室里充盈的灵能霎时消失无踪。

所幸这些晶体本身还是颇具价值的。即使我们也许永远无法完全了解这个先驱文明修建这个场所的目的，我们的努力至少没有完完全全白费。
ancrel.15005.desc.en:
Frustration on [From.Planet.GetName] as our science team has failed to remove the artifact from the crystal stalagmite. Perhaps working with too much vigor, the team's efforts caused the pillar to shatter. Worse, the artifact within was damaged beyond recognition, and all traces of psionic energy have vanished from the chamber.

One minor consolation is that the crystal itself could prove extremely valuable. While we may never fully understand the intentions of the precursor civilization that built this place, at least our efforts have not entirely been in vain.

ancrel.15006.desc.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上的科研团队发来紧急通讯！他们对丛林的鲁莽涉足似乎严重地激怒了一些当地的种群。

在几个夜晚中，团队成员看到了倏然闪过的阴影，在林下灌木从中时隐时现。然后，在月圆之夜，一支像猿类一样的生物组成的部队从天而降，嚎叫并挥舞着棍子。得益于我们先进的科技，这些袭击者很快被赶回了树上，不过还是有几名探险队的成员被他们掳走了。茂密的树林中还能听到他们哀嚎的回响。

尽管遭遇到了危险，科学家[Root.GetLeaderName]许诺仍会继续探索。
ancrel.15006.desc.en:
Emergency transmission from the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]! Their rough foray into the jungle appears to have badly angered some of the local fauna.

Over the course of several nights, the team sighted fleeting shadows, half-glimpsed between the underbrush. Then, on the eve of the full moon, a troop of simian-like creatures descended on the expedition, howling and brandishing sticks. Given our technological advantage, these raiders were quickly driven back into the trees, but not before they had made off with several members of the team. We are told the dense foliage did little to muffle the screams.

Despite the danger, scientist [Root.GetLeaderName] has vowed to continue the expedition.

ancrel.15007.a.zh: 那些猿类也没什么大不了的！

ancrel.15007.desc.zh: 我们从[From.Planet.GetName]上的探险队获悉了一条新消息。在迷宫般的丛林中探索比起先预期的还要困难。我们的团队每挣扎前进一步都要和意料之外的沼泽、坚硬诡异的藤蔓做斗争，同时还要面对那些出奇智慧的类猿生物。研究团队通过驯服一些温顺的有蹄类生物，终于是穿过了丛林中最困难的地区。它们还可以在巨大树木的树根下找到埋着某种类虫生物肉的埋藏点。因为这些生物看起来非常兴奋，这些虫肉一定是当地的某种美味佳肴。更重要的是，研究团队很快也从树林的地表下发掘出了一些制造物件，这些小发现也进一步表明了这颗行星上曾经存在着先驱文明。
ancrel.15007.desc.en: We have received an update from the expedition on [From.Planet.GetName]. Navigating the labyrinthine jungle has proven more challenging than initially hoped. As the team struggled to push forward, stymied by unexpected marshes and thick, creeping vines, they were approached by an unusually intelligent simian. Picking its way through the foliage on the back of a tamed ungulate, the creature led the team through the worst of the jungle. It also made sure to point out caches of edible insectoid larvae buried in the roots of the great trees. Given the creature's excited gestures, these must be something of a local delicacy. More importantly, the tip resulted in further evidence of the planet's precursor civilization, as the team quickly unearthed several artifacts from the forest floor.

ancrel.15008a.desc.zh: [From.Planet.GetName]上的研究团队遭遇了一些困难。在树林中意外发现了一座蜿蜒崎岖的河谷，他们在丛林地表的探索近乎停滞了。汹涌的河水中尖石穿空，犬牙交错，从现在这条路线几乎无法通过。随之而来的绕道又带来了意想不到的后果：一支当地群居猿类的大队靠近了他们。这些长着斜眉毛的生物以取悦探险队为乐事，每晚他们都满载着大量发酵的浆果而来。尽管士气空前高涨，但进度仍然缓慢，项目领导汇报时警告整支团队可能缺失行动力。
ancrel.15008a.desc.en: Hard times for the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]. Progress through the jungle ground to a near halt with the unexpected discovery of a river valley winding beneath the trees. The raging waters are stuttered with sharp rocks, and have proven impassable along the team's chosen course. The resulting detour has had surprising consequences: the arrival of a gregarious troop of local simians. These slope-browed creatures have delighted in entertaining the expedition, arriving each night laden with an extremely potent variety of fermented berry. Although morale is higher than ever, progress continues to slow, and the project lead reports an alarming lack of initiative among the team.

ancrel.15008b.desc.zh: [From.Planet.GetName]上的研究团队遭遇了一些困难。在树林中意外发现了一座蜿蜒崎岖的河谷，他们在丛林地表的探索近乎停滞了。汹涌的河水中尖石穿空，犬牙交错，从现在这条路线几乎无法通过。随之而来的绕道又带来了意想不到的后果：一支当地群居猿类的大队靠近了他们。这些长着斜眉毛的生物以取悦探险队为乐事，每晚他们都满载着大量发酵的浆果而来。尽管我们无法消化他们的礼物，这支团队还是被猿类大队所吸引，沉迷这些生物的有趣行为而荒废了任务。
ancrel.15008b.desc.en: Hard times for the science team on [From.Planet.GetName]. Progress through the jungle ground to a near halt with the unexpected discovery of a river valley winding beneath the trees. The raging waters are stuttered with sharp rocks, and have proven impassable along the team's chosen course. The resulting detour has had surprising consequences: the arrival of a gregarious troop of local simians. These slope-browed creatures have delighted in entertaining the expedition, arriving each night laden with an extremely potent variety of fermented berry. Despite our inability to digest their gift, the team has nevertheless taken to the troop, indulging the creatures' antics at the expense of the mission.

ancrel.15010.desc.zh:
我们的科学家在[From.Planet.GetName]发现了一些奇怪的东西。作为一颗热带星球，其表面大片区域被茂密的丛林覆盖：巨大的、寿达千年的古树从林冠中突兀而起，它们枝叶茂密的树冠俯瞰着其他陆上景观。

初看起来，这些参天大树的分布似乎杂乱无章。然而，更详细的分析表明这些树的分布具有数学精准性，也许是由某个消失已久的文明所种植的。不仅如此，团队领袖相信，树木的分布方式可能包含着一组坐标，指向丛林深处某个未被探索的区域。
ancrel.15010.desc.en:
Our scientists have discovered something unusual on [From.Planet.GetName]. A tropical world, much of the planet's surface is covered with dense jungle: massive, thousand year old trees erupt from the canopy, their leafy crowns towering over the landscape.

At first glance, the distribution of these giants appears random. However, further analysis indicates that the trees are arranged with mathematical precision, and it seems likely they were planted by some long-vanished civilization. What's more, the team leader believes the distribution pattern may comprise a set of coordinates, one that points to an unexplored location deep within the jungle.

ancrel.15021.desc.zh:
正如我们预期，这艘“恒星帆船”的内部相当古色古香。它的舰桥甚至仍是仿照古时候在行星液态海面上航行的那种帆船进行设计的。

甲板的材料似乎是金属，但大部分表面又以雕刻的木材覆盖，而观察窗和数据显示屏又是以类似玻璃的材料制成。

将舰船的计算机通电后，我们发现了一首老式的航海家之歌的数据文件。据我们的考古学家称，这种旋律曾一度被称为“船歌”或者“太空船歌”。我们目前正在尝试翻译歌词。
ancrel.15021.desc.en:
As we expected, the interior of this 'solar sailer' is appropriately archaic. The bridge resembles the deck of an old planetbound sailing ship designed to sail on watery seas.

The deck plating appears to be metal, but most surfaces are covered with carved wood, a contrast to the glass-like substance on viewports and datascreens.

Powering up the ship's computers, we have found a datafile with an old-fashioned seafarers' song. According to our archaeologist, this melody was once known as a 'sea chanty' or 'space shanty.' We are attempting to transcribe the lyrics.

ancrel.15022.desc.zh:
在我们完成对数据文件的修复和重新激活后，很快一首敲击节拍的音乐旋律充盈起了整艘舰船，伴随着一个自动调音过后的古代航海家的歌声。歌词大意：

“来啊，航行太空的年轻小伙子们，请听吧！
我要唱一首畅游于大海的鱼之歌！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。

恒星风骤起，
带我向远方。
穿过那太空航道，
我们驶向星光！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。”
ancrel.15022.desc.en:
Immediately after we completed the restoration and reactivation of the datafiles, a thrumming musical cadence surged throughout the ship, accompanied by the auto-tuned voices of ancient mariners. Transcription follows:

'Come all you young spacefarers, listen to me!
I'll sing you a song of our fish from the sea!

And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes.

Up come the solar winds
Taking us far
All through the space lanes
And out to the stars!

And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes!

ancrel.15023.desc.zh:
在我们探索这艘舰船的过程中，进一步的重新充能和对数据文件的恢复解锁了这首远古太空船歌的更多章节。这艘船的全息投影显示出水手、航海家们一起载歌载舞的扭曲抽动的影像：

“巨龙忽降临
寻找着我们的家乡
越过茫茫太空
找到波涛下的那个地方！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。

缇扬奇跃起
它是深空之王
在这超空间竞速中
与我们的舰船互不相让

（合唱重复）

星神兽出现了！
它伸出触手
扼住了我们的舰船
我们惊恐万状！”
ancrel.15023.desc.en:
As we explored the ship, further attempts to power it up and recover its datafiles unlocked more stanzas of the ancient space shanty. The ship's holographic display vibrantly projected images of sailors and spacefarers singing and dancing in accompaniment:

'Up comes the Great Dragon
In search of our home
Through space to a place that's
Beneath waves and foam!

'And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow!
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes.

'Up comes the Tiyanki
The king of deep space
Racing our ships
In a hyperspace chase!

(chorus repeats)

'Up comes Leviathan
Tentacles grasp
Choking our ship
As we shiver and gasp!

(chorus repeats)

ancrel.15024.desc.zh:
我们的考古学家发现了一处可能是饮料的贮藏点。那些水手们喝的就是这种臭不可闻的液体么？我们肯定是不会喝这些奇怪的液体的。但我们对这艘船的探索成果着实令人沉醉！

“石质人来了
他们从巨岩中诞生
当他们聚到一起
这些巨砾将强壮无比！

（合唱）

死灵族来了
恐怖而又高大
你怎么都杀不死他们，伙计
他们还能复活！

（合唱）

机器蜂群来了
大家快跑吧
你得打一个、十个、一百个
1101！

（合唱）”
ancrel.15024.desc.en:
Our archaeologists have unearthed of a stash of potent potables. Were the sailors consuming these foul fluids? We will not ingest these strange liquids. Our exploration of the ship is already sufficiently intoxicating!

'Up come the Lithoids
All hewn from their stone
These boulders are bolder
When they're not alone!

(chorus)

'Up come the Necroids
All fearsome and great
You can't kill them, mateys,
They'll reanimate!

(chorus)

'Up come swarms of robots
Get ready to run
Fight one, ten, a dozen,
1101!

(chorus)

ancrel.15025.a.zh: 记下这些歌词，设定新的航向！
ancrel.15025.a.en: Memorize the lyrics and set the next course!

ancrel.15025.desc.zh:
我们的探索人员发现了远古历史的一隅，向世人展现了古代探险家们的热血和勇敢。显然，船长使用这首“太空船歌”来激励船员、协调行动。甚至他们独处的时候都喜欢唱这首歌！我们的考古学家认为，这部作品应当保存到博物馆当中。

至于这支古老的歌曲，我们已经翻译了能找到的全部歌词，并存入了我们的数据库。我们的“水手”甚至从中获取灵感，唱起了我们自己版本的太空船歌，这也能大大激发他们的士气和效率。

“我们生于深海
直抵苍穹
我们建设家园
直到永久！

小伙子们，狂风将起，风暴将临
当大风吹起，我们就出航吧！
大风向远方吹吧，嘿！快吹吧！
向着星海，她缓缓启航。”

现在是时候从这艘古老舰船中离开了，“抛开锚链”，借助恒星风扬帆起航。我们的大船将向着星海深处稳稳航行！
ancrel.15025.desc.en:
Our exploration has revealed a glance of ancient history, displaying the zeal and courage of ancient explorers. Clearly the captain used this 'space shanty' to motivate and coordinate the crew. Perhaps they even sang along! Our archaeologists are suggesting this performance should be preserved in a museum installation.

As for the ancient melody, we've transcribed all the lyrics we could find and added them to our databanks. Our own 'sailors' now have a habit of singing versions of their own space shanties, which should improve their morale and efficiency.

'We rose from the ocean
And reached for the sky
We're building an empire
That never will die!

'And it's windy weather, boys, stormy weather, boys
When the wind blows, then we're all together, boys
Blow ye winds fringeward, hey! Blow ye winds, blow
Out to the galaxy, steady she goes!'

It's time to untether from this ancient vessel, 'casting off the hawser' as we set sail on solar winds. Steady as she goes!

ancrel.16.desc.zh:
我们发现了数个水晶并成功与其通讯，其中包括一位被流放的虚境实体研究员的记录。有了这个，我们对泽珞族的战争有了更多的了解。

以生命为代价得到的泽珞尘为福音派带来了转机，他们与升格派有了一战之力。然而，随着战败的阴影逐渐笼罩，升格派的愤怒和恐惧更进一步催化了新的可怕的虚境实体的诞生。这种反馈循环不断发展，将升格派推入疯狂的深渊。他们不断地制造更为骇人听闻的暴行，而福音派则越来越不计代价地试图终结这场战争。
ancrel.16.desc.en:
We have found- and communicated with several crystals, including one from the outcast Shroud-entity researchers. With these, we are learning more about the Zroni's war.

Using the Zro dust required great sacrifice from the Saviors, but with it they were able to turn the tide of their war against the Divine. As their defeat loomed, the ever-increasing rage and fear of the Divine spawned new and terrible entities within the Shroud. The feedback loop grew, pushing the Divine into the depths of madness. They were driven to ever-worsening atrocities, urging the Saviors to end the war at any cost.

ancrel.17.desc.zh:
随着我们与更多水晶建立通讯，越来越多的细节浮出水面：升格派在即将败亡之际决定实施最终计划：轮回之终末。星系核心处黑洞的增长将被加速，以尽可能快的速度吞噬掉整个星系。

在最坏的情况下，福音派（和所有其他物种）都将被毁灭，留下升格派在一段漫长却有限的时间内统治虚境，但也有可能黑洞的膨胀会达到自我维续的程度，不仅吞噬掉本星系，还会毁灭宇宙本身，给升格派提供无穷无尽的能量——就算不是无穷尽，因为能量总量和无穷足够接近，因此没有任何实际差别。
ancrel.17.desc.en:
As we communicate with more crystals, more details emerge. On the brink of defeat, the Divine decided upon their ultimate plan: the end of the cycle. The growth of the black hole galactic core would be accelerated to consume the galaxy as soon as possible.

At worst, the Saviors - and every other species in the galaxy - would be destroyed, leaving the Divine to rule the shroud for a vast but finite time. It was, however, possible that the expansion would become self-sustaining, consuming not just the galaxy but the universe itself: providing a source of energy which may not be infinite, but would at least come close enough amount to make no practical difference.

ancrel.18.desc.zh:
我们已经知悉了泽珞族的末路：当福音派知晓了升格派的最终计划后，加之升格派在虚境的防御简直固若金汤，他们只剩一条路可走了。毁灭已然近在眼前，他们选择牺牲几乎所有人口，只留下最后一人，最后的福音派将使用整个物种献祭而来的灵能尘去消灭每一个泽珞人——不放过升格派的任何一人——从而彻底终结这场浩劫。

泽珞族被几乎不留痕迹地从宇宙抹去，只剩下一小点未使用的泽珞尘……
ancrel.18.desc.en:
We have learned the fate of the Zroni: when the Saviors learned of the Divine's plan, they knew there was only one possible counter to the Divine's almost-impenetrable defenses in the Shroud. Faced with annihilation, they chose to sacrifice their entire population save for one Zroni. This last remaining Savior used the psionic residue of an entire species to destroy every Zroni - and thus every Divine - in existence, ending the threat for all time.

The Zroni were wiped out almost without a trace, save for a small amount of unconsumed dust.

ancrel.19.desc.zh: 当我们的探险队准备离开时，其中一块灵能晶体突然与我们重新建立了联系。它表示自己将会对我们有用，应该带着它一起走。即使它所言为虚，其它晶体也没有表现出任何智慧。因此我们应当带走它进行进一步的调查。
ancrel.19.desc.en: As our expedition made ready to leave, one of the psionic crystals suddenly re-established contact. It has indicated that it could prove useful to us, should we decide to bring it with us. Even if the claim is untrue, none of the other crystals we encountered showed signs of sapience; this could warrant further investigation.

ancrel.2.desc.zh: 这片奇怪的废墟除了疏于管理之外没有任何损坏的迹象。住所，工厂，未知用途的建筑，四处空空荡荡，了无人烟。人们都去哪儿了？似乎在殖民地中心的一座大型建筑物内能找到问题的答案。
ancrel.2.desc.en: The strange ruins show no sign of damage beyond neglect. Homes, factories, buildings of unknown use: they all stand empty and abandoned. Where did everyone go? It seems likely that a large building in the center of the colony may hold the answers.

ancrel.2000.desc.zh:
[Root.GetName]的船员们兴奋地报告称他们在[From.GetName]上发现了一处古代太空文明的遗迹，其似乎于七百万年前定居于这一行星！

尽管这些自称古茹努尔的物种离开[From.GetStarName]星系的原因尚不明确，我们的科学家已经在这颗行星上分离出了一处很有发掘价值的考古遗址。

也许进一步的研究会找到更多线索。
ancrel.2000.desc.en:
The [Root.GetName] crew are eager to report they have uncovered the remains of an ancient space-faring species on [From.GetName], who appear to have inhabited the planet some seven million years ago!

While it is unclear why this species, who called themselves the Grunur, disappeared from the [From.GetStarName] system, our scientists have isolated a promising archaeological dig site on their planet.

Perhaps further study will yield more clues.

ancrel.2001.desc.zh:
在对发掘现场找到的古代数据晶体进行解密后，我们获得了一份古茹努尔战功的编年史。虽然大多只是他们的本地事务，对我们意义不大，其中仍有数卷详细描述了古茹努尔与被称为巴奥有机体的外星物种的第一次接触。

除了巴奥是一种巨型植物类物种，在群星间播种了众多殖民地以外，我们目前对它还所知无几。
ancrel.2001.desc.en:
Decoded ancient datacrystals have been found at the dig site, chronicling the Grunur's military exploits. While most are local and of little interest, several volumes detail the Grunur's first encounter with an alien species referred to as The Baol Organism.

Little more can be gleaned about the Baol at this point, save that they were a massive, plantoid species, and had many colonies seeded among the stars.

ancrel.2002.a.zh: 或许对[baol_colony_1.GetName]开展深入调查会让我们获益良多。
ancrel.2002.a.en: Perhaps a closer investigation of [baol_colony_1.GetName] will prove fruitful.

ancrel.2002.desc.zh:
数据晶体中的记录表明古茹努尔曾对巴奥发动战争，希图夺取其行星据称拥有的丰富资源。我们已经成功从一份该类型的记录中提取出了一组恒星系坐标！

我们的考古学家正在将该行星的位置上传至我们的系统中。
ancrel.2002.desc.en:
Datacrystal records reveal that the Grunur waged war against the Baol, desiring the plentiful resources purportedly found on their planets. A set of system coordinates has been successfully extracted from one such record!

Our archaeologists are uploading the planet's location to our systems now.

ancrel.2003.desc.zh:
尽管在[first_grunur_site.GetName]发现的古代古茹努尔数据晶体宣称此处存在丰富的资源，[baol_colony_1.GetName]只是一颗干旱、荒凉的星球，甚至没有大气层。

幸运的是，地质扫描表明在行星深处的沉积层中存在几乎取之不尽的化石状生物遗体！遗体中最有可能是巴奥的是一种植物类物种，因为只有该物种具备开智生物所需要的神经结构。

一次定向发掘应当可以揭示更多信息。
ancrel.2003.desc.en:
Despite the promise of riches suggested in the ancient Grunur datacrystals recovered from [first_grunur_site.GetName], [baol_colony_1.GetName] is a dry, barren world, void of atmosphere.

Fortunately, geological scans have revealed a near-endless trove of fossilized remains deep in the planet's sedimentary record! Among them is a plantoid species most likely to have been the Baol, as it is the only one identified in possession of the neurological structures required for sapience.

A targeted excavation should uncover more information.

ancrel.2003.name.zh: 前巴奥殖民地：不毛之地

ancrel.2004.desc.zh:
地质编录中显示的灰烬厚层和引人注目的大规模灭绝事件与先前从古茹努尔数据晶体中提取到的材料相吻合，表明是古茹努尔在大约七百万年前使用胶凝燃烧弹轰炸了[From.Planet.GetName]。

在行星地表肆虐的森林大火扰乱了当地的生态系统，由于缺少能进行光合作用的植物，行星的大气层在接下来六万年间被逐渐消耗殆尽。
ancrel.2004.desc.en:
Thick layers of ash and a notable mass-extinction event in the geological record coincide with material previously extracted from Grunur datacrystals, suggesting the Grunur firebombed [From.Planet.GetName] with a gelling incendiary roughly seven million years ago.

Widespread deforestation of the planet's surface disrupted local ecosystems, and the lack of oxygen-fixing vegetation gradually depleted the planet's atmosphere over the next sixty-thousand years.

ancrel.2005.desc.zh:
我们找到了数具保存完好的巴奥化石，其揭示出这一早已消失的物种具有蜂巢思维：数十亿植物体单位同心协力一体合作，如同一棵树上的枝、叶和根。树木年轮学分析表明个体巴奥的寿命可达数百年。

[From.Planet.GetName]上缺少残留的建筑物似乎是由巴奥对其高度发达的有机科技的依赖造成的。时光流逝让他们的舰船、建筑和湿体电脑消失殆尽。
ancrel.2005.desc.en:
Several exemplary Baol fossils have been recovered, revealing the long-lost species to have been a Hive Mind: billions of plantoid units working together as a whole, like the leaves and roots and branches of a tree. Dendrochronology suggests individual Baol specimens had lifespans in the hundreds of years.

The lack of structural ruins on [From.Planet.GetName] appears to be the result of the Baol's reliance on remarkable organic technology, from ships and buildings to wetware biocomputers, and the ravages of time.

ancrel.2006.desc.zh: 我们从一块破碎的古茹努尔数据晶体中提取到了另一个前巴奥殖民地的坐标！也许这颗行星上会有巴奥古老的敌人们所追寻的财富。
ancrel.2006.desc.en: Coordinates describing the location of another former Baol colony have been extracted from a shattered Grunur datacrystal! Perhaps this planet will boast some of the riches sought after by the Baol's ancient enemies.

ancrel.2007.a.zh: 真可惜。也许我们会从中学到些什么。
ancrel.2007.a.en: A pity. Perhaps we will learn more.

ancrel.2007.desc.zh:
[Root.GetName]的船员最初确信他们在进行三角定位以推算[Root.GetStarName]恒星系中的巴奥殖民地的理论位置时出了差错，因为在原本该有足以支持生命存在的行星的位置上除了若干小行星之外什么都没有。

但是，对这些小行星成分更进一步的研究表明它们事实上是前巴奥殖民地的残骸！大约是在七百万年前，曾经草木葱茏的行星被未知撞击炸成了数千块碎片。可以推断古茹努尔在这颗行星的悲惨结局中起到了某种作用。

一颗最有发掘价值的小行星已被选定为接下来研究的对象，在其上保留有消失行星上大量生物的化石化残骸。
ancrel.2007.desc.en:
The crew of the [Root.GetName] were initially certain they had made a triangulation mistake when deducing the coordinates of the supposed Baol colony in the [Root.GetStarName] system, having found nothing but asteroids where they expected a life-bearing planet.

However, closer study of the asteroids' composition has revealed that they are in fact what remains of the former Baol colony! The once-lush planet was blown into several thousand rocky pieces by some unknown collision, occurring roughly seven million years ago. Deduction suggests the Grunur played some role in the planet's dark fate.

One particularly promising asteroid has been selected for further study, as it appears to possess a large number of fossilized lifeforms from the lost planet.

ancrel.2007.name.zh: 前巴奥殖民地：破碎行星

ancrel.2008.desc.zh:
我们设法从一块保存状况良好的巴奥生物计算机化石中提取出了一些数据片段！这一千万年前的古老遗物看起来存贮着教育学相关的信息，供该物种的未成年个体使用。由于尚未准备好与蜂巢思维进行完整的神经链接，幼年巴奥，或者说幼树，会被以更为精心设计的方式教授育苗技术、园艺学与营养学。

这些发现表明巴奥社会十分重视陆地景观美化和生态环境管理，其自身的生存也高度依赖这些技术。
ancrel.2008.desc.en:
We have managed to extract some data fragments from a particularly well-preserved Baol biocomputer fossil! This ten million year old relic appears to contain pedagogical information, intended for immature members of the species. Not yet ready to receive the full range of the Hive Mind's neural connection, young Baol, or saplings, were introduced to growth techniques, horticulture, and nutrition in a more curated experience.

These findings suggest Baol society prized terrestrial landscaping and ecosystem management, and were also highly dependent on it for their survival.

ancrel.2009.desc.zh:
发现另一台巴奥生物计算机的残片让我们对这一植物类蜂巢思维物种的历史有了更深入的了解。

巴奥看起来是纯粹的植物生命体，发源于位置未知的单一行星。史前巴奥全都是其亲代植物的克隆体，在其母星上缓慢而平和地生长了数百万年，并逐步发展出了承载蜂巢意识的能力。
ancrel.2009.desc.en:
The discovery of another ancient Baol biocomputer remnant has yielded further insight into this plantoid Hive Mind's history.
