研究站本身没什么特别。它规模很小，只是用来对抗严酷环境的一个临时庇护所，仅能在严酷的环境拖垮之前，进行时间有限的表面级的星球研究。

[From.From.From.GetName]的研究站已经接近生命的尽头，但那颗星球的严寒还未压下最后一根稻草。那些功能正常、廉价且可抛弃的器材得到了充分使用，本地数据库中填满了详尽却极为寻常的行星数据，以及在严酷环境下进行的简单试验。

有趣的是，似乎研究站地基下的矿脉并没有得到深入检查。[Root.GetName]的扫描表明这座大部分被冰雪覆盖的山脉可能是中空的。更令人警觉的是，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]报告这座研究站唯一的栖居者，那位神秘的“流亡者”消失不见了。
anomaly.171.desc.en:
There is nothing unusual about the research outpost itself. It is little but a temporary shelter erected against the savage elements, allowing surface-level planetary study for a limited time before it wears down and conditions become untenable.

The outpost on [From.From.From.GetName] is nearing the end of its lifespan, but the planet's intense chill has yet to critically degrade the impermanent structure. The equipment - functional, cheap, intended to be abandoned - is well-used, and the local databanks are filled with detailed but ultimately mundane accounts of the planet as well as the simple experiments that were carried out in its harsh environment.

Curiously, no closer examination seems to have been made of the mineral outcropping the outpost's foundations rest on; scans by the [Root.GetName] indicate that the geological formation, a mountain mostly buried under ice, may be partially hollow. More alarmingly, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the sole inhabitant of the outpost, the mysterious "exile," has gone missing and is nowhere to be found.

anomaly.172.desc.zh:
[From.From.From.GetName]上的研究站有点不寻常。建筑本身并无奇怪之处——用来对抗严酷环境的小型临时庇护所，仅能在严酷的环境拖垮之前，进行时间有限的表面级的星球研究——但它恰巧建在突破星球表面冰海的岩石之上。

[Root.GetName]的成员发现，这座山的内部有复杂的洞穴和通道，由研究站内部便可进入。

在一个较大的岩洞里，他们发现了研究站原成员脱水的遗体。这些[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]研究员原先被派往别处，但显然，他们却来到了这个无人居住的危险行星。

当然，那个所谓的“流亡者”如今已经不见踪影。[Root.GetName]发射了一所逃生舱，将逝者的遗体送回[Root.Owner.Capital.GetName]。
anomaly.172.desc.en:
There is something unusual about the research outpost on [From.From.From.GetName]. The structure itself is commonplace enough - a temporary shelter erected against the harsh elements, allowing surface-level planetary study for a limited time before it wears down and conditions become untenable - but it is situated on top of a rocky formation poking through the sea of ice that covers the planet.

The crew of the [Root.GetName] found an intricate system of caves and narrow passages leading into this mountain, accessible from inside the research outpost.

In one of the larger cavern-halls, they found the desiccated remains of the outpost's original staff. This contingent of [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] researchers had originally been dispatched elsewhere, but evidently diverted to this uninhabited and hostile planet to set up shop.

Of course, the self-proclaimed "exile" is now nowhere to be found. The [Root.GetName] has launched one of its escape pods, transporting the bodies of the deceased back to [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

anomaly.175.desc.zh:
科研船[Root.GetName]找不到我们在[From.From.GetName]上探测到的奇怪读数的来源，这些读数似乎只是传感器的回声。不过，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]——一位自称的美食家和历史爱好者——声称在那里有了重大发现。

在几块巨大的地表冰层中发现的矿藏似乎与[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]星盐关系密切：星盐曾经是许多传统[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]菜肴中不可或缺的调料，但长期以来一直被认为在[Root.Owner.Capital.GetName]上已经枯竭。

烹饪史学家长期以来一直怀疑这种矿物调味品不是我们母星的原产物，而科学专员在[From.From.GetName]上的发现则为这一理论提供了一些支持。至于这种盐的味道是否真的像以前的[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]星盐，这并不是最重要的：仅仅是用如此相近的调味料恢复传统食品的想法，就一定会让我们的经济和味觉非常兴奋。
anomaly.175.desc.en:
Science ship [Root.GetName] could find no source for the strange readings we detected on [From.From.GetName], which appear to be mere sensor echoes. Nevertheless, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] - a self-proclaimed gourmet chef and history buff - claims to have made a significant discovery there.

A mineral deposit found in several vast patches of surface ice appears closely related to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] Stellar Salt: once an essential ingredient in many traditional [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] dishes, long thought depleted on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

Culinary historians have long suspected that this mineral condiment was not native to our homeworld, and the Science Officer's discovery on [From.From.GetName] lends some credence to this theory. Whether or not the salt actually tastes like the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] Stellar Salt of old is ultimately of little consequence: the mere idea of reviving traditional foodstuffs with such closely-matched ingredients is bound to excite our economy and our palates.

anomaly.180.b.en: The [Root.Owner.GetName] will not suffer these creatures to live.

anomaly.180.b.tooltip.zh: [Root.GetName]的工作人员们进行了详尽迅速的驱除工作，保证这些可爱的外星生物再也不会侵犯[Root.Owner.GetName]。
anomaly.180.b.tooltip.en: A swift extermination campaign carried out by the crew of the [Root.GetName] will ensure that this cutesy alien menace can never rise to threaten the [Root.Owner.GetName].

anomaly.180.c.zh: 我们只能旁观，不能干涉。
anomaly.180.c.en: We need to remain a passive observer.

anomaly.180.d.zh: 别动那些可爱的小生物，[Root.GetLeaderName]。

anomaly.180.desc.zh:
[From.From.GetName]上满是微小且斑斓的生命体，介于植物与动物之间。它们缺乏真正的进化潜能，但与体型相比，它们的力量和组织协调性令人震惊。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]迷上了他们，并承认对那个“红色的小家伙”情有独钟。
anomaly.180.desc.en:
[From.From.GetName] is populated by tiny, colorful lifeforms that straddle the divide between flora and fauna. They lack any serious evolutionary potential, but their group coordination and great strength relative to their size is impressive.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has taken a shine to them, admitting a particular soft spot for "the red ones."

anomaly.180.e.tooltip.zh: 这些“可爱的”外星人的营养会喂饱我们的[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesSpawnNamePlural]。
anomaly.180.e.tooltip.en: The nutrients from these cutesy aliens will feed our [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesSpawnNamePlural].

anomaly.185.desc.zh:
信号似乎是从某个类似信号天线的结构中传来的。我方已经从[Root.GetName]发射了探索无人机，希望能够在星球表面发现更多线索。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]所发现的洞穴仓库十分容易地就被撬开。他判定这座仓库为某种早已灭亡的外星种族所用，似乎是其族群最后的一处避难所。该种族的科技水平虽然较为先进，但似乎从未进行太空探索，结果因为某种涉及到整颗星球的自然灾害而消亡了。库房面积广大，其中充斥着成千上万个黑匣子。据[Root.GetName]判定，这些匣子都是数据储存装置。

已发起特殊项目来进一步对这些匣子进行解读。
anomaly.185.desc.en:
The signal originates from the remains of an antenna-like structure. Exploratory probes were dispatched from the [Root.GetName] to the surface to investigate the matter more closely.

What Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] found was a cavernous vault that, while easily pried open, was evidently the last safehouse and refuge of some long-dead race of aliens. While reasonably technologically advanced, it seems they never reached for the stars and perished to some planet-wide natural disaster. The vault is immense, housing thousands upon thousands of black boxes that the [Root.GetName] has determined to be data storage devices.

A Special Project has been prepared to decode their contents.

anomaly.186.a.zh: 还是不要打扰死者了吧。

anomaly.186.a.alt.tooltip.zh: 清除[Root.Capital.GetName]的数据库中的神经网路投影。
anomaly.186.a.alt.tooltip.en: Purge the neural scans from the databanks on [Root.Capital.GetName].

anomaly.186.b.zh: 将神经模式下载到我们的数据库。
anomaly.186.b.en: Download the neural patterns for safekeeping.

anomaly.186.desc.v1.zh:
此次发现的避难所原来是一个希望永生的物种的大型坟墓。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]判定，这些巨大的匣子中所充满的三进制编码，实际上是神经网路投影、数据化的脑部扫描结果。毫无疑问，[From.From.GetName]的异星物种认为这是他们在星球毁灭前唯一的存活方法。虽然他们无法拯救自己，但心中仍然希望着或许有一天，其它物种可以使用这些数据来复活他们。
anomaly.186.desc.v1.en:
The vault is a tomb for hopeful immortals.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] asserts that the huge blocks of ternary code found in the databanks are neural images - digitized brain scans. Doubtless the aliens of [From.From.GetName] considered this their only shot at any kind of survival, following whatever calamity befell their planet. They did not have the means to resurrect themselves, but banked on the impossibly small hope that eventually, someone else would have those means.

anomaly.186.desc.v3.zh:
此次发现的避难所原来是一个希望永生的物种的大型坟墓。

数据库中发现的大量三进制编码，实际上是神经网路投影、数据化的脑部扫描结果。毫无疑问，[From.From.GetName]的异星物种认为这是他们在星球毁灭前唯一的存活方法。虽然他们没有复活自己的技术，但仍然抱着终有一天会有其他文明帮他们做到的微小希望。

考虑到我们高度发达的机器人技术，研究员们确信我们的机器人拥有承载这种高等智慧的精密度。
anomaly.186.desc.v3.en:
The vault is a tomb for hopeful immortals.

The huge blocks of ternary code found in the databanks are neural images - digitized brain scans. Doubtless the aliens of [From.From.GetName] considered this to be their only shot at survival, following whatever calamity befell their planet. Lacking the means to resurrect themselves, they banked on the small hope that eventually, someone else would.

With our expertise in the field of advanced robotics, researchers are confident that our robots are sophisticated enough to support a higher intelligence.

anomaly.186.desc.v4.zh:
此次发现的避难所原来是一个希望永生的物种的大型坟墓。

这些数据库中充满了大段的三进制编码，其中储存着的是他们的生物中央处理单元。[From.From.GetName]的异星物种似乎认为这是他们唯一的幸存方法。虽然他们无法拯救自己，但仍希望着其它物种或许可以做到。

我们可以将这些神经扫描结果传输到我们的机器人身躯中，但这样的实验是很难预料其结果的。
anomaly.186.desc.v4.en:
The vault is a tomb for hopeful immortals.

Within its databanks lie massive blocks of ternary code, housing digitized scans of their biological central processing units. The aliens of [From.From.GetName] likely saw this as their only chance for survival. Unable to resurrect themselves, they hoped that someone else would.

We can transfer these neural scans into robotic bodies like ours, but the results of such an experiment are difficult to predict.

anomaly.186.e.en: Download their neural patterns to the $building_identity_repository$.

anomaly.186.e.tt.en: 500 more Identities will be added to the $building_identity_repository$.

anomaly.189.a.tooltip.zh: 外星人加入我方帝国并在[new_colony.GetName]定居。
anomaly.189.a.tooltip.en: The aliens join our empire and colonize [new_colony.GetName].

anomaly.189.b.en: It's better if we part ways.

anomaly.189.b.tooltip.zh: 外星人们将去其它地方安家。
anomaly.189.b.tooltip.en: The aliens will look for a new home elsewhere.

anomaly.189.desc.zh: 在多次尝试与挫折之后，工程部门终于将已灭绝的外星人的神经扫描结果上传到了机器人中，结果十分令人惊喜。古代外星人已经彻底恢复了意识，并表达了加入我们帝国的意愿，他们希望在我们领地内的一个新星球上定居。
anomaly.189.desc.en: After many trials and setbacks, the engineering department has finally managed to transfer the extinct aliens' neural scans to robotic bodies, and the results are exhilarating. The ancient aliens have fully regained consciousness and have expressed a desire to join our empire, offering to colonize a new planet within our borders.

anomaly.190.desc.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]汇报说，他们觉得在[Root.GetName]上采集的感应数据一点也不可靠。其中最为可疑的就是[From.From.GetName]的卫星，他们已发起特殊项目来进行进一步的调查。

详情请查看情报日志。
anomaly.190.desc.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that they do not trust the sensor readings they've gathered aboard the [Root.GetName], not one bit of it. They are especially suspicious of [From.From.GetName]'s moon, and have outlined a Special Project for further investigation.

Consult the Situation Log for details.

anomaly.191.a.tooltip.zh:
卫星获得了卫星勘测修正：
£engineering£+6
anomaly.191.a.tooltip.en:
Adds the Projecting Moon modifier to the moon:
£engineering£ +6

anomaly.191.desc.zh:
在卫星上发现了十分不可思议的装置。其中心为三进制电脑，其程序似乎在不断地根据其收集的行星数据进行新的排列运算。计算后产生的数据经过强力通讯列阵调制后，被发射到卫星所环绕的星球表面。虽然这信号乍一看来似乎只是乱码，但这种调制方式却能让信号进入行星大气层并被反射后变得和普通的感应采集数据没有区别。

虽然我们无法判定这装置的用处，但通过此次调查，我学习了外星生物的工程技术，受益匪浅。
anomaly.191.desc.en:
There is a device on the moon, and it is mystifying. At its core lies a ternary computer, seemingly tasked with endlessly calculating new permutations based on a core set of planetary readings. These values are then passed to a powerful comm array, which modulates the data before blasting it at the surface of its parent planet. The raw signal appears nonsensical at a casual glance, but the careful modulation ensures that it becomes nearly indistinguishable from legitimate sensor readings once the signal is reflected from the parent planet's surface and filtered through its atmosphere.

The purpose of this set-up is difficult to deduce, but provides a good opportunity to study alien engineering techniques.

anomaly.195.desc.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]报告说，在[From.From.GetName]海域之中有人为制造的大型且柔韧的几何网格，材料主要为某种复合塑料。

这些塑料网格从大气层外的轨道上依然清晰可见，其作用暂时不明，似乎只是用来装饰的。
anomaly.195.desc.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that large, flexible geometric grids made up of some plastic polymer - clearly artificial in nature - have been placed in the seas of [From.From.GetName].

Visible from orbit, they seem to serve no purpose other than, possibly, an aesthetic one.

anomaly.200.desc.zh:
轨道上监测到的规律性敲击声原来是行星上十分古老的巨大地热采集器，仍然在垂死运行着。很久前就被遗弃的这些机器虽然已经不太坚固，但仍然在源源不断地从星球核心泵出超高温的液体。

虽然其储能单元已经全部破损泄露，但仍然能够从中获取少量能源。
anomaly.200.desc.en:
The measured pounding observed from orbit is the motion of immense and ancient geothermal extractors, breathing their last. Built and then abandoned at some point in the distant past, the vast batteries of disintegrating machinery have been pumping up superheated fluids from the planet's core ever since.

Their storage capacitors are all broken or leaking, but some energy can still be siphoned from them.

anomaly.2000.default.desc.zh:
$anomaly.2000.start.desc$

科学家们的意见发生了分歧；有些认为这些东西曾经是生物，是被一种未知的力量变成了石头。而另一些则认为它们代表了一个失落已久的文明所崇拜的神灵。更谨慎的少数人认为，这些雕像不是一种致敬，而是一种警告：对任何胆敢骚扰这颗行星的人发出严厉的警告。
anomaly.2000.default.desc.en:
$anomaly.2000.start.desc$

Our scientists are divided; some believe that these forms were once living beings, turned to stone by an unknown force. Others suggest they represent deities, worshipped by a long-forgotten civilization. A more cautious few believe the statues are not a tribute, but a warning: a grim message to any who would dare to disturb the planet.

anomaly.2000.hive.desc.zh:
$anomaly.2000.start.desc$

我们的集体意识中涌出了许多关于这些雕像的不同想法，比如它们可能是被未知力量变成石头的活物，或者代表了某种古代失落文明所崇拜的神祇。亦或许这些雕像并不是致敬，而是一种警告：对任何胆敢骚扰这颗行星的人发出严厉的警告。
anomaly.2000.hive.desc.en:
$anomaly.2000.start.desc$

Many different thoughts flood our collective consciousness some of these forms could have been living beings, turned to stone by an unknown force. Or perhaps they represent deities, worshipped by a long-forgotten civilization. Maybe these statues are not a tribute, but a warning: a grim message to any who would dare to disturb the planet.

anomaly.2005.desc.zh: [From.GetName]船员的进一步调查发现，这些雕像是某种与石质类高度相似的古代物种的遗骸。曾经维持其形态的某种力量早已消散了。现在，它们暴露在自然环境中，被逐渐侵蚀成细小的灰尘，将它们的历史残余散进了[From.GetName]无情的风中。
anomaly.2005.desc.en: Further investigation by the crew of [From.GetName] has identified the statues as remnants of an ancient species bearing strong resemblance to the Lithoids. Whatever essence once held their forms together has long since deteriorated. Now, exposed to the elements, they gradually erode into fine dust scattering the remains of its history into the relentless winds of [From.GetName].

anomaly.2006.desc.zh: [From.GetName]号船员们的进一步尝试被一阵突如其来的狂风打断，这股风横扫了整个研究现场。那些脆弱的石像瞬间化为齑粉，它们曾承载的谜题也随之湮灭无痕。由于缺乏可供分析的残留证据，也无法得出明确结论，我们别无选择，只能终止此次调查。
anomaly.2006.desc.en: Further attempts by the crew of [From.GetName] were abruptly halted when a sudden gust of wind swept across the research site. The brittle stone figures crumbled into dust, erasing any trace of the riddle they once posed. With no remaining evidence to analyze and no clear conclusions to be drawn, we are left with little choice but to discontinue the investigation.

anomaly.2010.a.en: There is more to explore here.

anomaly.2010.desc.zh: 在[From.GetName]冰壳之下的勘探，我们发现了一片广阔的地下洞穴。令人惊叹的是，这座隐蔽的温室中存在着一个郁郁葱葱的生态系统——茂密的动植物在隔绝环境中蓬勃生长，受到冰层保护而远离星球表面恶劣的环境。洞穴内保持着稳定的微气候，很可能是由地热喷口维持的。
anomaly.2010.desc.en: Excavation beneath the icy crust of [From.GetName] has revealed a vast subterranean cavern. Remarkably, this hidden greenhouses is a thriving ecosystem, a lush flora and fauna flourish in isolation, protected by the ice from the planet's surface otherwise hostile environment. The cave maintains a stable microclimate, likely sustained by geothermal vents.

anomaly.2015.desc.zh:
在洞穴的更深处，我们遇到了一片广袤的花田。当主动观测开始时，整片花田瞬间绽放，整个洞窟被绚丽的生物荧光所淹没。植物学分析表明，该物种每一亿年才开花一次，需要环境因素达到精确的排列组合才能触发。

我们的到来竟与如此罕见的事件同时发生，这概率微乎其微。但无论纯属巧合还是另有玄机，这无疑是一次非凡的体验。
anomaly.2015.desc.en:
Deeper within the cavern, we encountered a sprawling field of flowers. The moment active observation began, the entire field erupted into bloom, flooding the chamber in radiant bioluminescence. Botanical analysis suggests this species only blooms once every 100 million years, triggered by a precise alignment of environmental factors.

That our arrival coincided with such an event defies all probability, but whether mere coincidence or something more, it was surely a remarkable experience.

anomaly.2020.desc.zh: 随着进一步深入洞穴，地震活动突然导致结构失稳。突如其来的构造震颤在岩壁间传导，随时可能引发坍塌。面对迅速恶化的环境，我们立即启动了紧急撤离程序。洞穴中的秘密只能徒留遗憾，无法探索了。
anomaly.2020.desc.en: Upon further descent into the cavern, seismic activity abruptly destabilized the structure. A sudden tectonic tremor cascaded through the walls, threatening to trigger an imminent collapse. Faced with the rapidly deteriorating conditions, we initiated immediate evacuation protocols. The secrets within the cave remain unexplorable.

anomaly.205.a.tooltip.zh: 所有£blocker£地块障碍已从[From.From.GetName]被移除。
anomaly.205.a.tooltip.en: All £blocker£ Tile Blockers have been cleared from [From.From.GetName].

anomaly.205.desc.zh:
在彻底调查[From.From.GetName]的地理状况后，[Root.GetName]并未能找到任何值得注意的现象。

倒不如说，此处的地理状况平淡得让人惊讶……其唯一特征就是一点特征都没有。虽然地势稍有高低之分，但[From.From.GetName]的整个地表都十分不自然地平整。同时，星球上的各种植被也十分平淡，令人过目就忘。
anomaly.205.desc.en:
A thorough geological survey of [From.From.GetName] by the [Root.GetName] reveals nothing of interest.

In fact, it is extraordinarily uninteresting - its only defining feature is its lack of defining features. There are depressions and elevations, yes, but on the whole the surface of [From.From.GetName] can be regarded as unnaturally flat. Likewise, the native flora and fauna are strikingly docile and unworthy of attention.

anomaly.210.desc.zh:
[Root.GetName]本应前往[From.From.From.GetName]研究其附近的异常状况，但途中却遭遇了不测。包括科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]及船员在内的整艘舰船在调查太空废墟时突然消失不见了。

而在数分钟后，舰船又重新出现。

据[Root.GetLeaderName]汇报，他们在一瞬之间到达了某个超维度空间。他们从外部观察口看到其附近布满了各式各样的外星舰船，都一动不动地被困在无限的虚空之中。在船员能够判定所在位置之前，船外的景色突然消失，而舰船又重新回到了普通空间之中。

但不幸的是，船上的一半工作人员都消失了——科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这些船员应该是因为某种不可知的机制而永远地被困在那里了。
anomaly.210.desc.en:
The [Root.GetName] never made it all the way to [From.From.From.GetName] to study the anomalies surrounding it. The ship, along with Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] and crew, blinked out of existence as it was navigating the debris field.

And then reappeared minutes later.

[Root.GetLeaderName] reports that they found themselves, briefly, in some extra-dimensional space. External viewports revealed that they were surrounded by countless ships of alien design, suspended in a seemingly endless void. Before the crew could get their bearings, the vision abruptly faded and they found themselves back in regular space.

However, roughly half of the crew are missing - Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] speculates that they may have been selectively trapped, by some unknowable mechanism, in that strange space.

anomaly.211.b.zh: 为了[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]人民的安全必须毁灭它。
anomaly.211.b.en: The safety of the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] people hinges on their destruction.

anomaly.211.c.zh: [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]人民的安全与否取决于是否毁灭它们。
anomaly.211.c.en: The safety of the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] hinges on their destruction.

anomaly.211.desc.zh:
原本被认为迷失在维度裂缝中的[Root.GetName]失踪船员重新出现了。

所有失踪船员都被放置在一艘与我方科技飞船相似的飞船上，漂浮在[Root.GetName]原本遇到维度陷阱的地方。船员们全数声称，并不记得这期间发生了什么事情，只是隐约觉得自己离开了一段时间。

船员们希望能够回到科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]手下工作，并将飞船移交给了[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]帝国。
anomaly.211.desc.en:
The missing members of the [Root.GetName]'s crew, thought lost to the dimensional rift, have reappeared.

They hailed us from aboard an unknown vessel, not entirely dissimilar to our own science ships, idling close to where the [Root.GetName] originally experienced the dimensional disturbance. They claim to remember nothing of their time outside our dimension, aside from a vague awareness of having been away for some time.

They wish for nothing but to return to service under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName], and intend to surrender their ship to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] authorities.

anomaly.211.desc.bio.zh:
原本被认为迷失在维度裂缝中的[Root.GetName]失踪船员重新出现了。

他们从一艘有机舰船上向我们呼叫，这艘船诡异地与我们的科研船相似，但又微妙地……不同。它的移动方式、脉搏完全不遵循任何已知的基因蓝图，仿佛是某种扭曲的外星意识对我们舰船的怪异理解。它静静的在[Root.GetName]第一次遭遇扰动的坐标附近漂浮、等待着。

船员们什么也不记得。只是有一种模糊的缺席感，一种去了别的地方的感觉，比感受到的时间长得多。然而，它们又没有改变，至少他们自己是这么说的。

船员们希望能够回到科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]手下工作，并将他们怪异而沉默飞船毫不犹豫地移交给了[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]帝国。但当我们接收到它们的信息时，一种深沉而陌生的共鸣在通信中嗡嗡作响。船虽然静止不动，但感觉好像在倾听。
anomaly.211.desc.bio.en:
The missing crew of the [Root.GetName], long presumed lost to the dimensional rift, have inexplicably reappeared.

They hailed us from aboard an unfamiliar organic construct, its form eerily similar to our own science vessels, yet subtly... off. The way it moves, the way it pulses, it follows no known genetic blueprint, as though it were a reflection of our ships seen through a warped, alien mind. It drifted silently near the coordinates where the [Root.GetName] first encountered the disturbance, waiting.

The crew remembers nothing of their time beyond. Only a vague sensation of absence, of having been somewhere else, for far longer than time should allow. And yet, they are unchanged. Or so they claim.

They wish to return to service under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName], and they offer their strange, silent vessel to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] authorities without hesitation. But as we receive their transmission, a deep and unfamiliar resonance hums through the comms. The ship, though still, feels as though it is listening.

anomaly.215.desc.zh:
[From.From.GetName]的表面充斥着许多处过于茂盛的植被，十分不自然。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]仍然无法解释这颗星球的土地为部分地区异常肥沃的机理，但认为此处的植物稍经加工就能够被[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]正常食用。
anomaly.215.desc.en:
[From.From.GetName]'s surface is dotted with irregular patches of intense greenery.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is not yet ready to explain the mechanics behind the soil's localized hyperfertility, but asserts that much of the native flora is suitable for [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] consumption with only minimal processing needed.

anomaly.215.desc.serv.zh:
[From.From.GetName]的地表散布着不规则的密集植被。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]尚无法对土地局部性异常肥沃背后的原理作出解释，但声称大多数本地植物适合供[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]活体陈设食用，而且几乎无需进行加工。
anomaly.215.desc.serv.en:
[From.From.GetName]'s surface is dotted with irregular patches of intense greenery.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is not yet ready to explain the mechanics behind the soil's localized hyperfertility, but asserts that much of the native flora is suitable for [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] Bio-Trophy consumption with only minimal processing needed.

anomaly.220.desc.zh: 科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]就[From.GetName]的矿藏进行了详细报告。由于独特的地壳构造进程，[Root.GetName]的地表附近聚集了大量的珍贵矿脉。
anomaly.220.desc.en: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has provided us with a detailed report on [From.GetName]'s geological riches. Apparently the planet's unique tectonic history has served to concentrate many minerals of interest to the [Root.GetName] near the surface.

anomaly.225.a.tooltip.en:
Adds the Shadow Play modifier to [From.GetName]:
£society£ +4

anomaly.225.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]的表面总会有大片的阴影掠过。

造成这些阴影的并非是云朵，而是大气层上方漂浮着的一层有机物质，为了便于活动，上面还有关节一般的结构。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]仍然无法判定这些有机物质是植被还是动物，也不能解释其造成的阴影到底有什么作用。
anomaly.225.desc.en:
Immense, ragged planes of shadow drift across [From.GetName]'s face.

They are cast not by clouds but by sheets of organic material drifting through the upper layers of the atmosphere, hinged - or rather jointed - to allow for a small degree of articulation.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is as yet unwilling to say whether these things are flora or fauna, or what possible purpose, if any, their elaborate shadow-casting might serve.

anomaly.230.a.zh: 仅仅研究其变化的自然过程。

anomaly.230.b.tooltip.zh: 花费能量币，尝试稳定星球并使之更宜居。大约有50%的成功几率。
anomaly.230.b.tooltip.en: Spend Energy Credits to attempt to stabilize the planet in a more favorable state, with roughly a 50% chance of success.

anomaly.230.desc.v1.zh:
[From.GetName]的地理构造的确是处在变动之中。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这是地壳活动造成的。这一地壳活动虽然有趣但是却极其深奥。不过[Root.Owner.GetName]所感兴趣的，是某种可以停止星球这一无尽且无序的自我变构的方法。简单来说，使用此方法转化星球不仅用时极短，而且理论上也有可能让星球变得更加易于居住。

[Root.GetLeaderName]需要额外的200能量币进行地理活动勘测，以证明科学专员所提出的外科手术刀式精准改造方案是否真的可行。当然，如果以后想要使用现有的环境改造科技，也是可以的。
anomaly.230.desc.v1.en:
The very geological structure of [From.GetName] is indeed in flux, driven by what Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] assures us is a tectonic process as fascinating as it is esoteric. What is of more interest to the [Root.Owner.GetName] is that we may be able to strategically halt the planet's ceaseless, chaotic self-transformation. In short, a near-instant terraforming of the planet into something slightly - if not entirely - more habitable, is theoretically possible.

[Root.GetLeaderName] estimates that an additional 200 Energy Credits will be needed to power a thorough mapping of planetary activity and determine the validity of what the Science Officer has termed "a surgical terraforming strike." Of course, we can always choose to terraform it using existing technologies at a later date.

anomaly.230.desc.v2.zh:
[From.GetName]的地理构造的确是处在变动之中。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这是地壳活动造成的。这一地壳活动虽然有趣但是却极其深奥。不过[Root.Owner.GetName]所感兴趣的，是某种可以停止星球自我变更的步骤。简单来说，使用此步骤转化星球后，不仅用时极短，而且理论上也有可能让星球变得更加易于居住。

[Root.GetLeaderName]需要额外的200能量币进行地理活动勘测，以证明科学专员所提出的方案是否真的可以使用。目前我们还无法进行常规性的环境改造，所以这次真的是千载难逢的机会。
anomaly.230.desc.v2.en:
The very geological structure of [From.GetName] is indeed in flux, driven by what Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] assures us is a tectonic process as fascinating as it is esoteric. What is of more interest to the [Root.Owner.GetName] is that we may be able to strategically halt the planet's ceaseless, chaotic self-transformation. In short, a near-instant stabilization of the planet into something slightly - if not entirely - more habitable, is theoretically possible.

[Root.GetLeaderName] estimates that an additional 200 Energy Credits will be needed to power a thorough mapping of planetary activity and determine the validity of what the Science Officer has termed "a surgical terraforming strike." Actual terraforming lies beyond our grasp at present, so this is an exciting opportunity.

anomaly.231.desc.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]汇报说，[From.From.GetName]的确能够进行改造！在星球的自身转化进入时长几个月的不稳定阶段时，我们有一个非常短暂的时机。[Root.GetLeaderName]认为可以将小型炸药植入星球地壳中，再加上星球大气层的战略性辐照作用，便可以停止[From.From.GetName]永不停歇的自我转化过程，将其转变为更加易于居住的星球。

已经设立了特殊项目，但时间十分紧迫。
anomaly.231.desc.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that [From.From.GetName] can indeed be terraformed! A narrow window of opportunity is expected to open shortly, as the planet enters a particularly unstable phase of its cycle lasting a couple of months. [Root.GetLeaderName] believes that miniaturized explosive charges delivered to the planet's crust and strategic irradiation of the atmosphere during this time will halt [From.From.GetName]'s tumultuous changes and stabilize it in a form somewhat more suitable for sustaining life.

A Special Project has been issued, but we do not have much time.

anomaly.232.desc.zh: [Root.GetName]的船员遗憾地汇报：虽然我方成功判定了环境改造的时机，但最终仍然没赶上改造[From.From.GetName]的机会。这样的机会大概几个世纪之内是不会再有了。
anomaly.232.desc.en: The crew of the [Root.GetName] are disappointed to report that the window of opportunity for terraforming [From.From.GetName] has closed, despite their best efforts to identify it in time. Another opportunity is unlikely to arise for another few centuries.

anomaly.233.desc.zh: 科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]十分骄傲地汇报：[From.From.GetName]可以被重新定位为干旱星球，而不再是荒芜星球了。此次试验的成功大大促进了[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]的科学发展。
anomaly.233.desc.en: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is proud to report that [From.From.GetName] can now be re-classified as an Arid rather than Barren planet. This grand experiment has greatly enriched the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] sciences.

anomaly.235.desc.v1.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]汇报说，覆盖[From.GetName]的冰层下遍布的闪光波浪源于外星科技。

在这颗星球上曾经发生过上古战争，当时有一架外星战机解体后在此处坠落，只有露在船身外的主武器核心没被摧毁。看起来这个外星种族所运用的激光武器与[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]舰队目前正在使用的相似，其武器核心不定期地向[From.GetName]的冰层表面放射低能射束，但因为行星的气候过于恶劣，激光无法融化冰层，所以就产生了十分美丽的光影艺术。
anomaly.235.desc.v1.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the luminous waves coursing through the ice that blankets [From.GetName] are of alien origin.

Some ancient battle has deposited scattered wreckage from an alien fighter on the frozen planet, and only the exposed core of its main weapons remains intact. It seems this alien race used lasers similar to the ones currently in use by [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] fleets, and the fizzling innards periodically discharge low-powered beams into the ice of [From.GetName]. The planet's harsh climate prevents the lasers from actually melting the ice, allowing the chilly matrix to act as a brilliant prism.

anomaly.235.desc.v2.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]汇报说，覆盖[From.GetName]的冰层下遍布的闪光波浪源于外星科技。

在这颗星球上曾经发生过上古战争，当时有一架外星战机解体后在此处坠落，只有露在船身外的主武器核心没被摧毁。看起来这个外星种族所运用的激光武器比[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]舰队目前正在使用的先进许多，其武器核心不定期地向[From.GetName]的冰层表面放射低能激光，但因为行星的气候过于恶劣，激光无法融化冰层，所以就产生了十分美丽的光影艺术。
anomaly.235.desc.v2.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the luminous waves coursing through the ice that blankets [From.GetName] are of alien origin.

Some ancient battle has deposited scattered wreckage from an alien fighter on the frozen planet, and only the exposed core of its main weapons remains intact. It seems this alien race used lasers somewhat more advanced than the ones currently in use by [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] fleets, and the fizzling innards periodically discharge low-powered lasers into the ice of [From.GetName]. The planet's harsh climate prevents the lasers from actually melting the ice, allowing the chilly matrix to act as a brilliant prism.

anomaly.240.a.tooltip.en: [From.GetName]: Revealed to be a Barren planet.

anomaly.240.desc.zh:
我们曾经以为这颗星球是十分少见的小型气体星球，但事实并非如此。

在大气层上方浮动着的一层厚厚的粉尘欺骗了科学专员们，粉尘层下面掩盖的只不过是一颗贫瘠但十分普通的行星而已。

这一发现让[Root.Owner.Capital.GetName]的天文学家们十分尴尬。
anomaly.240.desc.en:
What we had assumed was an abnormally small gas giant is, in fact, not.

Beneath a deceptive cover of thick dust swirling in the upper atmosphere lies a regular planet. A barren planet, but a planet nonetheless.

This has proven quite embarrassing to the astronomical community on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

anomaly.245.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]上的确勃勃生机。

只不过这些生物全部都极为残忍。

虽然星球十分适于殖民，但[Root.GetName]的船员警告说，可能会遭遇当地生物的大肆袭击。
anomaly.245.desc.en:
[From.GetName] is indeed teeming with life.

Dangerous life.

While ripe for colonization, the crew of the [Root.GetName] warn that we are likely to run into problems with the local wildlife.

anomaly.25.a.zh: 我们应该研究一下它的设计。

anomaly.25.desc.zh: [From.GetName]小行星内部的大部分都被挖空，用于建造疑似是船坞的工程，然而该工程早已被遗弃，数个世纪以来，一直暴露在宇宙的真空之中。就算里面曾有一些有价值的东西遗留，也早已被之前的探索者掠夺一空。船坞的设计非常独特，有很多值得借鉴学习之处。
anomaly.25.desc.en: A large portion of asteroid [From.GetName] has been hollowed out to allow for the construction of some kind of shipyard. It has been abandoned and exposed to the vacuum of space for centuries - if anything useful remained, it has already been looted by previous explorers. The design of the shipyard itself is unique, however, and much could potentially be learned by its study.

anomaly.250.desc.zh:
[Root.GetName]从[From.GetName]的表面回收了一只长方形的金属匣子。这只匣子的五个面上都有一些小孔，而科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]也因此判定这并不是装东西用的匣子，而是用来散发气味的某种工具。初试测试表明，这匣子中原本存放的气味现在仍然在缓慢地释放着。

为了查明此匣子的具体功用，已经设立了特殊项目。或许外星物种是用味道来传递信息，然后再通过大气中的化学物质接收信息，从而进行交流也不一定呢。
anomaly.250.desc.en:
The [Root.GetName] has recovered an elongated metal box from the surface of [From.GetName]. Clusters of small perforations on five sides lead Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] to believe it is not a container, but some sort of aerosol dispersal device. Initial tests seem to confirm their suspicions as trace aromatics still emanate from the object.

A Special Project has been issued to confirm whether this might be an information-carrying device constructed by some alien race communicating primarily through the secretion and reception of atmosphere-borne chemical compounds; smells.

anomaly.2501.desc.zh: 科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]推断[From.From.GetName]被当做星际墓地来使用的，许多外星种群都死在了那里。尸体则在重力的作用下经过数百万年的时间慢慢的被拉向气态巨行星。这种古老的循环在一千五百万年前最后一批生物到达后突然的中断了。我们只能推测可能它们是被其他的太空生物所猎杀，或者遇到了天灾。
anomaly.2501.desc.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has deduced that [From.From.GetName] served as an orbital graveyard, where members of the dead alien species we found came to die. Gravity took care of the rest, slowly pulling the remains into the gas giant over a period of millions of years.

This ancient cycle seems to have stopped abruptly 15 million years ago when the last creature arrived. We can only speculate as to whether they were hunted to extinction by spacefaring civilizations or met their end through some other calamity.

anomaly.251.desc.zh:
这匣子的确是存放了某种数据。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]承认，本来大家都希望匣子中存放的是星球的历史或者某种文化的重要资料，但结果却令人十分失望。

这散发着芳香的匣子中存放的乃是十分短小的几段故事，故事每一章节快到末尾的时候气味都会快速变化，而这一转变似乎是为了惊吓或逗乐读者，也就是笑话了。虽然匣子储存气味的技术值得研究，但其中的笑话却毫无价值。

[Root.GetName]的船员们因为闻了外星生物所产生的某种气味而感到不太舒心。然而，对于匣子为什么会被扔在这了无人烟的荒凉星球上，[Root.GetLeaderName]却不愿进行猜测。
anomaly.251.desc.en:
The box is indeed a document, of a sort. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] admits that they had been hoping for a historical record or some other kind of codex significant to whatever culture left it behind, but they were disappointed.

The true nature of the aromatic box seems to be a collection of fairly short narratives which, going by the rapid changes in odor towards the end of each sequence, are intended to surprise or be interpreted as comedic. The techniques used to store and reproduce specific smells is of some interest, but the tales it tells are not.

The crew of the [Root.GetName] are left with the uncomfortable feeling that they have unwittingly become intimately familiar with what certain gaseous byproducts of alien digestion smell like. However, [Root.GetLeaderName] is unwilling to speculate as to why the box was dumped on this frozen hellscape of a planet.

anomaly.2510.desc.zh: 对[From.GetName]进行深度扫描显示，覆盖表层的冰幔下面有很多水暖阀口，这些阀口将一整片大洋加热。首席[Owner.GetScientist][Root.GetLeaderName]从[Root.GetName]派遣了探测器，这些探测器钻透了几里厚的冰层，发现了地下的水体里面充满了生命。我们需要更多的资源进行一次彻底的研究，探查居住在这片深洋里的诸多生命形式。
anomaly.2510.desc.en: Deep scans of [From.GetName] have revealed a large ocean heated by hydrothermal vents beneath the ice mantle covering the surface. Lead [Owner.GetScientist] [Root.GetLeaderName] dispatched probes from the [Root.GetName] that drilled through several miles of thick ice and found the water below teeming with what appears to be life. We will need more resources to conduct a thorough study of the many unique life forms inhabiting this ocean.

anomaly.2512.desc.zh: 首席[Owner.GetScientist][Root.GetLeaderName]已经从探险中返回，结束了对[From.From.GetName]冰下之海中的丰富生物圈的调查。在大海的底层区域，科研人员发现了几种大型原生物种，它们能产生一种独特的无机分子，具有十分神奇的疗养性质。如果这种分子能够被成功地大量采集，它将会掀起医疗科学领域的一场革命，甚至可能出现产业规模的应用！
anomaly.2512.desc.en: Lead [Owner.GetScientist] [Root.GetLeaderName] has returned from the expedition that studied the rich biosphere in the seas beneath the ice mantle of [From.From.GetName]. Several large species native to the lower regions of the global sea have been found to produce a unique, inorganic molecule with immense healing properties. If this molecule is successfully harvested in large enough quantities, it could revolutionize the field of medical science, and may even have industrial applications!

anomaly.2512.desc.mach.zh:
首席[Owner.GetScientist][Root.GetLeaderName]已经从探险中返回，结束了对[From.From.GetName]冰下之海中的生物圈的调查。在大海的底层区域，我们发现了几种大型原生物种，它们能产生一种独特的无机分子，具有十分神奇的疗养性质。

如果这种分子能够被成功地大量采集，它将会让我们对最亲爱的活体陈设的医疗看护产生革命性的变化，甚至可能出现产业规模的应用！
anomaly.2512.desc.mach.en:
Lead [Owner.GetScientist] [Root.GetLeaderName] has returned from the expedition that studied the biosphere in the seas beneath the ice mantle of [From.From.GetName]. Several large species native to the lower regions of the global sea have been found to produce a unique, inorganic molecule with immense healing properties.

If this molecule is successfully harvested in large enough quantities, it could revolutionize medical care for our beloved bio-trophies, and may even have industrial applications!

anomaly.2513.desc.zh: 首席[Owner.GetScientist][Root.GetLeaderName]已经完成了对[From.From.GetName]冰层下海洋中丰富生物圈的考察任务。我们的水下探测器已经绘制了地形图，并记录了大部分生命形式。虽然这些数据可能对我们的生物学家有些用处，但除此之外并未发现任何具有特殊应用价值的东西。
anomaly.2513.desc.en: Lead [Owner.GetScientist] [Root.GetLeaderName] has returned from the expedition that studied the rich biosphere in the seas beneath the ice mantle of [From.From.GetName]. Our underwater probes have mapped the terrain and cataloged most of the life forms. Although this data may be of some use to our biologists, no particular discoveries have been made that would have any applications beyond that.

anomaly.2520.a.rean.zh: 我们能让它再次动起来吗？
anomaly.2520.a.rean.en: Can we make it move again?

anomaly.2520.a.term.zh: 我们可能会学到一种新的灭绝方式。
anomaly.2520.a.term.en: We might learn a new method of extermination.

anomaly.2520.desc.zh:
我们先前以为[From.GetName]的南半球地区有一座山脉，其实这是一个巨型外星生物的庞大骨架。

这副骨架已经有三十四亿年的历史了，但我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]认为在这个[From.GetPlanetMoon]的任何历史节点上，[From.GetName]的环境都无法支持这么大体型生命体的生存。[Owner.GetScientistCapital][Root.GetLeaderName]正在准备新的研究计划，进一步探究其中的奥秘。
anomaly.2520.desc.en:
What was previously thought to be assorted mountains in the southern hemisphere of [From.GetName] have been identified as the massive skeletal remains of a single colossal alien life form.

The bones have been dated as 3.4 billion years old, but our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have ruled out that [From.GetName] could have supported life on that scale at any point in the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s history. [Owner.GetScientistCapital] [Root.GetLeaderName] has prepared a special research project to delve further into this mystery.

anomaly.2521.b.evopred.zh: 先吃飞行员还是先吃飞船？
anomaly.2521.b.evopred.en: Do we start by consuming the pilots or the ship?

anomaly.2521.desc.zh: 根据对[From.From.GetName]上巨型骨骼遗骸的分析，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]得出结论：这种生物是被作为某种飞船而使用的。在巨型的骨骼中至少发现了三种不同种群生物的骨骼，我们推断这些骨骼是属于该船船员的。出于未知原因，这艘生物飞船遭受了极为严重的损伤，坠毁在了[From.From.GetName]。虽说我们根本无法理解需要何等水平的生物工程才能“培养”出这样巨大的飞船，但单单对其骨骼的研究就已令我们的科技获得了巨大的进步。
anomaly.2521.desc.en:
After continued studies of the massive skeletal remains found on [From.From.GetName], Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has concluded that the creature served as some kind of organic starship. Much smaller bones from at least three separate species were found within the larger skeleton, and we assume these came from members of the crew.

For unknown reasons, this organic starship suffered catastrophic damage and crash-landed on [From.From.GetName]. While we cannot begin to understand the biological engineering necessary to "grow" a starship like this, the study of these bones alone has substantially advanced our knowledge.

anomaly.2521.desc.bio.zh:
在对[From.From.GetName]上的巨大骨架进行深入研究后，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]肯定了最不可能的可能：这原来是一艘活体舰船。该生物与我们自己的生物舰船拥有一些相似性。

它的结构既熟悉又陌生，令人无比惊奇，仿佛是被截然不同的演化哲学所塑造而成。在其巨大的胸腔中还发现了一些至少属于三种不同物种的小型骨架，暗示它可能曾在体内搭载船员。这种概念令人不太舒服，因为我们自己的生物舰船是共生的，而不是能塞进人的中空船。

其死亡原因尚不清楚，但受到的伤害是灾难性的，它巨大的骨架在坠落星球表面时摔碎了。它的船员或者说什么更高级的引导智能究竟只是与它一同死去，还是其自我无可分割的一部分？

虽然我们可能永远无法完全解开它起源的谜题，但对其遗骸的研究使我们对活体舰船的意义有了更深入的理解。然而，一个令人不安的问题挥之不去：它是被创造出来的……或者它是生来如此？
anomaly.2521.desc.bio.en:
After extensive study of the colossal skeletal remains on [From.From.GetName], Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has confirmed the impossible: this was once a living starship. This creature bore little resemblance to our own biological vessels.

Its structure is bizarre, both familiar and alien, as if shaped by an entirely different evolutionary philosophy. Smaller bones, belonging to at least three distinct species, were found nestled within its massive ribcage, suggesting it once carried a crew inside its very body. A disturbing notion, given that our own ships are symbiotic, not hollow vessels to be inhabited.

The cause of death is unclear, but the damage is catastrophic, its massive frame shattered as it plummeted to the planet's surface. Did its crew die with it, or were they something more - a guiding intelligence, inseparable from the being itself?

Though we may never fully unravel its origins, the study of its remains has advanced our understanding of what it means to be a living ship. And yet, an unsettling question lingers: Was it created... or was it born?

anomaly.2522.b.evopred.zh: 管它来自哪个次元，DNA就是DNA！
anomaly.2522.b.evopred.en: No matter its dimension of origin, DNA is DNA!

anomaly.2522.desc.zh: 我们对[From.From.GetName]上巨型骨骼遗骸进行持续研究后，渐渐搞清了这个生物为何会流落到[From.From.GetPlanetMoon]。在骸骨的尾部，我们侦测到了十分细微的残余能源读数，证明在这个位置曾打开过某种空间传送门。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为，这个生物是从其他空间穿越这道传送门后来到这里，并很快由于[From.From.GetName]严酷环境的侵袭而死亡。它为何来到这里，或是从何而来，都将成为永远的无解之谜。
anomaly.2522.desc.en:
Our continued studies of the massive skeletal remains on [From.From.GetName] have managed to shed some light on how the creature ended up on the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]. There are very faint residual energy readings that indicate some kind of dimensional portal existed briefly towards the rear of the skeleton.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] theorizes that the creature passed through this gateway from another dimension only to quickly perish in the hostile environment of [From.From.GetName]. Why it did this and where it came from are questions that may never be answered.

anomaly.2523.desc.zh: 这堆骸骨再次移动了起来！巨兽高高地越过我们的死灵法师，迈出摇摇晃晃的第一步，接着是第二步，然后是稳当当地一步接一步。它可能没有生前一样数量的腿，或者数目正确的附肢。我们混合使用了实验室培养的肌肉和工艺水平的液压替代装置，现在这只巨兽已经准备在任何战场上支援我们的战斗，想必它足下的大地必将震颤。
anomaly.2523.desc.en: The skeletal remains are moving once more! The behemoth towers above our necromancers as it takes a shaky stride, followed by another, more steady, one. It might not have the same amount of legs it had in life or the correct number of appendages. Using a mix of lab-grown muscles as well as state-of-the-art hydraulic replacements, the Giant is ready to aid us on any battlefield, and the earth below its feet shall tremble.

anomaly.2523.tooltip.zh: 轨道上增加1支骸骨巨兽陆军。
anomaly.2523.tooltip.en: Adds 1 Skeletal Giant Army in orbit.

anomaly.2530.desc.zh: 五千年前的某段时间，[From.GetName]的近地轨道上发生了一次大规模的太空战役。[From.GetPlanetMoon]的一侧地表上到处都是武器打偏留下的打击坑。对[Root.GetName]的扫描显示地表存在一些遗骸。虽然这些破损飞船的保存状况都很差，但历经数千年这些飞船还能留下一些东西就足以证明了它们的设计是非常尖端的。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]正在组织一次考察行动，考察的目的是通过盘查这些古老舰体来寻找一些有价值的科技。
anomaly.2530.desc.en:
There is clear evidence that a massive space battle took place in close orbit of [From.GetName] at some point in the last 5,000 years. The surface on one side of the [From.GetPlanetMoon] is pockmarked with craters from stray weapons blasts, and scans from the [Root.GetName] have picked up several hulks on the ground.

Though these wrecked ships are all in very poor condition, the fact that anything remains at all after the damage they must have sustained is a testament to their advanced design. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is preparing an expedition to sift through these derelict hulls for any valuable technologies.

anomaly.2530.desc.bio.zh:
证据毋庸置疑地证明在过去的5000年内，[From.GetName]的上空曾经发生过一场活体舰船的巨兽之战。[From.GetPlanetMoon]的地表烙印着深深的伤痕——垂死的生物舰船从轨道上坠落，产生巨大的撞击坑，它们残破的外壳在撞击中如过熟的水果一般迸裂。即使到现在，干燥已久的有机残留物和软骨化石仍残留在支离破碎的地面上。

这些雄伟生物的生物结构被岁月扭曲石化，其遗骸几乎无法辨认。然而，经过数千年的腐烂和暴露，竟然还有东西能幸存下来，这已经说明了它们的非凡韧性。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]正准备考察这些巨兽化石，以期能发现它们基因结构或生物工程共生体的残余；这些秘密中可能仍在潜伏着生命的脉搏。
anomaly.2530.desc.bio.en:
There is irrefutable evidence that a titanic battle of living starships once took place in the skies above [From.GetName], sometime in the last 5,000 years. The surface of the [From.GetPlanetMoon] bears deep scars - vast impact craters where dying vessels plummeted from orbit, their ruptured husks bursting like overripe fruit upon collision. Even now, traces of long-dried organic residue and fossilized cartilage linger in the blasted terrain.

The remains of these once-majestic creatures are barely recognizable, their bio-structures twisted and petrified by time. Yet the fact that anything endures at all after millennia of decay and exposure speaks to their remarkable resilience. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is preparing an expedition to examine these fossilized leviathans, hoping to uncover remnants of their genetic architecture or bio-engineered symbiotes; secrets that may still pulse with dormant life.

anomaly.2531.desc.zh: 科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]领导的队伍已完成了对[From.From.GetName]的探索，回到了[Root.GetName]。可喜的是，地表上的飞船墓地中包含着大量的先进科技，可供我们探索。其中包含的科技我们尚未完全发掘完毕，但对这些飞船遗骸的研究已令我们数个领域的科技水平前进了数年之巨。若能在轨道上建立永久的科学站，将对我们的飞船工程水平提供极大的帮助。
anomaly.2531.desc.en:
The team under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has finished their expedition on [From.From.GetName] and returned to the [Root.GetName]. Thankfully, the starship graveyard on the surface proved to be a technological treasure trove.

Studying the remains of these vessels has advanced our research in certain fields by several years, and there are yet things to discover. A permanent science outpost in orbit would be a great boon to our starship engineering efforts.

anomaly.2532.desc.zh: 科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]领导的队伍已完成了对[From.From.GetName]的探索，回到了[Root.GetName]。遗憾的是，地表那些坠毁的飞船损毁过于严重，未能回收任何可用的科技。然而，我们可以明显看出这些飞船极为先进，若对其结构和设计进行分析，它们将会为我们提供宝贵的工程知识。我们应该考虑在此轨道上建造一座永久的科学站。
anomaly.2532.desc.en:
The team under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has finished their expedition on [From.From.GetName] and returned to the [Root.GetName]. Sadly, the wrecked starships on the surface were too badly damaged to recover any useful technologies.

These vessels were clearly very advanced, however, and we could gain valuable engineering insights if we analyze the way they were designed. We should consider the construction of a permanent science outpost in orbit.

anomaly.2532.desc.bio.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]的团队完成了[From.From.GetName]上的悲惨探险现已返回[Root.GetName]。不幸的是，时间对这具古老的有机遗骸并不仁慈。其的结死亡构不是早已石化就是变成易碎的钙化外壳，几乎没有立即修复的价值。

然而，即使已经死亡，它们的设计也超越了我们目前的理解。它们生物工程骨骼的复杂晶格、曾经活跃的肌肉组织的残余，以及远远超出我们自己理解的神经结构的痕迹，都表明其中的复杂技术仍需要进一步研究。在轨道上建立一座永久的研究基地可能是解开这些早已灭绝的庞然大物秘密的关键。
anomaly.2532.desc.bio.en:
The team under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has completed their harrowing expedition on [From.From.GetName] and returned to the [Root.GetName]. Unfortunately, time has not been kind to the remains of these ancient, organic vessels. Their once-living structures have long since fossilized or crumbled into brittle, calcified husks, leaving little of immediate value to recover.

Yet even in death, their design speaks of wonders beyond our current understanding. The intricate lattice of their bio-engineered skeletons, the vestigial remains of once-reactive musculature, and the traces of a neural architecture far beyond our own comprehension, all suggest a level of technological sophistication that demands further study. Establishing a permanent research presence in orbit may be the key to unraveling the secrets of these long-extinct leviathans.

anomaly.2540.desc.zh: 在对[From.GetName]的地表进行扫描时，[Root.GetName]上的[Owner.GetScientistCapital][Root.GetLeaderName]发现了人工雕刻的石板，上面写着外星文字。[From.GetPlanetMoon]上没有侦测到其他的外星活动，这个壁画究竟是如何到这里来的仍然是个谜。我们接下来就准备着手进行破译工作。
anomaly.2540.desc.en: While conducting surface scans of [From.GetName], [Owner.GetScientistCapital] [Root.GetLeaderName] aboard the [Root.GetName] discovered what appears to be an artificially carved slab of rock covered in alien writing. No other signs of alien activity on the [From.GetPlanetMoon] have been detected, and exactly how this mural came to be here is a mystery. We have prepared a special project to translate the text.

anomaly.2541.desc.zh:
[Owner.GetScientistCapital][Root.GetLeaderName]已经部分破译了[From.From.GetName]上发现的外星壁画。它是为了纪念一个曾在本地区建立过一个小型星际帝国的已灭亡外星种族。很明显消灭他们的人就是这幅壁画的作者，他们似乎很后悔这个决定。

鉴于这幅壁画已经有三亿多年的历史了，它的作者很可能也已灭绝。或许最有趣的是这幅壁画的材料——尽管历史久远，但保存的却依然非常完好。
anomaly.2541.desc.en:
[Owner.GetScientistCapital] [Root.GetLeaderName] has managed to partially translate the alien mural discovered on [From.From.GetName]. It is a memorial for an extinct alien race that once maintained a small interstellar empire in this region of the galaxy. They were apparently exterminated by the creators of the mural, a fact that they seem to regret.

Given that the mural has been dated to be in excess of 300 million years old, it is likely that its creators are also extinct by now. Perhaps most interesting of all is the material that the mural was made of - despite its age, it is in remarkably good condition.

anomaly.2542.desc.zh:
[Owner.GetScientistCapital][Root.GetLeaderName]已经部分破译了[From.From.GetName]的外星壁画。其中包含了大量的数据，因此这幅壁画很可能是某种简陋的图书馆。壁画中大致记载了八千万年前统治这片区域的外星文明收集到的所有科技知识。

大多数知识我们已经知晓，但数据中仍有一些非常有启发性的科技信息。这里的数据够科学家研究上几十年的，因此需要设立一个轨道研究设施来继续进行翻译的工作。
anomaly.2542.desc.en:
[Owner.GetScientistCapital] [Root.GetLeaderName] has managed to partially translate the alien mural discovered on [From.From.GetName]. The text contains a staggering amount of data, and the mural evidently serves as some sort of low-tech library. It describes, in broad terms, the collected technological knowledge of an alien civilization that dominated this region of the galaxy some 80 million years ago.

A lot of it is already known to us, but the data does contain several promising leads for technologies we had yet to consider. There is enough data here to keep our scientists busy for decades, but we will need an orbital research facility to continue the translation efforts.

anomaly.255.a.zh: 那我们还是别去找了吧。

anomaly.255.desc.zh:
在[From.GetName]上曾经居住着某个智力较为发达的外星物种，或许再过几十年就能够研发出太空旅行，但在那之前他们就已经把自己终结了。虽然星球本身已经从毫无意义的大肆毁灭中恢复了过来，但表面上仍然有十分明显的伤疤。

地表上残存着几处遗迹，其中有座保存得较为良好的石碑。[Root.GetLeaderName]十分轻松地解读了上面的讯息，原来是世界末日的幸存者们为后来之人所刻下的一则警告。其种族灭亡的直接原因便是“终极武器”的发明。这个种族的某种心理学特征导致共同毁灭机制不再有效。

因为最终武器很难被摧毁，那些最终由于不明原因迅速死去的幸存者们在临死前便将其藏在了地底深处，并留下讯息劝告后人不要去寻找它们。
anomaly.255.desc.en:
[From.GetName] was once home to a race of reasonably intelligent beings who destroyed themselves when they were seemingly only decades away from space flight. The planet has recovered from what must have been immense acts of senseless destruction, but it still bears very visible scars.

One of the few remaining ruins on the surface holds a reasonably well-preserved stone monolith inscribed with a message, quickly decoded by [Root.GetLeaderName]. It is a warning, from the last of the extinct species to whoever they believed would arise after their passing. It was the development of an "ultimate weapon" that was their downfall; some quirk in the psychology of this species evidently rendered deterrence through mutually assured destruction impossible.

Survivors, before dying of unknown causes soon after, hid this weaponry deep underground as destroying them was difficult, and left this message dissuade us from going looking for them.

anomaly.2550.desc.zh:
在对[From.GetName]进行调查时，[Root.GetName]检测到轨道中有一个自动化船坞的残骸。这个船坞至少有一千年的历史了，并且曾经被重型导弹轮番轰炸过，所幸的是其中一个船坞仍可以使用。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]确信能够恢复船坞的电力，但过程会比较复杂。
anomaly.2550.desc.en:
While conducting their survey of [From.GetName], the [Root.GetName] detected the remains of an automated shipyard in orbit. It is at least a thousand years old and seems to have been subjected to a heavy missile barrage, but one of its manufacturing bays is still in working condition.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is confident that power can be restored to the shipyard, but it would be a significant project.

anomaly.2550.desc.bio.zh:
在调查[From.GetName]的过程中，[Root.GetName]有了个惊人的发现：一个古老而凋败的太空孕育摇篮的遗迹；这是一座巨大的有机结构，它曾经可以制造星际飞船。它在寂静中漂流，外膜破裂萎缩，这似乎是在几个世纪前的残酷轰炸中发生的。它的大部分管路组织都石化了，神经网络没有反应……然而，还有一个孕育室仍在微弱地蠕动着，它的反应堆缓慢地跳动着剩余的生命。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]相信，只要小心地介入，我们也许可以复活这个沉睡的生命，至少部分复活。然而，这会是一件颇费时间的工程，不可预见的生物响应风险也不能忽视。
anomaly.2550.desc.bio.en:
While surveying [From.GetName], the [Root.GetName] has made an astonishing discovery: the decayed remains of an ancient, spaceborne gestation cradle; a vast organic structure once capable of birthing starships. It drifts in silence, its outer membranes ruptured and withered from what appears to have been a brutal bombardment, likely centuries ago. Most of its vascular conduits are petrified, its neural lattice unresponsive... and yet, one gestation chamber still stirs faintly, its reactors sluggishly pulsing with residual life.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] believes that, with careful intervention, we may be able to revive this slumbering entity, at least partially. However, it will be a delicate and time-consuming process, and the risk of unforeseen biological responses cannot be ignored.

anomaly.2551.desc.zh:
[Root.GetFleetName]成功恢复了[From.From.From.GetName]上自动化造船厂的电力。船厂很快就恢复了之前被中断的生产程序，使用现有的材料建造了三艘结构未知的掠袭者战舰。

可惜在这之后这个古老的造船厂发生了无法修复的严重故障。因此我们只能选择接管这三艘飞船，让其加入我们的舰队。
anomaly.2551.desc.en:
The [Root.GetFleetName] has successfully restored power to the automated shipyard over [From.From.From.GetName]. The facility immediately resumed its interrupted construction order, using what materials it had on hand to build three advanced raiders of an unknown design.

Unfortunately, the ancient facility broke down completely afterwards and has been deemed beyond repair. We have sent crews to the new ships and commissioned them into our fleet.

anomaly.2551.desc.bio.zh:
[Root.GetFleetName]成功复苏了围绕着[From.From.From.GetName]的休眠摇篮。常年闲置的生物锻造器突然复苏使这个古老的有机结构颤抖起来，它匆忙地完成了三头战兽的生长周期，它们的设计都是未知的，但却异常复杂。

然而，这种意想不到的重生对这个衰老的有机体来说，压力太大了。它的维管崩溃，神经中枢枯萎，溶解成惰性的生物质。新组建的舰队虽然一开始迷失了方向，但很快便适应了我们的存在。它们被整合进我们的舰队，迫不及待地为新的共生主体建功立业了。
anomaly.2551.desc.bio.en:
The [Root.GetFleetName] has successfully reawakened the dormant cradle orbiting [From.From.From.GetName]. The ancient, organic structure trembled as its long-idle bio-forges surged to life, hastily completing the growth cycle of three warforms, each an unknown yet eerily sophisticated design.

However, the strain of this unexpected rebirth proved too much for the aged organism. Its vascular conduits collapsed, its neural core withered, and it dissolved into inert biomass. The newly formed ships, though disoriented at first, quickly adapted to our presence. They have been integrated into our fleet, eager to serve their new symbiotic masters.

anomaly.2552.desc.zh:
[Root.GetFleetName]成功恢复了[From.From.From.GetName]上自动化造船厂的电力。船厂很快就恢复了之前被中断的生产程序，使用现有的材料建造了一艘结构未知的炮艇。

可惜在这之后这个古老的造船厂发生了无法修复的严重故障。因此我们只能选择接管这艘飞船，让其加入我们的舰队。
anomaly.2552.desc.en:
The [Root.GetFleetName] has successfully restored power to the automated shipyard over [From.From.From.GetName]. The facility immediately resumed its interrupted construction order, using what materials it had on hand to build an advanced frigate of unknown design.

Unfortunately, the ancient facility broke down completely afterwards and has been deemed beyond repair. We have sent a crew to the new ship and pressed it into service with our fleet.

anomaly.256.b.zh: 对于[Root.Owner.GetName]来说，都没什么用处。
anomaly.256.b.en: None of this is of any use to the [Root.Owner.GetName].

anomaly.256.desc.zh:
看起来这颗星球上的“最终武器”只不过是我们眼中最为基本的武器科技而已。

他们能运用这些科技导致世界末日，或许只是因为十分爱好杀戮而已吧。
anomaly.256.desc.en:
It seems the people of this planet were experimenting only with what we would consider to be fairly basic weapons technologies.

The havoc they wrought is more a testament to their incredible, genocidal tenacity than it is to the power of their weaponry.

anomaly.2560.a.en: Bring it up, whatever it is.

anomaly.2560.b.en: The effort is too great. Leave it down there.

anomaly.2560.desc.zh: 对[From.GetName]的深度扫描显示这颗气态巨行星的大气层中有一艘大型飞船。根据附近的碎片看，过去曾经有人试图回收它，但都失败了。任何足以抵挡如此强大引力的飞船都是非常珍贵的。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]提出了自己的回收计划。
anomaly.2560.desc.en: Active scans of [From.GetName] have picked up what appears to be a large ship deep inside the atmosphere of the gas giant. Judging by the nearby debris, there have been several failed attempts to salvage this derelict in the past. Any ship strong enough to withstand such crushing gravity must be a magnificent prize, and Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has proposed a salvage project of our own.

anomaly.2561.desc.zh: 运用无与伦比的大师级工程技术，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]和他的小队成功将[From.From.GetName]上被遗弃的飞船升到了高层大气中。尽管年久失修，这个古老的巡洋舰依然比较完好，系统在供能之后依然运转正常。不清楚原有的船员下落如何，但我们依然派遣了新的船员，并让其加入了我们的舰队。
anomaly.2561.desc.en: In a masterful display of engineering, the team under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has managed to gently raise the derelict ship on [From.From.GetName] to the gas giant's upper atmosphere. Despite its age, the ancient cruiser is in remarkably good condition and we have restored power to its systems. No trace of the original crew remains, but we have brought over our own and commissioned the ship into the fleet.

anomaly.2562.desc.zh: 科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]试图将[From.From.GetName]大气层中的飞船回收的计划失败了。星球的强引力使得我们的一艘工程拖船引擎熄火，并与这艘被遗弃的飞船撞在了一起。几个人因此丧命，那艘飞船也进而被拖进了大气层的深处-我们对此无能为力了。
anomaly.2562.desc.en: The attempt by Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] to salvage the derelict ship from the atmosphere of [From.From.GetName] was a failure. The gas giant's heavy gravity disabled the engines of one of our engineering tugs, which then collided with the derelict. Several lives were lost, and the ancient vessel was pushed even deeper into the atmosphere - beyond our reach.

anomaly.257.a.zh: 什么？我们已经有这些科技了。
anomaly.257.a.en: What? We already possess this technology.

anomaly.257.c.zh: 升级我们的质量投射器。

anomaly.257.desc.zh: 科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为幸存者们隐藏武器的决定十分正确。在地底洞穴中找到的这些武器虽然与[Root.Owner.GetName]的现役装备原理相同，但更为先进。这些科技一定会对[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]战争机器大有帮助。
anomaly.257.desc.en: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] remarks that the previous inhabitants of this place were right to hide these weapons, recovered from a cave beneath the ruins, away. They build on the same basic principles as weapons already in use in the [Root.Owner.GetName], but are far more advanced. These technologies are sure to be a boon to the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] military machine.

anomaly.2570.desc.zh: 环绕[From.GetName]的众多卫星之一有一个终结轨道。它即将与气态巨行星相撞，这无疑会造成极大的破坏。这将是数百万年一遇的奇观，更巧合的是，这次撞击恰好在我们的一艘飞船拜访那里之后发生。许多科学家都想亲临现场观测和记录这次事件，但这样的碰撞转瞬即逝，因此留给我们的时间并不多。
anomaly.2570.desc.en:
One of the many moons circling [From.GetName] has a terminal orbit. It will soon collide with the gas giant in what is sure to become a massive impact event. This event has been millions of years in the making, and it is a startling coincidence that the impact has been fated to occur just after a visit by one of our ships.

Many of our scientists wish to observe and record the event, but we only have a narrow window before it is too late.

anomaly.2571.desc.zh: 我们成功的从不同角度记录了[CollisionLocation.GetName]和卫星相撞的奇观，并且对区域内的所有观众进行了现场直播。更重要的是，我们的科学家在[Root.GetLeaderName]的带领下记录了大量珍贵的物理数据，这对研究毫无疑问是有帮助的。
anomaly.2571.desc.en: We were successful in our attempt to record the collision between [CollisionLocation.GetName] and its moon! The event was captured from several different angles, and transmitted live throughout our space. Most importantly, our scientists under the leadership of [Root.GetLeaderName] were able to record a large amount of valuable physics data that will surely benefit our research.

anomaly.2575.a.zh: 总有一天它能被再度唤醒。
anomaly.2575.a.en: In time, perhaps we can reawaken it.

anomaly.2575.desc.1.zh:
$anomaly.2575.desc.intro$

对[From.GetPlanetMoon]环境改造理论上是可行的，但我们目前所拥有的科技并不足以在切合实际的时间内完成这一壮举。
anomaly.2575.desc.1.en:
$anomaly.2575.desc.intro$

Terraforming this [From.GetPlanetMoon] would theoretically be possible, but we do not yet possess the technology to accomplish this monumental task within a realistic timeframe.

anomaly.2575.desc.2.zh:
$anomaly.2575.desc.intro$

能量花费将令人生畏，但我们拥有将[From.GetPlanetMoon]逐渐环境改造成再次能维持生命的状态所必须的科技。
anomaly.2575.desc.2.en:
$anomaly.2575.desc.intro$

The energy costs would be daunting, but we do have the technology to gradually terraform this [From.GetPlanetMoon] into something that would support life once again.

anomaly.2575.desc.3.zh:
$anomaly.2575.desc.intro$

很不幸，这一恒星系中的戴森球使得恢复行星环境不再可能。
anomaly.2575.desc.3.en:
$anomaly.2575.desc.intro$

Unfortunately the Dyson Sphere in this system has removed any possibility of restoring the planet.

anomaly.2576.desc.zh:
对[From.GetName]的表面细致勘探后我们发现了一个巨大撞击坑，其中散步着一些来历不明的古代舰船残骸碎片。这些舰船中似乎完全没有装配生命支持系统，我们推测它们可能是一些巨型无人机或者由某种人工智能操控。

这些舰船的船体材料颇为有趣，是由活性金属这种极其稀有的无机材料构造而成。这种材料属性多样而独特，可以被“编码”成特定形状，在受到损伤时，能够缓慢地自我修复。数千年过去，舰船上的活性金属逐渐熔化，形成了巨大、致密的矿脉，可供我们采集数个世纪。
anomaly.2576.desc.en:
Detailed surface scans of [From.GetName] have identified a large impact crater containing the wreckage of several ancient starships of unknown design. The ships appear to be completely devoid of life support systems, leading us to suspect that they were either unusually large drones or controlled by some form of artificial intelligence.

Interestingly, the hull of the ships was constructed out of Living Metal, an exceedingly rare and inorganic material with many unique properties. This metal can be "programmed" to assume a certain shape or form, and it will slowly regrow itself if damaged. Over a period of several millennia, the surviving metal from the wrecked ships was fused into a large and extremely dense deposit that could potentially be mined for centuries to come.

anomaly.258.desc.zh: 搜查无果。不管是怎样强大的武器，现在都没了。
anomaly.258.desc.en: The search proves fruitless. Whatever these mystical weapons were, they are now gone.

anomaly.2580.desc.zh:
我们的科学家在调查[From.GetName]上的早先文明的过程中，发现了一个神秘的小机器人试图隐藏自己。在对这个小东西经过数周的接近和示好之后，它终于将我们的科学家们带回到一个自它的创造者离去后起就由它照看的还在运作中的工厂。

被带到这座建筑之后，我们的人获赠了一大批可以带回飞船上的资源。尽管稀奇古怪难以沟通，但这个小机器人似乎把我们的科学家当成了自己的朋友。
anomaly.2580.desc.en:
As our scientists were looking into the earlier civilization on [From.GetName], they came across a small enigmatic robot trying to hide from them. Following weeks of approaching and befriending the little thing, it finally brought them back to a still-functional factory that it has been supervising since the demise of its creators.

After being guided to the building, our people were given a large quantity of resources they could bring back to their ship. Though weird and hard to communicate with, the little robot seems to think of our scientists as its friends.

anomaly.260.desc.zh:
[Root.GetName]在[From.GetName]上发现了全星球仅有一座的外星建筑。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为星球上所有的其它建筑都因为某种原因被移到了别处，但不知为何只留下这么一座建筑。

这建筑乃是处理星球上丰富矿脉的加工厂，经过[Root.GetName]初步勘测后，认定可以十分轻松地重新运作。
anomaly.260.desc.en:
The [Root.GetName] has found an alien structure on [From.GetName]. It seems to be the only one of its kind on the planet - Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] speculates that all other xenoarchitectural traces may have been moved off-world, with this sole building left behind for reasons unknown.

It is a processing plant working the planet's abundant mineral resources, and preliminary scans by the [Root.GetName] indicate that it can be reactivated with relative ease.

anomaly.265.a.tooltip.en:
Adds the Skid Marks modifier to [From.GetName]:
£engineering£ +6

anomaly.265.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]浅层松软表面上的坑洞中有着不规则的长条印记。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]在印记的附近发现了十分令人惊讶的各种废品：被撞毁的轮式载具。它们看起来并不像是科研用品，而是载人用的。

[Root.GetName]的船员们认为这里应该是外星人用作赛车的地点。在这几乎零重力的地方，外星生物们驾着自己车辆互相对抗，测试车辆的强度与速度，真是激动人心。
anomaly.265.desc.en:
The crater on [From.GetName] exhibits long, irregular marks imprinted into the relatively soft upper layers of the asteroid. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has recovered some interesting unexpected wreckage from the edges of the depression; wheeled vehicles, seemingly personal transports rather than research craft.

The crew of the [Root.GetName] speculate that the crater may once have been used for sport, with some alien species pitting their personal locomotion devices against each other in tests of mechanical strength or speed in near-zero-G.

anomaly.270.a.tooltip.en:
Adds the Circuits in the Dust modifier to [From.GetName]:
£engineering£ +3

anomaly.270.desc.zh:
虽然此处的陨石坑应该只是普通的陨石撞击造成的，但陨石坑中复杂的纹路应该是产生于撞击之后。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这些地表的印记应该不是陨石造成的，而是小行星[From.GetName]与某种未知的轨道设施或外星飞船之类的东西撞击后造成的。
anomaly.270.desc.en:
While the crater in question was most likely the result of a regular meteorite impact, the complex patterns in the resulting depression originated at a later time.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] argues that these surface-level patterns are not the result of an impact but a collision, one between asteroid [From.GetName] and some unspecified orbital installation or ship of alien make.

anomaly.275.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]的其中一个大坑中心有外星工艺制造的金属机械。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这些大型机械是用于推动整颗星球的。其目的便是将[From.GetName]从原先轨道中推出，但目的地不明。[Root.GetName]正在待命，可以将这些推动装置进行拆卸与分析，或许可以提升我方的推进科技。
anomaly.275.desc.en:
In the center of a particularly large crater on [From.GetName] lies a cluster of metal shapes, doubtlessly of alien origin.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is convinced that they are massive, planetoid-mountable propulsion devices, intended to push [From.GetName] from its orbit for purposes and destinations unknown. The [Root.GetName] is on standby, its crew ready to begin disassembly and analysis of the alleged propulsion systems with the hopes of improving our own thruster technology.

anomaly.285.a.tooltip.en:
Adds the Unusual Tectonics modifier to [From.GetName]:
£engineering£ +2
£physics£ +2

anomaly.285.desc.zh:
[Root.GetName]在[From.GetName]上找到的并非是建筑，而是十分普通的矿物岩层。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这些岩层之所以会露出地面，是因为不同的地壳构造版块互相撞击而形成的，其形状的特殊性是由行星地壳中不同寻常的物理构造造成的。

因为其形状过于工整，看起来某种外星生物似乎曾经对[From.GetName]的地壳进行过改动。
anomaly.285.desc.en:
What the [Root.GetName] found on [From.GetName] were not buildings, but surprisingly regular mineral outcroppings. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] asserts that these angular blocks of rock are the product of interactions between tectonic plates, their shapes the result of the unusual tectonophysics inherent in the planet's crust.

The perfect angularity of these thrust faults implies a possibility of aliens tampering with [From.GetName]'s crust at some point in the past.

anomaly.290.b.en: Very well, ready the positron charges.

anomaly.290.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]的矿脉资源十分丰富。

不幸的是，其中大部分矿石对我们都没用。然而，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为[From.GetName]地壳中的许多元素都可以通过正电子轰炸转化成对我方有用的矿石。

[Root.GetName]希望[Root.Owner.GetName]能拨出1000能量币实行此计划。
anomaly.290.desc.en:
[From.GetName] is exceptionally rich in minerals.

Minerals that are, unfortunately, of no use to us. However, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] believes the many elements in the crust of [From.GetName] can be transformed into potentially more useful forms through positron bombardment.

The [Root.GetName] has requests that the [Root.Owner.GetName] set aside 1000 Energy Credits for the purposes of this project.

anomaly.292.desc.zh: [Root.GetName]的船员们汇报了试验的成功。[From.From.GetName]上的许多矿脉现在都可以被我们所使用了。
anomaly.292.desc.en: The crew of the [Root.GetName] are pleased to report that the experiment was a success, and a significant number of dense mineral veins on [From.From.GetName] have been transmuted into usable resources.

anomaly.295.desc.zh:
[Root.GetName]穿过小行星带前往[From.GetName]的路上时，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]汇报飞船经历了几次来势突然的重力变化。因为好奇，[Root.GetLeaderName]派遣了无人机前去勘测原因。

结果，无人机发现了几只老旧的外星重力生成器。因为极性反转，电池又不足，这些重力生成器时常会对着虚空放射出反重力波。但其效果不强，无法造成任何实质性的伤害。我们无法将生成器的效果恢复至其原本具有的强度。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这些生成器本来是为小行星带中某颗较大的小行星提供人造重力用的，但因为某种故障，这颗小行星已经四分五裂了。
anomaly.295.desc.en:
As the [Root.GetName] passed through the asteroid belt on its way to [From.GetName], Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reported that the ship experienced a number of sudden gravitational shifts. Ever curious, [Root.GetLeaderName] dispatched a number of probes to scan the debris field to discern the cause.

It turns out that the culprit is a number of gravity generators of old, alien make. Sputtering on dying energy sources and with their polarities inverted, they occasionally spew reverse-gravity into the void, though not with enough force to cause any serious harm. Not anymore.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] theorizes that the generators once provided artificial gravity for a large asteroid in the belt, but some malfunction eventually tore the rock apart.

anomaly.30.a.zh: 回收一切可以回收的东西。
anomaly.30.a.en: We should recycle what we can.

anomaly.30.desc.zh: 在遥远的过去，这颗小行星显然被某些人在某段时间当成了垃圾场。各种各样的报废器械和金属废料都被小行星的低重力捕获，被缓缓地拉到一大堆残骸碎石之中，现在这些残骸碎石已经覆盖了小行星的表面。在这里我们没有发现什么有价值的东西，但许多金属可以用开采站回收。
anomaly.30.desc.en: This asteroid was evidently used as a junkyard by someone at some point in the distant past. All manner of discarded machinery and metallic refuse has been deposited inside the asteroid's weak gravity well, being slowly pulled into the jumble of debris that now covers the surface. There is nothing of particular value to be found here, but a lot of the metal could be salvaged by a mining station.

anomaly.300.desc.zh: 我们在气态巨行星[From.GetName]的上层大气中发现了一个生机勃勃的生态系统。巨大的漂浮生物已经进化出密度轻于空气的身体，可以随风而动，并从气态巨行星频繁的雷暴中摄取能源。这些生物也养活了浮游生物以及猎食浮游生物的小型动物，这些小型动物也互相为食。
anomaly.300.desc.en: We have discovered a thriving ecosystem in the upper atmosphere of the gas giant [From.GetName]. Massive floating creatures, having evolved bodies filled with lighter than air gases, follow the wind currents and feed off the energy released by the gas giant's frequent lightning storms. These beings in turn support colonies of smaller animals that prey on atmospheric plankton and each other.

anomaly.3000.a.zh: 碎了的矿石也还是矿石。
anomaly.3000.a.en: Its parts are equal to the sum of its parts.

anomaly.3000.desc.zh:
据[Root.GetName]的船员汇报，他们的任务失败了。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]心血来潮想手动操纵无人机采集矿石样本，结果不小心撞上了矿石，虽然撞击力度并不大，但矿石还是粉碎殆尽了。

船员还提到，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]对此十分内疚，并且那些粉碎的矿石还有些价值。
anomaly.3000.desc.en:
According to a report from the crew of the [Root.GetName], their mission was a failure. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] allegedly took manual control of the probe sent to retrieve a sample from the cluster, resulting in a collision between drone and mineral cluster that, while mild, resulted in the mineral cluster breaking apart completely.

The crew is careful to note that the experience has left Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] somewhat shaken, and the mineral shards should still be of some value.

anomaly.3005.desc.zh:
这块矿物的构造就像是个房间，没有其他更贴切的词能形容了。

构成房间的矿物在[Root.Owner.GetName]十分常用。这块矿石是中空的三十二面体，磁共振扫描显示其内部中空，很可能曾有人居住过。但是矿石内部与其光鲜的外表并不相同，看起来被人破坏的混乱不堪。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]报告称由于这些破坏，我们很难从矿石内部找到有价值的信息。但其建筑的外部结构能够抵御深空压力，其构造技术一定十分先进。
anomaly.3005.desc.en:
The mineral construct is, for lack of a better term, a room.

Made out of the same type of minerals in common use in the [Root.Owner.GetName], the construct is a hollow icosidodecahedron. Resonance scans indicate that it is mostly hollow, and was likely inhabited at some point in time. Unlike its pristine exterior, the interior is in complete disarray, possibly the result of an intentional act of sabotage.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that this makes it difficult to learn anything of value from the construct's insides, but stresses that the engineering techniques involved in creating the outer shell, eminently capable of withstanding the stresses of deep space, must have been tremendously advanced.

anomaly.3010.a.en: Nothing good would come of it.

anomaly.3010.desc.zh:
这块矿石是个全息记录仪，外表棱角分明，呈半透明状。其目前被安全地放置于[Root.GetName]的牵引光束中，但解码其内容仍需假以时日。

已经设立加速该进程的特殊项目。
anomaly.3010.desc.en:
The mineral cluster is a holographic record, multi-sided, many-edged, and translucent. It remains secure in the [Root.GetName]'s tractor beam, but our experts will need some time to decode its contents.

A Special Project has been issued to expedite this process.

anomaly.3012.desc.zh: 全息记录仪中的数据文档乃是一份曾经称霸此区域的三个大国之间的贸易协议。其中的内容我们无法理解也毫无意义，但科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为这可以大大提高我们与外星人的沟通能力。
anomaly.3012.desc.en: The holographic data documents the terms and conditions for a trilateral trade treaty between three major alien powers that once dominated this quadrant of the galaxy. Context eludes us and the details are meaningless, but Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] feels that this find will prove invaluable to improving our own ability to communicate with alien forces.

anomaly.3015.b.pacifist.zh: 既然已经化为废墟，那就不要多管了。
anomaly.3015.b.pacifist.en: That this outpost is dead and buried speaks volumes.

anomaly.3015.desc.zh:
轨道上探查出的影像的确是建筑。进一步调查后发现建筑显然是用于军事用途。虽然被遗弃了一段时间——从星系尺度上看并不算久——但科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为从尘土下的废弃军营和空旷的军火库中仍然可以找到外星战术秘密。

已经设立了研究废墟的特殊项目。
anomaly.3015.desc.en:
The silhouettes discernible from orbit are indeed buildings, and closer inspection reveal them to be of an obvious martial nature. While abandoned for some time - though very recently on a galactic timescale - Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] believes that secrets of alien tactics may yet be exhumed from beneath the dust that covers the decaying barracks and looted armories.

A Special Project may be issued to study the remains.

anomaly.3017.desc.zh:
科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]对于[From.From.GetName]进行了详尽的外星历史分析，但最终结果不佳。该兵营早在行星变得贫瘠之前就被建立了，但不知是因为自然原因还是战争原因，才变成了今天这样的废墟。

可以得出的结论是：这些外星人使用的武器与战略并不比我们现在使用的要先进。

不过，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]说自己因为这次勘探，获取了不少灵感。
anomaly.3017.desc.en:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName]'s thorough xeno-historical analysis of the military installation on [From.From.GetName] has yielded few tangible results. The base was constructed before the planet turned completely barren, but it is unclear if its current inhospitality is the result of armed conflict or some more peaceful or even natural process.

What can be deduced of their strategies and tactics in armed conflict does not seem to have been far in advance of our own.

On the upside, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] claims to have drawn much inspiration from the alien remnants.

anomaly.3020.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]的特殊拓扑结构整齐地将星球划分为无数个不同的群落，各群落的气候以一种微妙的方式维持着周边环境的平衡。科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]强烈怀疑这是先进的环境改造的结果，但我们无法解释这是如何做到的。

尽管如此，环境改造的结果对[Root.GetLeaderName]和[Root.GetName]的船员来说显而易见。
anomaly.3020.desc.en:
The unique topology of [From.GetName] neatly divides the planet into innumerable distinct biomes, micro-climates that interact only in subtle ways seemingly engineered to sustain neighboring climes. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] strongly suspects advanced terraforming techniques at work, but few clues remain regarding the process itself.

Its effects, however, remain plainly visible to [Root.GetLeaderName] and the [Root.GetName]'s crew.

anomaly.3025.desc.zh:
我们在[From.GetName]一处植被非常茂密的地域的中心发现了被植物掩盖的外星建筑，起初我们以为它已被摧毁，但经过[Root.GetName]仔细勘察发现，它还没有被这颗星球上格外茂盛的植物所侵蚀。

已发起特殊项目来寻找建筑入口。
anomaly.3025.desc.en:
One of the major areas of extreme verdancy on [From.GetName] is centered on an overgrown alien structure. Initially thought ruined, closer observations by the [Root.GetName] reveal that the building has mostly survived the crushing embrace of the planet's flora.

A Special Project has been issued to find a way into the structure.

anomaly.3027.desc.zh:
这座杂草丛生的建筑是外星人的矿物加工厂。位于[From.From.GetName]的工厂尽管早已被废弃，但似乎曾基本实现了自动化，工厂的地上还躺着大量全自动机器人的残骸——他们的身体主要由有机化合物组成，体内以高分子内骨骼作为支撑，现在也一并腐烂了。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]认为正是这些有机残余物在液化后渗入了地面，使得土壤变得肥沃，星球上的各种植物也才会如此繁茂坚韧。

工厂可以被重新激活，但是[Root.GetLeaderName]感兴趣的那些迷人的，全自动的工人们却再也不能活过来了。
anomaly.3027.desc.en:
The overgrown structure - an alien mineral processing plant - on [From.From.GetName] was, prior to its abandonment in the distant past, mostly automated. Husks of artificial workers litter the floor, their organic components - for their bodies were largely of a biological nature, held upright by polymer endoskeletons - long since rotted away.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] speculates that it is the organic remains of these automatons that, soon liquefied and drained into the ground, provided an intense boost to soil nutrition and allowed the native flora to grow both abundant and resilient.

The plant can be reactivated but the automatons, fascinating as they may be to [Root.GetLeaderName], will never walk its halls again.

anomaly.3030.a.en: No one will miss it, surely.

anomaly.3030.b.phobe.zh: 我们既不知道这是哪儿来的，也不知道这玩意要到哪儿去。拆掉吧。
anomaly.3030.b.phobe.en: We don't know whence it came or where it is going. Dismantle it.

anomaly.3030.desc.zh:
在[From.GetName]的平原发现了一艘无人船只，其传感器对星球轨道上的[Root.GetName]做出了回应。

[Root.GetName]的船员未能确认此船何时被弃，也不知道此船是何人所弃。至于原船员的下落更是无从调查。根据科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]所说，若想将其收编入我方舰队，远程激活这艘轻装飞船应该不成问题。
anomaly.3030.desc.en:
There is a ship idling on the plains of [From.GetName], its sensors reacting to the [Root.GetName] in orbit around the planet.

The [Root.GetName]'s crew have been unable to confirm exactly when the craft was abandoned - for it is abandoned - or who left it there, or where they are now. According to Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName], remotely activating the lightly armed ship would be trivial, should we wish to add it to our fleets.

anomaly.3035.desc.carefree.zh:
事实证明，荒芜的[From.GetPlanetMoon][From.GetName]毫无有趣之处。

当船员们监视着了无动静的仪器时，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]闲来无事查看了[Root.GetName]的能源储备情况。根据他们的报告，[Root.GetName]上次离港时获得的能量补给少于标准量，不过更有可能是[Root.GetLeaderName]对于资源管理的松懈造成了此次窘境。

不管怎么说，这艘船需要更多的能量作为补给。
anomaly.3035.desc.carefree.en:
The desert [From.GetPlanetMoon] [From.GetName] turned out to be rather unremarkable.

While the crew monitored silent instruments, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] was idly eyeing the [Root.GetName]'s energy reserves. According to their report the [Root.GetName] was issued less than the standard amount of energy when it last left port, but is more likely that [Root.GetLeaderName]'s carefree approach to resource management is to blame for the deficit.

Regardless, the ship does need additional Energy Credits.

anomaly.3035.desc.meticulous.zh:
事实证明，荒芜的[From.GetPlanetMoon][From.GetName]毫无有趣之处。

当船员们监视着了无动静的仪器时，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]对[Root.GetName]的能源储备进行了认真盘点。根据他们的报告，[Root.GetName]上次离港时获得的能量补给多于标准量，这很可能是书写错误造成的。

[Root.Leader.GetName]已提出要自愿将多余的能量交还给[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]当局。
anomaly.3035.desc.meticulous.en:
The desert [From.GetPlanetMoon] [From.GetName] turned out to be rather unremarkable.

While the crew monitored silent instruments, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] was conscientiously taking inventory of the [Root.GetName]'s energy reserves. According to their report the [Root.GetName] was issued more than the standard amount of energy when it last left port, probably due to some clerical error.

[Root.Leader.GetName] has volunteered to return the excess to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] authorities.

anomaly.3040.b.zh: 我们不需要他们的帮忙。把他们的东西都没收，只留他们一条命吧。
anomaly.3040.b.en: We do not need their services. Take what they have but their lives.

anomaly.3040.c.zh: [Root.Owner.GetName]不能容忍他们这种家伙存在。
anomaly.3040.c.en: The [Root.Owner.GetName] will not suffer the existence of their kind.

anomaly.3040.d.zh: 我们必须拒绝他们的避难请求。
anomaly.3040.d.en: We must deny their asylum claim.

anomaly.3040.desc.zh:
我们误以为是矿物簇的物体实际上是两艘外星护卫舰的金属外壳，它们正悄悄飘过小行星带。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]已经与其建立联系，这两艘船的船员自称他们以前都是海盗，现在被首领放逐了。他们听说[Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle][Root.Owner.GetRulerName]是[Root.Owner.GetName]的统治者，为人亲民，特来寻求庇护。
anomaly.3040.desc.en:
What was thought to be a cluster of minerals are the metal hulls of two alien corvettes, stealthily drifting through the asteroid belt.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] established contact, and the two ships are crewed by alleged former pirates, now cast out from their robber-clan. They have heard whispers that [Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle] [Root.Owner.GetRulerName] of the [Root.Owner.GetName] is a champion of the people, and seek asylum.

anomaly.3040.desc.fallback.zh:
我们误以为是矿脉的物体实际上是两艘外星护卫舰的金属外壳，它们正悄悄飘过小行星带。

科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]已经与其建立联系，这两艘船的船员自称他们以前都是海盗，现在被匪帮首领放逐了。很神奇的是，他们相信我们会妥善对待他们，因此特来寻求庇护。
anomaly.3040.desc.fallback.en:
What was thought to be a cluster of minerals are the metal hulls of two alien corvettes, stealthily drifting through the asteroid belt.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] established contact, and the two ships are crewed by alleged former pirates, now cast out from their robber-clan. Curiously, they believe that we will be well-disposed towards them, and are seeking asylum.

anomaly.305.desc.zh: 一艘货舱早已被遗弃在[From.GetName]的大气层上部。不知为何，这个货舱没有被其他的太空远行者发现。其轨道正在逐渐降低，预计将在几年后在气态巨行星的大气中消磨殆尽。当[Root.GetName]的船员们打开货舱后，他们发现了一大堆贵金属制作的外星珠宝。
anomaly.305.desc.en: A discarded cargo pod was left by someone in the upper atmosphere of [From.GetName] long ago. It has somehow escaped the notice of other spacefarers, and its decaying orbit means it would have been lost in the gas giant's crushing atmosphere within another few years.
