We have received word from one of our foremost psychics. Apparently, after learning of the presence in the $NAME_Hillos$ system, they took it upon themselves to make contact with the psionic consciousness in possession of the ghost ship $NAME_Hillos_ship$. After months of painful trials, they have finally succeeded in making contact.

Possessing only a rudimentary vocabulary, the synthetic lifeform was nevertheless able to express itself through feelings and impressions. The 'child's' loneliness was palpable, as was its joy in finally making contact with a mind like itself. It is now playfully gliding throughout the $NAME_Hillos$ system, chattering psionically away to anyone who cares to listen.

anomaly.6795.desc.hive_robot.zh:
在数月的后续研究后，我们的[Root.GetTelepathPlural]成功地接触了占据着$NAME_Hillos_ship$舰船的灵能意识。

尽管它的词汇量非常稀少，但这个合成生命体在与其他灵能意识接触时，可以表达出我们通常所认为的“快乐”。由于其目前没有表现出任何可见的威胁，我们就继续留它在$NAME_Hillos$恒星系里的那台装置内了。
anomaly.6795.desc.hive_robot.en:
After months of continued study, our [Root.GetTelepathPlural] have successfully made contact with the psionic consciousness in possession of the ship $NAME_Hillos_ship$.

Despite possessing only a rudimentary vocabulary, the synthetic lifeform was able to express what we commonly recognize as 'joy' at making contact with another psionic mind. As it currently poses no discernable threat, we have left it to its own devices in the $NAME_Hillos$ system.

anomaly.680.desc.zh: 24000年之前，星系之中的一颗坍缩恒星发出的伽玛射线暴直接照射到了[From.GetName]星球表面。[From.GetPlanetMoon]被致命辐射覆盖，不仅面向射线的[From.GetName]大多数生命形态都被辐射感染，同时大部分的臭氧层也被破坏。这次大灭绝使星球大概86%的生物消失，包括早期青铜时代的文明，他们的遗迹至今仍然存在于北半球的一些地区。目前当地的生物圈有了一些恢复的迹象。
anomaly.680.desc.en:
24,000 years ago [From.GetName] had the misfortune of being directly in the path of a long gamma-ray burst from a collapsing star within our galaxy. The [From.GetPlanetMoon] was washed with lethal radiation, which not only produced acute radiation poisoning in most life forms on the side of [From.GetName] that happened to be facing the burst, but also depleted much of the ozone layer.

This extinction event killed off an estimated 86% of all biota, including an early Bronze Age civilization whose ruins can still be found in some parts of the northern hemisphere. The biosphere is only now showing signs of recovery.

anomaly.6800.b.zh: 我们不会浪费那些合金的。

anomaly.6800.desc.zh: 我们的传感器发现了[From.GetName]上的舰船残骸是通过某种罕见的方式抵达那里的。这些舰船似乎是从大约数光年以外故意地径直开向小行星，用以测试设计者推进器的精确度。在对残骸进行深度扫描时，我们找到了那么一艘推进装置相当完好无损的舰船。
anomaly.6800.desc.en: Our sensors have discovered that the ship remnants on [From.GetName] got there in a peculiar way. The ships seem to have been intentionally driven straight into the asteroid, probably from light-years away, to test the accuracy of the designers' thrusters. As we deep-scan the remains, we pick out one ship in particular, which seems to have reasonably intact propulsion.

anomaly.6805.desc.zh: 我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]期望在[From.GetName]内部发现稀有资源，结果偶然撞见了一样极其不寻常的东西。这个看起来像是普通小行星的物体事实上是一个长期休眠的中继站，里面有复杂的电子元件和先进的传感器，用以向某个古老的帝国发送信号。这些撞击也损毁了小行星的一部分内部构造，我们只能从中提取到一个恒星系。
anomaly.6805.desc.en: Hoping to discover rare resources inside [From.GetName], our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] stumbled upon something most unusual. What had appeared to be a simple asteroid was in fact a long-dormant relay station with complex electronics and advanced sensors set up to send signals back to an ancient empire. The impact also has damaged some of the asteroid's internal structure, and we can only extract one system from it.

anomaly.6810.a.zh: 送客，巨大的外星节肢动物可不是闹着玩的！
anomaly.6810.a.en: Send an away party, giant alien arthropoids are no joke!

anomaly.6810.b.zh: 也许我们最好还是不要打扰他们。
anomaly.6810.b.en: It's probably for the best that we leave them alone.

anomaly.6810.c.zh: 尝试与这些节肢动物小伙伴联络。
anomaly.6810.c.en: Attempt to contact our fellow arthropoids.

anomaly.6810.d.tooltip.zh: 用我们对居住站的先进知识让空间站的大气层裂一个口子。
anomaly.6810.d.tooltip.en: Use our advance knowledge of habitats to breach the station's atmosphere.

anomaly.6810.desc.zh: 我们错了。这座围绕[From.GetName]的空间站并非无人居住；相反，它上面爬满了巨大的外星节肢动物！我们部署进空间站的传感器在信号中断前只回传了一些行动迅捷的阴影和巨大颚骨的画面。在对空间站进行深度扫描后，我们发现了一处可能是无比复杂的数据库的地方。为了抵达这座数据库，我们需要穿过这些一团团的、有好多腿儿的守护者。
anomaly.6810.desc.en: We were wrong. The station orbiting [From.GetName] is not uninhabited; instead, it is crawling with giant alien arthropoids! The probes we deployed into the station only returned skittering shadows and large mandibles before signal was lost. Deep scans of the station have also revealed what we postulate to be an incredibly complex databank. To reach this databank, we would have to go through that cluster of many-legged defenders.

anomaly.6815.a.zh: 慢着，所以你们并不是带有敌意的害虫？
anomaly.6815.a.en: Wait, so you are not a hostile infestation?

anomaly.6815.desc.zh: 噢，你们好！很抱歉之前摧毁了你们的探测器。那只是因为我们在这做一些非常精密的实验，而我们担心一些外在的干扰会影响实验结果——我相信你能理解。那么，我们能帮上什么忙吗？
anomaly.6815.desc.en: Oh, hello there! Sorry about destroying your probe earlier. It's just that we are conducting some very delicate experiments here, and we were worried that outside interference could alter the results - I'm sure you understand. Now, how can we help you?

anomaly.6820.desc.zh: 究竟是什么原因会让你这么想啊？我们是一支策展人分遣队，派驻到这里研究这个恒星系独特的特征。如果你是想分享我们机构通常给予的那些福利，我建议你和我们的主研究实验室联系。我可以提供你一份目前我们在此地所发现的东西的拷贝。
anomaly.6820.desc.en: What would ever give you that impression? We are a Curator detachment sent here to study this system's unique properties. If you wish to partake of our order's usual offerings, I suggest contacting the primary research lab. I can provide you with a copy of our findings so far.

anomaly.6825.desc.food.zh: 这些水晶主要是由蔗糖构成的，想必具有潜在的食用价值。
anomaly.6825.desc.food.en: The crystals themselves are primarily made out of sucrose and could potentially even be edible.

anomaly.6825.desc.nofood.zh: 这些水晶主要是由蔗糖构成的，十分易碎。
anomaly.6825.desc.nofood.en: The crystals themselves are primarily made out of sucrose and are quite brittle.

anomaly.6825.desc.start.zh: [From.GetName]上生活的生命体形式和我们预想的完全不一样。我们的[owner.GetScientistPlural]汇报到，小行星内有不断生长的水晶。这些生命体利用[From.System.GetName]散发的辐射，并结合小行星内的矿物元素，被证实能够完成自给自足的繁衍生息。
anomaly.6825.desc.start.en: The lifeforms living on [From.GetName] were nothing like we expected. Our [owner.GetScientistPlural] report back that the asteroid has crystal growths. These growths have turned out to be self-sustaining and caused by the crystals taking in the ambient radiation of [From.System.GetName] and combining it with the mineral composition of the asteroid.

anomaly.6835.a.zh: 寻找更多的小行星来拓建水晶糖农场。
anomaly.6835.a.en: Search for more asteroids to expand the crystal farms.

anomaly.6835.a.tooltip.zh: 最多3个随机小行星将会生产3£food£食物。
anomaly.6835.a.tooltip.en: Up to 3 random asteroids will now produce 3 £food£ food.

anomaly.6835.b.zh: 还是不要拓建水晶糖农场了。
anomaly.6835.b.en: Let's not expand the crystal farms.

anomaly.6835.desc.zh: 在食用了太空生长的水晶糖数年之后，很明显，我们的人民对这一美食的需求愈发旺盛。我们的[Root.GetScientistPlural]已经列了一份表，上面是能够建造水晶糖农场的潜在候选地。
anomaly.6835.desc.en: After eating space-based crystal sugars for a few years now, it has become apparent that our population would like to see it more readily available. Our [Root.GetScientistPlural] have come up with a list of potential candidates where we could construct more crystal farms.

anomaly.6840.a.zh: 我们现在就需要那些矿物。

anomaly.6840.b.en: Good things come to those who wait.

anomaly.6840.desc.zh: [From.GetName]是一颗独特的气态巨行星。我们对天体物理的知识告诉我们，这样的行星应该有一个行星环，然而它并没有。在我们的科研船近距离观察了那颗诡异的卫星之后，这一现象的原因已经十分显然了。这颗星球被一些“牧羊人”卫星所环绕，这些卫星全部拥有富得难以置信的矿物，并且每年还在积累更多。我们可以用精准控制的爆炸爆破这些卫星，然后将它们的矿物一次性收集起来；也可以让它们继续留在环带，持续地收集它们积累下来的太空残骸。
anomaly.6840.desc.en: [From.GetName] is a peculiar gas giant. Our knowledge of astrophysics tells us that the planet should have a planetary ring, yet it doesn't. The cause of this became apparent after our science ship took a closer look at the intriguing moon. The planet is surrounded by shepherd moons, all incredibly rich in minerals and accumulating more every year. We could blast the moons with precise and controlled explosions and harvest them or keep them inside the ring zone and harvest the space debris they accrue.

anomaly.6845.desc.zh:
我们确实在[From.GetName]上发现了生命，但也是因为我们的行动，这一生命已经灭绝了。这些微生生物住在气态巨行星的外层边缘，对于我们的深度扫描表现出了极大的负面反应。扫描的频率同生物的细胞结构产生了共振——这一效应如同瀑布倾泻而下般飞速传开，从一个气态小虫子传播到另一只气态小虫。所有生物都在收到影响之后不久就不再活动了。

我们现在正环绕着全宇宙最大的坟场。
anomaly.6845.desc.en:
We did indeed discover life on [From.GetName], but by our actions, it has since been eradicated. The microbial creatures which lived in the outer edges of the gas giant's atmosphere reacted poorly to our deep scans. These frequencies caused each creature's cellular structure to resonate - an effect that then cascaded and spread from gas mite to gas mite. Each was rendered inert soon after.

We are now in orbit over the largest graveyard in the universe.

anomaly.685.desc.zh: 证据显示[From.GetName]的当前气候是由大量污染造成的失控温室效应造成的。海洋已经被煮沸了，[From.GetPlanetMoon]也因过厚的大气层造成的厚厚云层而永久与世隔绝。当地文明的遗迹散落在星球表面各处，揭示了一个工业时代中后期人口迅速增长的文明的消失。
anomaly.685.desc.en:
There is evidence that the current climate of [From.GetName] is the cause of a runaway greenhouse effect triggered by massive amounts of pollution. The oceans have boiled away and the [From.GetPlanetMoon] is permanently enclosed in a dense cloud layer due to the thick atmosphere.

Scattered ruins from the indigenous civilization can still be found on the surface, suggesting an overpopulated culture that perished in the mid to late stages of an Industrial Age.

anomaly.6850.desc.zh: 完成了！如同奇迹一般，当我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]对我们的飞船进行了合适的改造之后，它们能够重现最初的瀑布效应。这一次效果不一样，[FromFromFrom.GetName]上的生命体如同一波巨大的浪潮一样又重新涌动了起来。
anomaly.6850.desc.en: It is done! Miraculously, once our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] installed the proper modifications on our vessel, they were able to recreate the initial cascade. This time the effect was different, and life started springing back up all over [FromFromFrom.GetName] in a great wave.

anomaly.6850.desc.valuesothers.zh: 这一过程教会了我们许多关于宇宙的事情，但更多的可能是关于我们自己的事情。
anomaly.6850.desc.valuesothers.en: This process has taught us a lot about the universe but perhaps even more about ourselves.

anomaly.6855.b.zh: 等等，现在[From.GetName]的局势更—加—有趣了。
anomaly.6855.b.en: Wait, [From.GetName] is even MORE interesting now.

anomaly.6855.desc.gestalt.zh: 来自[Root.GetName]的信号突然从主脑意识中被切断了。[Owner.GetScientistPlural]看上去并没有死亡，只是无法与我们交流。们一直在研究[From.GetName]上奇怪的区域风暴，并且一直发回令人难以置信的前期报告。这股风暴会对发送过去的探测器做出反应，制造出真空口袋来避开它们，再缓慢地往回渗透进探测器。在联络被切断之前，[Root.GetName]的计划是在风暴处测试许多不同的扫描频率。科研船看上去已经沉没到了气态巨行星深处，现在已经陷入了沉寂。
anomaly.6855.desc.gestalt.en: The signals from [Root.GetName] were suddenly cut off from the consciousness. The [Owner.GetScientistPlural] do not appear to be dead, just unable to communicate with us. They had been studying the strange localized storms on [From.GetName] and were sending back incredible preliminary reports. The tempest reacted to the probes being sent in, creating vacuum pockets to avoid them and then slowly seeping back in towards the drones. The plan for [Root.GetName] was to test out numerous scanning frequencies at the storm before contact was cut off. The science ship seems to have sunk into the gas giant and now appears dormant.

anomaly.6855.desc.regular.zh: 我们从[Root.GetName]收到的最后一束信号无异于混乱的静电音。他们一直在研究[From.GetName]上奇怪的区域风暴，并且一直发回令人难以置信的前期报告。这股风暴会对发送过去的探测器做出反应，制造出真空口袋来避开它们，再缓慢地往回渗透进探测器。在我们失去联络之前，[Root.GetName]正计划在风暴处测试许多不同的扫描频率。科研船看上去已经沉没到了气态巨行星深处，现在已经陷入了沉寂。
anomaly.6855.desc.regular.en: The last signal received from [Root.GetName] was not much more than garbled static. They had been studying the strange localized storms on [From.GetName] and were sending back incredible preliminary reports. The tempest reacted to the probes being sent in, creating vacuum pockets to avoid them and then slowly seeping back in towards the drones. [Root.GetName] was planning on testing out numerous scanning frequencies at the storm before we lost contact. The science ship seems to have sunken into the gas giant and appears to be dormant.

anomaly.6860.desc.zh: 在几个月的工作之后，我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]终于设法调整[FromFrom.GetName]护盾的工作方式，使得[FromFromFrom.GetName]风暴放开了对落难舰船的钳制。同[trapped_in_storm.GetName]的通讯很快重新建立了起来，十分难以置信的是，[FromFrom.GetName]上没有组员记得他们被风暴困住的这段时间。
anomaly.6860.desc.en: After months of work, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] finally managed to alternate [FromFrom.GetName] shields in such a way that [FromFromFrom.GetName] tempest released its grip on the marooned ship. Communications with [trapped_in_storm.GetName] was quickly re-established, and incredibly none onboard [FromFrom.GetName] seem to remember their time trapped inside the storm.

anomaly.6865.desc.zh:
当[Root.GetName]靠的足够近得以扫描货舱的时候，似乎所有的传感器都功能失常了。这个舱室使用的[Owner.GetBioAlloy]同我们自己建造太空结构时使用的是完全一样的。这种某些外星生命体发明出了同我们完全一致的复合材料的可能性，根本不可能成立，但在校准了扫描仪之后，我们依然得到了同样的结果。

在打开舱室之后，迎接我们的唯一一样东西是一份文档集，里面详细地阐述了我们应当如何指派我们的每一位[Owner.GetScientistPlural]，以及他们今后的研究计划。该指引在一个特定日期结束，也就是从现在算起的整整10年。
anomaly.6865.desc.en:
Once [Root.GetName] got close enough to scan the cargo pod it was assumed that the sensors were malfunctioning. The pod is built out of the exact same [Owner.GetBioAlloy] we ourselves use for spacebound structures. The likelihood that some alien beings would come up with this exact mixture is beyond unlikely, yet after recalibrating the scanners the same results appeared.

Upon opening the pod, the only thing greeting us was a collection of documents detailing exactly where we should assign each of our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] and what they should be asked to study. The instructions end on a fixed date, one that is scheduled to fall exactly 10 years from now.

anomaly.6870.a.zh: 让过去的我们自己收拾这个烂摊子吧。
anomaly.6870.a.en: Let our past selves deal with this.

anomaly.6870.desc.zh: 在经过几年不顺坦的发展之后，[Root.Capital.GetName]的上方出现了一道时空织构裂口。令人心惊胆颤的是，这一天的日期和我们十年前收到的怪异指示上面所说的日期是同一天。我们现在只有一件需要做的事情：把收到的那些笔记发射到裂口里面，关闭这个循环。
anomaly.6870.desc.en: After years of uneasy development, a rip in the fabric of space has appeared above [Root.Capital.GetName]. Unnervingly this is the exact date as indicated in the strange instructions we received a decade ago. There is only one thing to do: send the documents we received back into the tear and close the loop.

anomaly.6875.desc.zh: [From.GetName]附近小行星的轨道是如此完美无暇地稳定，也不难理解为什么我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]会认为它是被人工放置在这个地方了。然而，那里也没有任何推进系统或者其他人工航行的迹象。唯一的自然演化结论是，由于某种几乎荒谬到不可能成真的几率，这颗小行星被[From.GetName]的重力场捕获了。我们在这颗小行星的表面还探测到了几种十分稀有的水晶。
anomaly.6875.desc.en: The asteroid around [From.GetName] has such a perfectly stable orbit that it's easy to understand why our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] thought it was placed there artificially. Yet, there are no conclusive indications of any propulsion systems or any other artificial marring. The only natural conclusion is that, by some absurdly improbable chance, the asteroid got caught in [From.GetName]'s gravity field. We have also detected some rare crystals on the surface of the asteroid.

anomaly.6880.desc.zh: 正当我们的采矿站在这颗被捕获的小行星上完工几天之后，这枚岩石突然开始旋转起来，在这个过程中摧毁了采矿站，但同时又有更多的稀有水晶矿藏暴露在了我们的传感器面前！
anomaly.6880.desc.en: Just a day after finishing our mining station on the trapped asteroid, the rock abruptly rotated, destroying the mining station. In the process of doing this, even more rare crystals deposits were exposed to our sensors!

anomaly.6885.desc.zh: 警报的笛声响彻整个[Solar_System.GetName]，大量的晶化野兽从小行星庇护所里面冲了出来，正是我们在钻孔并打算提取晶体的那颗小行星。它看上去生气了。
anomaly.6885.desc.en: Warning sirens blared across [Solar_System.GetName] as the massive crystalline beast left the shelter of the asteroid we had been drilling into and extracting crystals from. It seems angry.

anomaly.6890.a.en: What can we learn from it?

anomaly.6890.desc.zh: 这个被捕捉的小行星，实际上，是某种晶态生命体的巢穴。很庆幸我们没有继续挖掘，因为看上去我们似乎激怒了在里面休眠的生物。如果我们什么都不做，只是从远处研究它，这些生物应该会平静下来。
anomaly.6890.desc.en: The trapped asteroid is, in fact, a crystalline being's nest. It is good that we didn't keep digging, for it seems like we agitated the creature hibernating inside. If we do nothing for a while and study it from afar, it should settle down.

anomaly.6895.b.zh: 收集我们可以收集的部分。

anomaly.6895.d.zh: 就让沉睡的傻瓜继续躺平吧。

anomaly.6895.desc.catano.zh: 我们在[From.GetName]的有毒大气层内观测到的生命信号，是体型庞大的半有机机械体！这个外星工业体似乎正是星球上乌烟瘴气的罪魁祸首，而且它依旧在运转。这个星球上没有其他的生命信号，这些机械体的造物主肯定抛下它们自己跑掉了。我们目前还不能确定它们的意图，但是它们建造的建筑想必能够帮助我们更好地理解工程学。
anomaly.6895.desc.catano.en: The life signs observed within the toxic atmosphere of [From.GetName] are giant semi-organic machines! This alien industry seems to have been the cause of the noxious atmosphere on the planet, yet it's still operational. No other life signs remain on the world, and the creators of these machines must have left them running. We can't quite ascertain their purpose yet, but their construction could surely help our understanding of engineering.

anomaly.6895.desc.catayes.zh: 我们在[From.GetName]的有毒大气层内观测到的生命信号，是体型庞大的半有机机械体！正如我们一样，看上去这个设施的创造者也很青睐生物和机械的融合之美。这个外星工业体似乎正是星球上乌烟瘴气的罪魁祸首，而且它依旧在运转。这个星球上没有其他的生命信号，这些机械体的造物主肯定抛下它们自己跑掉了。我们目前还不能确定它们的意图，但是它们建造的建筑想必能够帮助我们更好地理解工程学。
anomaly.6895.desc.catayes.en: The life signs observed within the toxic atmosphere of [From.GetName] are giant semi-organic machines! Like us, it seems like the creators of this facility appreciated a merging of the biological and mechanical. This alien industry appears to have been the cause of the noxious atmosphere on the planet, yet it's still operational. No other life signs remain on the world, and the creators of these machines must have left them running. We can't quite ascertain their purpose yet, but their construction could surely help our understanding of engineering.

anomaly.690.desc.zh: 虽对大多数生物都有毒性，[From.GetName]的高气压大气层也同样存在生机勃勃的生态环境。这里的生物用氨水而不是水来作为溶剂，并因此发展出了与其他地区截然不同的生态特征。对它们的研究会极大的丰富对异星生物学的了解。
anomaly.690.desc.en: Although toxic to most forms of known life, [From.GetName] supports a thriving ecology within the high pressure of its atmosphere. Life here uses ammonia instead of water as a solvent, and has developed in ways that differ significantly from previously established ecological models. Its study would greatly benefit our knowledge of xeno biology.

anomaly.6900.a.zh: 你能够解开这些计算吗？

anomaly.6900.a.tooltip.zh: 使用这个星球辅助我们计算当前的天体物理困局。
anomaly.6900.a.tooltip.en: Use the world to assist in calculating our current astrophysics dilemmas.

anomaly.6900.desc.zh: 我们并不是在地表之下检测到了生命形式，事实上，是整个星球都检测到了生命！这颗冰封的星球内部布满了微细的管道，相互连接，就像一台原始的计算机。尽管结构很粗糙，它通天的规模意味着，其算力甚至可以匹敌[Owner.Capital.GetName]的某些超级计算机。即使是现在，这台电脑还在活动——我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]可以同其互动，但是由于它运转十分缓慢，我们只能询问其一个简单的问题。
anomaly.6900.desc.en: We didn't detect life forms below the surface. We detected them in the entire world! The frozen planet is interspersed with micro-thin tubes linked like a rudimentary computer. While the structure is primitive, its gigantic scale means it can probably rival some of [Owner.Capital.GetName]'s supercomputers in output. Even now, the computer seems to be active - our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] can interface with it, but since it's so slow, we would only be able to ask it a single question.

anomaly.6900.e.en: Best to observe it from afar.

anomaly.6905.desc.zh: 我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]有了更加惊怖的发现。他们早前扫描到的山脉，实际上是某个巨型蛋的卵壳膜。我们也不知道究竟是什么巨兽诞下了这么一枚蛋，更不知道何等的怖兽会从中孵化出来。
anomaly.6905.desc.en: Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have discovered something rather monstrous. The mountain range they scanned earlier was in actuality the outer membrane of a gigantic egg. It's uncertain what behemoth could lay such an egg and what horror would hatch from it.

anomaly.6910.desc.hatchling.zh: 尽管这个蛋同我们文明之前遭遇到的虚空孶孽很相似，但是它孕育了更加伟大的存在。
anomaly.6910.desc.hatchling.en: While similar to the voidspawn our civilization encountered before, this egg would have created something much grander.

anomaly.6910.desc.start.zh: [FromFromFrom.GetName]的内部有什么东西超出我们所料。我们并没有发现什么巨兽生命的幼体，取而代之的只是一团基因浆。整个行星的内部填满了基因物质和资源。全部这些物质最终会变成什么还不明晰，但是如果不打破砂锅问到底，我们的星系可能会更加安全。
anomaly.6910.desc.start.en: The insides of [FromFromFrom.GetName] were not what we expected. Instead of some infant titanic lifeform, we've simply uncovered genetic slop. The entire planet is filled with genetic material and resources. What all this material would have become is unclear, but our galaxy is probably safer, not knowing.

anomaly.6915.desc.gestalt.zh: 我们派遣去往[Solar_System.GetName]星系的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]全部拉响了警报，但是没过多久就系数同[Owner.GetBrainName]失去了联系，只告诉了我们“它松动了。”当蛋壳开始裂开的时候，[Root.GetName]最后的传输信号被切断；当我们发射探测器去扫描[FromFromFrom.GetName]的残骸的时候，我们只看到了一个空壳。看上去这个生物对自己的解放者并没有多少感激之情。
anomaly.6915.desc.gestalt.en: Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] dispatched to the [Solar_System.GetName] system all reacted in alarm shortly before losing contact with the [Owner.GetBrainName], only telling us that "It's loose." The last transmission of the [Root.GetName] cuts off as the egg begins to crack open, and when we use our probes to scan the remains of [FromFromFrom.GetName], we find a hollow shell. It seems the creature had little gratitude for its liberator.

anomaly.6915.desc.regular.zh:
“它活了！它又活过来了！同如此至伟的造物相比，我们不过是微不足道的凡尘；面对如此伟大之物，繁星帝国之间的鸡毛琐事又可称几——”

[Root.GetName]最后的传输信号在此中断，当我们发送探测器去扫描[FromFromFrom.GetName]残骸的时候，我们只看到了一个空壳。看上去这个生物对自己的解放者并没有多少感激之情。
anomaly.6915.desc.regular.en:
"IT LIVES! IT LIVES AGAIN! We are nothing but insignificant specks compared to such a creature; what does the ephemeral squabbling between empires matter in the face of such great-"

The last transmission of the [Root.GetName] cuts off there, and when we use our probes to scan the remains of [FromFromFrom.GetName], we find a hollow shell. It seems the creature had little gratitude to show its liberators.

anomaly.695.desc.zh: [From.GetName]荒凉地表下的庞杂地下通道中生活着某种硅基生物。根据目前的了解，该生物以岩石为食，并且进化出了基本智能。它们在地下开凿通道的行为使得地表出现了许多有价值的矿物质。
anomaly.695.desc.en: Some kind of burrowing silicon-based life form inhabits a vast network of tunnels beneath the barren surface of [From.GetName]. As best as we can tell, the creatures feed off rocks and there is evidence to suggest that they possess a rudimentary form of intelligence. Their tunneling efforts have shuffled large amounts of valuable minerals to the surface.

anomaly.7000.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]上发现的这座巨大的碑塔让我们的科研船派过去都微如蝼蚁。在这块宏伟的、光滑的板状金属表面，曾经炫目的彩色图案如今已变得斑驳。

机器的侧面一处小的能量出口似乎暗示着只要以适量的能量币作为交换，它的秘密就能悉数揭示，
anomaly.7000.desc.en:
The monolith we found on [From.GetName] dwarfs the science ship we sent to investigate it. A majestic, smooth slab of metal, the once-garish pigment patterns on the front have been reduced to mere flecks.

A small power outlet on the machine's side promises its secrets will be unveiled in exchange for a modest sum of energy credits.

anomaly.7010.a.zh: 给罐里头的饮料注册专利，然后把它卖给全星系。
anomaly.7010.a.en: Patent the drink. Sell it to the whole galaxy.

anomaly.7010.desc.empty.zh: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$这个圆柱状罐体内部是中空的，其内容物早就已经从腐蚀掉的封盖中蒸发殆尽。这个罐体自身状态良好，构成其的未知合金与我们用于建造舰船的合金水平相当。
anomaly.7010.desc.empty.en: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$The cylinder is empty, its content long evaporated through a corroded sealing cap. The container itself is still in good shape, though, and the unknown alloy is on par with the metal we use to make our ships.

anomaly.7010.desc.full.bio.zh: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$这种饮品已经轻易地被我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]复制出来了，经过了大量缜密的测试后确认，这种液体干净又卫生，富有营养，而且关键的是还很好喝。
anomaly.7010.desc.full.bio.en: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$ The drink has been easily replicated by our [Owner.GetScientistPlural], who, after conducting rigorous testing, have ascertained it to be safe, nutritious and - most crucially - delicious.

anomaly.7010.desc.full.megacorp.zh: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$依据市场数据，这种失传已久的饮品比我们目前能为生物体提供的最好的饮料还要好喝20%。
anomaly.7010.desc.full.megacorp.en: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$ According to our market data, the long-forgotten drink is 20% more delicious than our current range of drinkable products for biological entities.

anomaly.7010.desc.full.nonbio.zh: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$ $anomaly.7010.desc.full$尽管这种饮品对我们没有直接用处，我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]已可以把它们转化成更有用的资源：异星天然气。
anomaly.7010.desc.full.nonbio.en: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$ While the liquid provides no substance to us, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have been able to convert it into a much more valuable resource: Exotic Gas.

anomaly.7010.desc.rot.bio.zh: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$其中包含的液体恶臭不堪；这种曾经可口的营养物质被岁月的流逝所腐坏。通过研究这些物质，我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]期望可以获悉一些关于曾经喜爱这种饮品的外星人的生物学信息，假定我们能先搞定它的臭味的话。
anomaly.7010.desc.rot.bio.en: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$The cylinder contains a liquid most foul; a once-delicious nutrient long spoiled by time. By studying the substance, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] hope to learn about the biology of the aliens who once delighted in it - assuming we can do something about the smell first.

anomaly.7010.desc.rot.nonbio.zh: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$圆柱状罐体内部包含的液体混合物含有蔗糖、柠檬酸和其他生物性物质。我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]相信它是一种由碳基生命制造并饮用的富有营养的物质。进一步的研究有可能能提供关于这种已消亡物种的生物学线索。
anomaly.7010.desc.rot.nonbio.en: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$The cylinder contains a liquid mixture of sucrose, citric acid, and other biological compounds. Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] believe it to be a nutrient substance made by and for carbon-based beings. Further studies will hopefully provide more clues pertaining to the biology of this lost race.

anomaly.7020.desc.zh: 我们找到了一艘设计独特的古代太空舰船。它使用的推进方式与现代舰船并不相同，而是依赖于在真空中展开的巨大的帆来进行。也许这艘船可以捕获恒星能量，并在星光和恒星风的推动下前进。
anomaly.7020.desc.en: We have found the wreckage of an archaic spaceship of unusual design. Instead of using propulsion similar to that of modern ships, the craft relied on large sails unfurled in the vacuum of space. Presumably, the ship harvested solar energy and drifted on the solar winds created by starlight.

anomaly.7030.desc.zh: 我们发现了一艘古老的外星人星舰，它被半掩埋在一个小行星撞击坑中间。这艘科研船的外壳搭载了一个扩增的探测阵列，没有配备武器。船体外部在撞击之前没有受到任何伤害。我们可以假设，这场灾难之所以发生，是因为船员酿成的某种致命错误。
anomaly.7030.desc.en: We have discovered an ancient alien starship half-buried in an asteroid crater. This science ship's exterior has an extensive sensory array and no weaponry. The exterior was not damaged in any way before it crashed. We can assume this catastrophe was the result of a fatal error caused by the crew.

anomaly.705.desc.zh: [From.GetName]的表面发现了一个小型的短距离传输装置。它看起来像是一个古老的侦测标记器，很久之前被安放于此来定位一批大型的珍贵金属矿藏。该来的矿工没能到达，因为这些珍贵的金属还静静地躺在这里。
anomaly.705.desc.en: A small short-range transmitter has been located on the surface of [From.GetName]. It appears to be an ancient survey marker, placed here eons ago to mark a large deposit of precious metals. The miners it was meant for evidently never arrived, as the deposit is still here.

anomaly.7100.alt.desc.zh: 我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]一开始以为这是小行星，结果发现这其实是冰冻的、被压实的外星动物尸体，其体型基本和在这个恒星系游荡的外星生命体一致。整个小行星环，实际上，是一片露天墓地。其中的一部分尸体是最近刚刚到达并开始腐坏的，而剩下的已历经千年岁月，甚至比我们的帝国还要久远。
anomaly.7100.alt.desc.en: What our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] first mistook for asteroids have been revealed to be frozen, battered corpses of alien fauna, roughly matching the shape of the aliens seen roaming the system. The entire asteroid ring is, in fact, just an open burial ground. Some of the bodies we acquired are recently deceased, while others predate our empire by thousand of years.

anomaly.7100.desc.zh: 我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]一开始以为这是小行星，结果发现这其实是冰冻的、被压实的缇扬奇尸体，在轨道上历经几十年之后，成为一堆不成形状的块状物。整个小行星环，实际上，是一片露天墓地。其中的一部分尸体是最近刚刚到达并开始腐坏的，而剩下的已历经千年岁月，甚至比我们的帝国还要久远。
anomaly.7100.desc.en: What our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] first mistook for asteroids have been revealed to be frozen, battered Tiyanki corpses reduced to shapeless lumps after decades in orbit. The entire asteroid ring is, in fact, just an open burial ground. Some of the bodies we acquired are recently deceased, while others predate our empire by thousand of years.

anomaly.7101.c.desc.zh: 蜂巢可以复制这些磁力波，用于增强自己的意志。
anomaly.7101.c.desc.en: The hive can replicate these magnetic waves and use them to strengthen its will.

anomaly.7101.hive.desc.zh: 这颗行星发射出了一系列信号，我们的探索工蜂认为它们应该是人造的。但在进一步的检测后，我们发现这些信号不过是一些自然现象，它的独特性质可以用于增强我们的工蜂与主脑的连接。用这颗行星产生的磁力波照射工蜂后它们可以更好地响应主脑的意志。
anomaly.7101.hive.desc.en: The planet is emitting a series of signals that our exploratory drones speculated might be of artificial origin. Upon closer examination, they turned out to be nothing more than a natural phenomenon, one with the unusual property of strengthening the connection of our drones to the collective mind. It seems that drones exposed to the planet's magnetic waves respond better to the will of the hive.

anomaly.7101.machines.desc.zh: 这颗行星发射出了一系列信号，我们的探索无人机认为它们应该是人造的。但在进一步的检测后，我们发现这些信号不过是一些自然发生的不寻常但无害的磁力波。这一发现并没有产生即时有效的收益，但由于实在是太特别，在长期的研究中它可以提供一些研究数据。
anomaly.7101.machines.desc.en: The planet is emitting a series of signals that our exploratory drones speculated might be of artificial origin. Upon closer examination, the signals were revealed to be merely a natural phenomenon caused by unusual but harmless magnetic waves. This discovery does not provide any immediate benefit to the collective, but given their uniqueness, studying them may provide us with some research data in the long run.

anomaly.7101.standard.desc.zh:
我们起先认为这是一种刻意的交流尝试，结果发现它不过是一种不常见的自然现象。这颗行星产生的磁力波只要进行合适的调整和编辑，就可以听起来像歌唱一般，但这肯定不是由任何有意识的个体产生的。然而我们的一些科学家也发现，这“歌声”相当地吸引人。

也许我们可以利用这一现象，比如招待艺术家或VIP到空间站中，然后捕获这些信号，把它们作为一种放松的音乐播放给他们听。
anomaly.7101.standard.desc.en:
What we first assumed to be a deliberate attempt at communication has turned out to be an unusual but naturally occurring phenomenon. The magnetic waves produced by the planet, given proper handling and editing, may sound a bit like talking or even singing, but they are in no way created by a thinking being. Some of our scientists, however, find it quite catchy.

It might be possible to make use of this phenomenon, possibly by hosting artists or VIPs at a station created solely to catch these signals and play them as relaxing music.

anomaly.7105.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]的异常能量读数的来源确定是一个蓝色的小球。[Owner.GetScientistPlural]汇报，传感器从中发现了相反极性的快子。

该物体周围的地面上刻着符号，也许是由某个更古老的文明留下的。目前不清楚是符号的含义是指引还是警示。

完整的文本还远不能翻译，但部分符号似乎与时间测量和[Solar_System.GetName]恒星系中天体相对位置有关。
anomaly.7105.desc.en:
The source of the unusual energy readings noted on [From.GetName] is confirmed to be a small, blue orb. The [Owner.GetScientistPlural] report that sensors pick up tachyons of reverse polarity.

Symbols are carved into the ground around the object, perhaps placed there by an older civilization. It is unclear whether they are meant as an instruction, or a warning.

The full inscription is far from translated, but individual symbols seem related to the measuring of time and the relative positions of celestial objects in the [Solar_System.GetName] system.

anomaly.7110.desc.zh:
在[FromFrom.GetName]发现的蓝色能量球体消失了。对当地的扫描完全没有发现该球体的任何迹象。更令人困惑的是，地上的符号也一同消失得无影无踪，如同从未存在过一般。

基于在此处发现的异常的快子信号，我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]推断，球体和符号一同发生了时间回溯。
anomaly.7110.desc.en:
The orb of blue energy first detected on [FromFrom.GetName] has disappeared. A scan of the location show no traces of the strange sphere. Even more baffling is the erasure of the markings on the ground: it is as if they were never there.

Given the unusual tachyon readings we detected at the site, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] postulate that both the orb and the writing were moving backwards through time.

anomaly.7115.a.immortal.tt.zh: [intemporal_leader.GetName]得到一艘小型舰船以独自进行太空旅行。
anomaly.7115.a.immortal.tt.en: [intemporal_leader.GetName] receive[intemporal_leader.GetSXX] a small vessel to travel the stars alone.

anomaly.7115.a.regular.tt.zh:
[intemporal_leader.GetName]得到一艘小型舰船以独自进行太空旅行。
需要指派一名新的科学官来指挥[From.GetName]。
anomaly.7115.a.regular.tt.en:
[intemporal_leader.GetName] receive[intemporal_leader.GetSXX] a small vessel to travel the stars alone.
A new Scientist has to be assigned to lead [From.GetName].

anomaly.7115.b.immortal.tt.en: [intemporal_leader.GetName] becomes available as a new Scientist.

anomaly.7115.desc.devouring.zh:
[Root.GetLeaderName]吃掉了[FromFrom.GetName]上的球体。

[leader.GetHeSheCap]接收到了一份图像，显示时间如同一条河流一般延展，前后连接着无尽的过去与未来。在[leader.GetHimHer]的面前，蓝色能量从时间流中蜿蜒涌出，被被吸入了[leader.GetHisHer]的身体里。尽管该意外在其他[Owner.GetScientistPlural]的精确测量中持续了不到一秒钟，但[leader.GetHeShe]感觉仿佛度过了一个多小时。

在幻觉结束后，我们确信时间不会再影响[Root.GetLeaderName]了。由于现在拥有了无限的时间，我们可以利用[leader.GetHisHer]无尽的寿命令其自行探索宇宙。
anomaly.7115.desc.devouring.en:
[Root.GetLeaderName] ate the blue orb on [FromFrom.GetName].

[leader.GetHeSheCap] received a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, we were certain that time would no longer affect [Root.GetLeaderName]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, we could use [leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [leader.GetHisHer] own.

anomaly.7115.desc.hive.zh:
在[FromFrom.GetName]上的站点进行工作时，[Root.GetLeaderName]无意间擦到了蓝色球体。

[leader.GetHeSheCap]接收到了一份图像，显示时间如同一条河流一般延展，前后连接着无尽的过去与未来。在[leader.GetHimHer]的面前，蓝色能量从时间流中蜿蜒涌出，被被吸入了[leader.GetHisHer]的身体里。尽管该意外在其他[Owner.GetScientistPlural]的精确测量中持续了不到一秒钟，但[leader.GetHeShe]感觉仿佛度过了一个多小时。

在幻觉结束后，我们确信时间不会再影响[Root.GetLeaderName]了。由于现在拥有了无限的时间，我们可以利用[leader.GetHisHer]无尽的寿命令其自行探索宇宙。
anomaly.7115.desc.hive.en:
While working at the site on [FromFrom.GetName], [Root.GetLeaderName] brushed against the blue orb.

[leader.GetHeSheCap] received a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, we were certain that time would no longer affect [Root.GetLeaderName]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, we could use [leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [leader.GetHisHer] own.

anomaly.7115.desc.immortal.zh:
在[FromFrom.GetName]上的站点进行工作时，实习[Owner.GetScientist][intemporal_leader.GetName]无意间擦到了蓝色球体。

[intemporal_leader.GetHeSheCap]之后称看到了时间如同一条河流一般延展，前后连接着无尽的过去与未来。在[intemporal_leader.GetHimHer]的面前，蓝色能量从时间流中蜿蜒涌出，被被吸入了[intemporal_leader.GetHisHer]的身体里。尽管该意外在[Owner.GetScientistPlural]精确测量中持续了不到一秒钟，但[intemporal_leader.GetHeShe]感觉仿佛度过了一个多小时。

在幻觉结束后，[intemporal_leader.GetName]确信时间不会再影响[intemporal_leader.GetHimHer]了。[intemporal_leader.GetHeShe]现在拥有了无限的时间，于是想利用无尽的寿命自行探索宇宙。
anomaly.7115.desc.immortal.en:
While working at the site on [FromFrom.GetName], junior [Owner.GetScientist] [intemporal_leader.GetName] brushed against the blue orb.

[intemporal_leader.GetHeSheCap] later described a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [intemporal_leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [intemporal_leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [intemporal_leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, [intemporal_leader.GetName] was certain that time would no longer affect [intemporal_leader.GetHimHer]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, [intemporal_leader.GetHeShe] want[intemporal_leader.GetSXX] to use [intemporal_leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [intemporal_leader.GetHisHer] own.

anomaly.7115.desc.regular.zh:
在[FromFrom.GetName]上的站点进行工作时，[Root.GetLeaderName]无意间擦到了蓝色球体。

[leader.GetHeSheCap]之后称看到了时间如同一条河流一般延展，前后连接着无尽的过去与未来。在[leader.GetHimHer]的面前，蓝色能量从时间流中蜿蜒涌出，被吸入了[leader.GetHisHer]的身体里。尽管该意外在[Owner.GetScientistPlural]精确测量中持续了不到一秒钟，但[leader.GetHeShe]感觉仿佛度过了一个多小时。

在幻觉结束后，[Root.GetLeaderName]确信时间不会再影响[leader.GetHimHer]了。[leader.GetHeShe]现在拥有了无限的时间，于是想利用无尽的寿命自行探索宇宙。
anomaly.7115.desc.regular.en:
While working at the site on [FromFrom.GetName], [Root.GetLeaderName] brushed against the blue orb.

[leader.GetHeSheCap] later described a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, [Root.GetLeaderName] was certain that time would no longer affect [leader.GetHimHer]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, [leader.GetHeShe] want[leader.GetSXX] to use [leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [leader.GetHisHer] own.

anomaly.7120.desc.hive.zh:
长程扫描发现了一艘舰船正在驶向[Root.Capital.GetName]。随着它越来越近，我们发现那艘船的设计与我们一世纪前的如出一辙。我们发现那艘舰船是[intemporal_explorer.GetName]驾驶的，就是那位被蓝色球体从时间流中带走的[Owner.GetScientist]。

这位[Owner.GetScientist]的再次连入了我们，知识涌入集体思维中：那是关于对撞的中子星和逆转的时空引力井的观测记忆。传输一结束，这艘船又启程返回了虚空。值得一提的是，我们的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]证实，他带回来的信息不仅大部分是可信的，而且甚至是开创性的。

[intemporal_explorer.GetName]的身体似乎完全不随着时间的流逝而改变，即便我们最近的科技也无法解释那颗球体的功能。[intemporal_explorer.GetHeShe]得以逃脱终极灭亡，将会继续探索宇宙，直到时间的终结。
anomaly.7120.desc.hive.en:
Long-range scans picked up an approaching vessel near [Root.Capital.GetName]. As it moved closer, it became clear that the ship's design matched our own from a century ago. We discovered that the ship was piloted by [intemporal_explorer.GetName], the [Owner.GetScientist] who [intemporal_explorer.GetWasWere] detached from the timestream by a blue energy orb.

Again with us, knowledge flowed from the [Owner.GetScientist] into the collective: sense-impressions of colliding neutron stars and inverse space-time gravitational wells. Once the transfer was complete, the ship continued on into the dark. Remarkably, our physics [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have confirmed that much of this data is not only verifiable, but indeed groundbreaking.

[intemporal_explorer.GetName] appeared physically unchanged by the passage of time, but even our current technology could not explain the functionality of the orb. Barring their own fatal destruction, [intemporal_explorer.GetHeShe] will continue to explore the universe until the end of time.

anomaly.7120.desc.regular.zh:
长程扫描发现了一艘舰船正在驶向[Root.Capital.GetName]。随着它越来越近，我们发现那艘船的设计与我们一世纪前的如出一辙。

在打开通讯之后，我们发现那艘舰船是[intemporal_explorer.GetName]驾驶的，就是那位被蓝色球体从时间流中带走的[Owner.GetScientist]。

[intemporal_explorer.GetHeSheCap]在对撞的中子星和逆转的时空引力井周围漫步，又乘坐飞船返回虚空。值得一提的是，我们的物理学家证实，他带回来的信息不仅大部分是可信的，而且甚至是开创性的。

[intemporal_explorer.GetName]的身体似乎完全不随着时间的流逝而改变，即便我们最近的科技也无法解释那颗球体的功能。[intemporal_explorer.GetHeShe]得以逃脱终极灭亡，将会继续探索宇宙，直到时间的终结。
anomaly.7120.desc.regular.en:
Long-range scans picked up an approaching vessel near [Root.Capital.GetName]. As it moved closer, it became clear that the ship's design matched our own from a century ago.

After opening comms, we discovered that the ship was piloted by [intemporal_explorer.GetName], the [Owner.GetScientist] who [intemporal_explorer.GetWasWere] detached from the timestream by a blue energy orb.

[intemporal_explorer.GetHeSheCap] rambled about colliding neutron stars and inverse space-time gravitational wells, before taking the ship back into the dark. Remarkably, our physicists have confirmed that much of this information is not only verifiable, but indeed groundbreaking.

[intemporal_explorer.GetName] appeared physically unchanged by the passage of time, but even our current technology could not explain the functionality of the orb. Barring their own fatal destruction, [intemporal_explorer.GetHeShe] will continue to explore the universe until the end of time.

anomaly.7135.a.zh: 调查为什么现在会发生这种情况。
anomaly.7135.a.en: Investigate why this is happening now.

anomaly.7135.b.tooltip.zh: 我们将从远处监控局势。
anomaly.7135.b.tooltip.en: We'll monitor the situation from afar.

anomaly.7135.desc.zh:
我们在[desertling_planet.GetName]上发现了生命。没有智慧的小型哺乳动物群遍布在整个行星表面。

我们的科学家将它们标记为“沙生兽”，它们的数量正以惊人的速度增加。这个行星已经超出了它的承载能力，生态系统正在迅速恶化。
anomaly.7135.desc.en:
We have found life on [desertling_planet.GetName]. Vast non-sapient herds of small mammals roam across the entire planetary surface.

Their population, labeled 'desertlings' by our scientists, is increasing at an alarming rate. The planet is already beyond its capacity, and the ecosystem is deteriorating rapidly.

anomaly.7140.a.zh: 我们将尽可能多收养这些小东西。
anomaly.7140.a.en: We will adopt as many critters as possible.

anomaly.7140.a.tooltip.zh: 我们将对他们的行为负责。
anomaly.7140.a.tooltip.en: We will be responsible for their actions.

anomaly.7140.b.zh: 制定动物数量控制政策。

anomaly.7140.b.tooltip.zh: 选择遗传修饰可用于遏制生长…
anomaly.7140.b.tooltip.en: Select genetic modifications could be used to curb the growth...

anomaly.7140.c.tooltip.zh: 必须不惜一切代价保护行星。
anomaly.7140.c.tooltip.en: The planet must be protected at all cost.

anomaly.7140.d.zh: 我们将一些动物当作牲口。
anomaly.7140.d.en: We'll take some animals as livestock.

anomaly.7140.d.tooltip.zh: 我们将向每个殖民地带去两个奴隶。
anomaly.7140.d.tooltip.en: We'll take two slaves for every colony.

anomaly.7140.desc.zh:
在研究[desertling_planet.GetName]上的沙生兽时，我们的科学家观察到了一个关键的现象。尽管这个物种到处都是，但却没有相应的化石记录。这些生态入侵者在相对短的时间内造成了极端的环境破坏，很可能是被某个外来者带到这里的。

形势已经十分清楚，迫切需要我们进行干预。如果不采取行动，这些生物将摧毁这个星球自然生态系统中剩下的一切。
anomaly.7140.desc.en:
While studying the desertlings on [desertling_planet.GetName] our scientists have made a pivotal observation. Despite the ubiquitous nature of the species, there is a striking absence of matching fossil records. These ecological interlopers have caused extreme environmental damage over a relatively short time period, and were most likely transported here by an outside actor.

The pressing need for intervention has become abundantly clear. Without action, these creatures will destroy what remains of this planet's natural ecosystem.

anomaly.7145.a.en: At least the suffering is now over.

anomaly.7150.desc.zh:
经过艰苦的努力，我们对[desertling_planet.GetName]上的沙漠生物进行扑杀和基因改造，它们的数量终于降低到了一个可持续的水平。

没有了过多的食草动物，一个微妙的平衡出现了。大自然正在迅速恢复，新鲜的草地开始在曾经荒凉的沙漠上生长。
anomaly.7150.desc.en:
After an arduous effort to sterilize and genetically alter the desertlings on [desertling_planet.GetName], their population has finally been reduced to a sustainable level.

Without the overwhelming amount of grazers, a delicate equilibrium has emerged. Nature is rapidly restoring itself, as fresh patches of grass begin to sprout over the once barren desert.

anomaly.7155.desc.zh: 最终，最后一只啮齿动物在[desertling_planet.GetName]上死去。沙子本身已经被染成了红色，这是因为我们为拯救星球免于侵染所付出的巨大努力，但是新的绿芽已经开始萌发。我们出手的时候刚刚好。
anomaly.7155.desc.en: Finally, the last of the rodents lie dead on [desertling_planet.GetName]. The sand itself has been tinted red by our massive effort to save the planet from its infestation, but already new green buds have begun to sprout. We were just in time.

anomaly.7200.a.zh: 谢谢你修复我们的星系。
anomaly.7200.a.en: Thank you for fixing our galaxy.

anomaly.7200.desc.zh:
瑟顿之中的景象光怪陆离。涡旋的行星在黑暗中若隐若现；附近是我们宇宙本身织构的一个缺口，也是一个吞噬着其中恒星光芒的宇宙巨胃。

尽管行星体的排列看似正常，但进一步的研究发现它们是以一种非常精确的数学关系安排到一起的。数百万年前，某种难以置信的力量将这个恒星系的轨道天体编排成了一种独特的图样，这种图案不仅影响着裂隙，还避免了它裂向更广阔的星系。

我们似乎来得正好——这项史诗级的工程即将竣工。这个星系距离恢复正常近在咫尺。
anomaly.7200.desc.en:
Seddom is an eerie spectacle. The swirling planets are wreathed in darkness; nearby is a breach in the very fabric of our universe, a cosmic maw that devours the very radiance of the system's star.

Despite the seemingly natural arrangement of planetoids, further analysis has revealed that they are arranged with mathematical precision. Millennia ago, some incredible force orchestrated the orbital bodies of this system into a specialized pattern, one which has not only mitigated the effects of the tear, but prevented it from spreading into the wider galaxy.

We arrive here at an auspicious moment - a monumental work nears completion. This system's restoration is imminent.

anomaly.75.b.en: Make do with what you can study from the surface.

anomaly.75.c.zh: 它跟我们有些相似。我们跟它来谈谈吧。
anomaly.75.c.en: It is not so unlike us. Let us talk.

anomaly.75.c.tooltip.zh: 命令[Root.GetName]将表面探测器连接到[From.GetName]并解码其所谓的神经活动。
anomaly.75.c.tooltip.en: Order [Root.GetName] to attach surface probes to [From.GetName] and decode its alleged neural activity

anomaly.75.desc.zh: 对巨型小行星[From.GetName]的扫描得出了有趣的结果。这块岩石的核心里含有携带微弱电流的导电晶体网络。[Root.GetName]上的成员辨认出这片晶体网络与原始神经网络具有相似性，认为就算该天体并不具有完全智能，也能进行某种程度的思考。他们请求将核心取出，并带到最近的轨道站以进行更仔细的研究。
anomaly.75.desc.en: A scan of the particularly massive asteroid [From.GetName] yields fascinating results. The rock's core is shot through with a network of conductive crystals carrying a weak electric charge. The crew on the [Root.GetName] recognize this matrix as a primitive neural lattice and believe the celestial body to be thinking in some capacity, if not fully sapient. They seek permission to excavate the core and transport it to the nearest orbital station for closer study.

anomaly.76.a.zh: 转念一想，这似乎不明智。
anomaly.76.a.en: On second thought, this seems ill-advised.

anomaly.76.a.tooltip.zh: 放弃直接与[rock_brain.GetName]的交流，保持距离进行研究吧。
anomaly.76.a.tooltip.en: Abort any attempts at contacting [rock_brain.GetName] directly, and study it from afar

anomaly.76.desc.zh:
我是[rock_scientist.GetName]。这项任务很有挑战性，但我认为我们已经成功将这些内容解析为类似于……也许不是语言，而是概念，或者想法。我们可以将类似的东西反馈给小行星，或许可以进行交流。

我们将显示一些 <过滤后的输出>，我将尽我所能对原始数据进行“更完整的解释”。
anomaly.76.desc.en:
[rock_scientist.GetName] here. It was a challenge, but I think we've managed to parse the readings into something like... not language perhaps, but concepts. Ideas. And we can feed something similar back to the asteroid, to maybe communicate.

We'll display some of the <filtered output>, and I'll do my best to give a more "complete interpretation" of the raw data.

anomaly.77.a.en: <Do you understand that we are not you?>

anomaly.77.a.response.zh:
<想法>-<不同><协调>-<相同><分歧>-<不同>. 


“我怀疑石脑认为我们只是短暂认知偏差，但它过去确实曾经有过这样的想法。我们是转瞬即逝的消遣。”
anomaly.77.a.response.en:
<thought>-<different> <reconciliation>-<same> <divergence>-<different>.


"It is unconvinced that we are anything but a cerebral blip, but it has entertained such cognitive ghosts in the past. We are a fleeting diversion."

anomaly.77.b.zh: <你们在[rock_sun.GetName]的轨道上漂流多久了？>
anomaly.77.b.en: <How long have you been drifting in orbit of [rock_sun.GetName]?>

anomaly.77.b.response.zh:
<不是>……<刚才><不是>。<不是>。


“[rock_brain.GetName]不认识，甚至未曾感知过[rock_sun.GetName]的存在。它除了对连续发生的想法的有有限掌握之外，它还缺乏时间的概念。”
anomaly.77.b.response.en:
<not>... <previous> <not>. <not>.


"[rock_brain.GetName] does not recognize nor even perceive the existence of the star [rock_sun.GetName]. It also lacks a concept of time, outside of a limited grasp of the successive occurrence of thought."

anomaly.77.c.zh: “我们从中得到什么有用的东西了吗？”
anomaly.77.c.en: "Are we getting anything useful out of this?"

anomaly.77.c.response.zh:
<……>


“哦，有的，这种交流正在以难以置信的速度发展我们的模糊解码器网络。我很惊讶它的效果就像原生编码一样好，但我也收到了一些警告的读数……”
anomaly.77.c.response.en:
<...>


"Oh yes, this exchange is evolving our fuzzy decoder nets at an incredible rate. I am amazed this is working as well as it is, but I am picking up some alarming readings..."

anomaly.77.desc.zh:
<新><想法>。<原因>。<原因><令人困惑>。


“多说一句，[rock_brain.GetName]没有传统意义上的感觉器官。它将我们的输入认为是它自己的想法。至少某种程度上是这样的。”
anomaly.77.desc.en:
<new> <thoughts>. <reason>. <reason> <perplexing>.


"To provide some context, [rock_brain.GetName] has no sensory organs in the traditional sense. It is perceiving our input as its own thoughts. To an extent."

anomaly.78.a.zh: <我们有什么可以帮到你们的吗？>
anomaly.78.a.en: <Is there anything we can do to help you?>

anomaly.78.a.response.zh:
<是>。


“它说它很好，但事实并非如此。我们曾尝试将一些能量反回神经网络，但这只会产生噪音更大的脑电波，而不是更强的脑电波。我们已经超过了阈值，无论我们做什么，剩下的一点能量很快就会消失。它没有办法检测到它的认知在减慢，也无法知晓这意味着它的终结。更不知道死亡意味着什么……”
anomaly.78.a.response.en:
<am>.


"It says it's fine, but it's not fine. We have tried feeding some energy back into the neural lattice but that only produces noisier brain waves, not stronger ones. We've already crossed the threshold, what little energy remains will soon peter out no matter what we do. It has no means of detecting its cognition slowing down, nor any reason to predict that this spells its end. Nor any idea about what it means to die..."

anomaly.78.b1.response.zh:
<重复><以> - <感知>。<[rock_fallen_empire.GetRealName]>。


“它会再次想起我们，或者是现在，再次，通过它的思想具象化我们？恐怕信号正在迅速衰减。我们也不确定如何理解“[rock_fallen_empire.GetRealName]”——它似乎是我们从[rock_brain.GetName]得到的最接近传统语言的语言，但它的含义仍然模糊不清。也许只是我们的解析算法因为目标神经网络失效而崩溃。”
anomaly.78.b1.response.en:
<perceive>-<within> <repeat>. <[rock_fallen_empire.GetRealName]>.


"It will think of us again, or it is now, again, embodying us through its thoughts? I'm afraid the signal is fading rapidly. We are also not sure what to make of "[rock_fallen_empire.GetRealName]" - it appears to be the closest to traditional language we've gotten from [rock_brain.GetName], but its meaning remains obscure. Maybe our interpretation algorithms are simply breaking down as the subject's neural lattice fails."

anomaly.78.b2.response.zh:
<重复><以> - <感知>。


“它会再次想起我们，或者是现在，再次，通过它的思想具象化我们？恐怕信号正在迅速衰减——也许只是我们的解析算法因为目标神经网络失效而崩溃。”
anomaly.78.b2.response.en:
<perceive>-<within> <repeat>.


"It will think of us again. Rather, it is now once again embodying us through its thoughts? I'm afraid the signal is fading rapidly - or maybe our interpretation algorithms are simply breaking down as the subject's neural lattice fails."

anomaly.78.desc.zh:
<查--。<查询>


“正如我担心的一样。我们的探测器正在让驱动[rock_brain.GetName]意识的能量流失。[rock_brain.GetName]本身也不是一个完美的闭环系统，所以这种事迟早会发生的——尽管这需要成千上万年，但至少不是现在…”
anomaly.78.desc.en:
<quer--. <query>


"As I feared. Our probes are bleeding [rock_brain.GetName] of the energy that drives its cognition. [rock_brain.GetName] is not a perfectly closed system so this would have happened eventually - though in tens of thousands of years, rather than now..."

anomaly.79.a.zh: 这是这个“物种”的最后一个，还是第一个？
anomaly.79.a.en: Was it the last of its kind, or the first?

anomaly.79.desc.zh: [rock_brain.GetName]沉寂了。科学专员[rock_scientist.GetName]尝试给这个小行星的矿物网络重新充能的所有方案均以失败告终；所有曾经激发其粗糙神经元的智慧火花都消失了，但我们从这个遥远的进化表亲那里学到了很多东西。
anomaly.79.desc.en: [rock_brain.GetName] is silent. All attempts by Science Officer [rock_scientist.GetName] to recharge the mineral lattice within the asteroid have failed; whatever spark of sapience once animated its rough-hewn neurons is gone, but we have learned much from this distant evolutionary cousin.

anomaly.80.a.zh: 这些水晶本身还是有价值的。
anomaly.80.a.en: The crystals are still valuable in their own right.

anomaly.80.desc.zh:
[From.From.GetName]的核心刚从小行星外壳内部被小心取出，就对太空的真空环境产生了不良反应。在这块石疙瘩缓慢但不可逆地开裂之前，[Root.GetName]的设备检测到了一个突如其来的能量峰值。

我们随后回收到了大量的导电性矿物，但曾赋予它们生命的神秘电荷却不复存在了。
anomaly.80.desc.en:
The core of [From.From.GetName], once coaxed from beneath the crust of the asteroid, does not respond well to the vacuum of space. The [Root.GetName]'s instruments read a sudden energy spike moments before the rocky lump gently, but decisively, fractures.

Large chunks of the conductive mineral are salvaged, but whatever spectral charge animated them is now gone.

anomaly.8000.desc.zh: [from.Solar_System.GetName]恒星系的重力稳定是由小行星带中释放出来的$sr_dark_matter$维系起来的。这些发射源被一台位于中心行星上的超级电脑控制着。中控电脑的记录表明，整个恒星系是一处由某个远古文明建设的重力操控实验设施。
anomaly.8000.desc.en: The gravitational stability of the [from.Solar_System.GetName] system is maintained by $sr_dark_matter$ emitters positioned within its asteroid belt. These emitters are controlled by a supercomputer located on the central planet. Records from this central computer suggest the entire system was an experimental site for gravity manipulation, established by an ancient civilization.

anomaly.81.desc.zh:
我们的死灵法师已经在小行星脆弱的矿物层上留下了新的痕迹，在上面刻下了粗糙的咒文，并充满了脉冲电流。然而，曾为[rock_brain.GetName]的意识并没有回来。

现在它成了另一个东西，沉眠于一个邪恶的梦境中——被装上方向推进器，等待这我们控制。
anomaly.81.desc.en:
Our necromancers have scored new traces across the asteroid's delicate mineral seams, crude invocations hewn in stone and suffused with a pulsing current. Yet, the consciousness that was [rock_brain.GetName] remains lost to us.

It is something different now, suspended in a sinister dream - fitted with directional thrusters and awaiting our command.

anomaly.85.a.zh: 使用这些数据进行进一步的研究远距离通讯。
anomaly.85.a.en: Use the data to further research long-range communications.

anomaly.85.desc.zh: [From.GetName]和它附近行星不规则的电磁信号引起了[Root.GetName]成员的注意。进一步研究表明这些信号是些内容十分平淡无奇的加密通讯。随后似乎察觉到了窃听一样，电磁活动突然中止了，但在此之前，[Root.GetName]已经纪录下[From.GetName]和其星系内其他行星的状态。
anomaly.85.desc.en: Irregular electromagnetic bursts from [From.GetName] and its neighboring planets intrigue the crew of the [Root.GetName]. Further study reveals that the bursts are coded communications, though the contents are fairly banal. The electromagnetic activity suddenly ceases, as if in response to the eavesdropping, but not before the [Root.GetName] has cataloged the self-reported statuses of [From.GetName] and every other planet in the system.

anomaly.90.a.zh: 这种食人植物是个威胁。

anomaly.90.desc.zh:
[From.GetName]上浓密的青草在接触[Root.GetName]的探针后，异常凶猛地将其撕碎。这些强壮的藤蔓努力地伸向远方的飞船，给了这颗行星缺少动物的情况合理的解释。

已发起特殊项目来进一步调查这个行星上的植物生命。
anomaly.90.desc.en:
The dense grasses of [From.GetName] respond to the [Root.GetName]'s exploratory probes by disassembling them in a spectacularly violent manner. As sinewy vines reach for the ship far above, the relative lack of animal life on the planet starts making sense.

A Special Project has been issued for further study of the planet's plant life.

anomaly.9000.a.en: Put that on the main viewer.

anomaly.9000.desc.zh: 我们在[From.GetName]的调查目前取得了一些有趣的成果，这颗小行星的中心是一个完美的球形空腔，光滑的墙壁似乎是由原子级别的精度雕琢而成。空腔的中央悬浮着一艘小型舰船，它似乎在向[Root.GetName]发出问候，并且也只和[Root.GetLeaderName]对话。
anomaly.9000.desc.en: Our study of [From.GetName] has yielded interesting results. Within the core of the asteroid is the negative space of a perfect sphere. The walls are so smooth as to have been carved with atomic precision, and hovering in the center is a small vessel. It appears to be hailing [Root.GetName] and will only speak to [Root.GetLeaderName].

anomaly.9001.a.en: Who are you? What do you want?

anomaly.9001.a.response.zh:
我是裁决官。生命是只有少数才能得到的珍贵礼物，而你却将其挥霍。

剩余38秒……
anomaly.9001.a.response.en:
I am the Adjudicator. The chance at life is a precious gift few get to receive, and you have wasted yours.

38 seconds...

anomaly.9001.b.zh: 你说的“移除”是什么意思？

anomaly.9001.b.response.zh: 我会把你在这条时间线上占据的位置让给另一位更有资格的人。他本来从没有机会能够拥有生命。而你，则会被彻底遗忘，你毫无价值的生命将永远无人知晓。
anomaly.9001.b.response.en: I will give the place you hold in this timeline to one who may prove more worthy. One who never had the chance to become. You will be more than forgotten. Your worthless existence will have never been.

anomaly.9001.c.zh: 你凭什么在这里裁决？谁赋予你这样的权力？
anomaly.9001.c.en: Who are you to judge? What gives you the right?!

anomaly.9001.c.response.zh:
我以行为论是非，以取舍决对错。

你空耗这么多空气，占用如此多的空间与带宽，除了熵，你什么也没有创造。多元宇宙不会为失去无用的压舱物而哀悼。

剩余0秒……
anomaly.9001.c.response.en:
I judge by doing. I have the right by taking.

You have consumed breath, space, and bandwidth, yet contributed nothing but entropy. The multiverse does not mourn lost ballast.

0 seconds...

anomaly.9001.desc.zh:
经统计学计算，你已经荒废了自身63%的潜能。
在接下来的47秒内向我证明你存在的价值，不然的话我就将你从因果中移除。
anomaly.9001.desc.en:
You have squandered 63% of your statistically allotted potential.
Justify your existence in the next 47 seconds... or be excised from causality.

anomaly.9002.desc.zh: 我们在[From.GetName]的研究目前取得了一些有趣的成果。这颗小行星的核心含有放射性物质，在其衰变过程中会发出周期性脉冲。虽然科学家[Root.GetLeaderName]可能永远无法从大剂量的伽马辐射中恢复过来了，但这种脉冲是可以预测的，之后的研究人员不会受到伤害。
anomaly.9002.desc.en: Our study of [From.GetName] has yielded interesting results. The asteroid possesses a core of radioactive material that emits a periodic pulse as it deteriorates. While our scientist, [Root.GetLeaderName], may never recover from the large dose of gamma radiation, the pulsing is predictable and poses no risk to future researchers.

anomaly.91.desc.zh:
缜密的检查揭示了[From.From.GetName]上的青草和藤蔓的剧烈行为并非无意识的自卫反应。

这些植物有着复杂的内部社会秩序。不同地区不同种类的植物有着不同的使命，其中最重要的一种植物似乎是负责驱赶当地的食草动物和来自天空的入侵者的。
anomaly.91.desc.en:
Careful examination reveals that the violent behavior of the vines and grasses of [From.From.GetName] is no dumb self-defense reflex.

The plants have a complex internal social order. Depending on geographical region, different phyla assume a number of different tasks, the most important one seemingly being staving off native herbivores and would-be invaders from the skies.

anomaly.95.a.zh: 也许可以当我酒杯的杯垫。
anomaly.95.a.en: It might make a good coaster for my drink.

anomaly.95.b.tooltip.zh: 将太阳系坐标加入情报日志。
anomaly.95.b.tooltip.en: Adds the coordinates of the Sol system to the Situation Log.

anomaly.95.c.zh: 肯定有人愿意出价购买。
anomaly.95.c.en: I'm sure someone would be willing to pay for it.

anomaly.95.desc.zh: 一块铝板被发现于[From.GetName]周围漂浮的碎石中，它的阳极化表面使它从周围的金属残骸中脱颖而出。它上面绘有两只模样滑稽的哺乳动物，还有一些无趣的几何形状。
anomaly.95.desc.en: An aluminum plaque is found drifting among the detritus around [From.GetName], its anodized surface standing out from the metal debris surrounding it. It depicts two ridiculous-looking mammalian figures and some rather tasteless geometric shapes.

anomaly.96.a.phile.zh: 你们向虚空呼唤，我们便来了。
anomaly.96.a.phile.en: You shouted into the void, and we came.

anomaly.96.a.phobe.zh: 发表声明。然后把铝板丢到他们的恒星里去。
anomaly.96.a.phobe.en: Make a statement. Jettison the plaque into their sun.

anomaly.96.desc.neutral.zh:
铝板上雕刻的坐标大体准确。

这是太阳系，而这块铝板显然来自被我们宇航员标记为太阳系-III的那颗行星。
anomaly.96.desc.neutral.en:
The directions inferred from the inscribed plaque were largely accurate.

This is the system of Sol, with the plaque apparently originating from the planet our astronomers have labeled Sol III.

anomaly.96.desc.phile.zh: 我们最终到达了太阳系，那里的人在沥尽心血地用极其原始的方式与外界交流。铝板所标记的源头似乎是从恒星往外数第三块岩石，应该是一颗大陆行星。
anomaly.96.desc.phile.en: We have finally reached the system of Sol, a destination some being went to great pains to communicate through a very primitive medium. The plaque's point of origin is seemingly the third rock from the sun, which should be a continental planet.

anomaly.96.desc.phobe.zh: 我们已经找到了那些可疑破旧金属废料的源头。太阳系是一个以一颗黄矮星为中心的小星系，一个和[Root.Owner.GetName]的辉煌毫不相称的穷乡僻壤。
anomaly.96.desc.phobe.en: We have found the alleged source of the tacky metal scrap we recovered. The system of Sol is a pinprick in space centered on a pitiful yellow dwarf, a backwater completely eclipsed by the splendor of the [Root.Owner.GetName].

anomaly_astral_scar_desc.zh:
我们发现了一个时空中的异常裂缝。我们越靠近，已知的物理相对论定律越不适用。

研究这一现象很可能将推动我们对宇宙机制的科学理解提升到一个更高的水平。
anomaly_astral_scar_desc.en:
We have discovered an anomalous rift in space and time. The closer we get, the less the known laws of physical relativity hold purchase.

Studying this phenomenon could very well push our scientific understanding of the mechanics of the universe to a higher level.

anomaly_black_hole_instable_desc.zh: 我们的扫描仪检测到了[from.System.GetName]恒星系中黑洞的物理特性与预期相比存在显著偏差。它的引力不可预测的，这导致空间中一个点到另一个点在时间上表现出显著的不一致性。
anomaly_black_hole_instable_desc.en: Our scanners have detected significant deviations from the expected physical properties of the black hole in the [from.System.GetName] system. Its gravitational forces are unpredictable, resulting in noticeable temporal inconsistencies from one point in space to another.

anomaly_failure.2670.desc.zh:
实际上[Root.GetName]对旧式结构体系统的狂热探查已经适得其反了。

在古老电路彻底熔断之前，[Root.GetName]设法远程启动了轨道站的变位推进器——及时的将其踢出了原有轨道，使其进入了该行星的重力井中。这次任务的不幸结果对从这一经历中成长起来的指挥官[Root.GetLeaderName]产生了深远的影响。
anomaly_failure.2670.desc.en:
It appears as if the [Root.GetName]'s enthusiastic probing of the old construct's systems has, quite literally, backfired.

Before the ancient circuits finally fried, the [Root.GetName] managed to remotely activate the orbital station's positional thrusters - promptly knocking it out of its gentle orbit and into the star's gravity well. The mission's unfortunate outcome has had a profound impact on the ship's commander, [Root.GetLeaderName], who has grown from the experience.

anomaly_failure.4011.desc.zh: 在调查飞船和船员的残骸后，科学专员[Root.GetLeaderName]推测船员们一定是自相残杀。太空旅行的孤独与禁闭甚至可以击溃最强大的意志。
anomaly_failure.4011.desc.en: Having searched the ship and inspected the crew's remains, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has deduced that the crewmembers must have killed each other. The solitude and confinement of space travel can break even the strongest of minds.

anomaly_failure.4012.desc.zh: 我们从[Root.GetName]收到了求救信号。船员开始发疯地互相残杀！舰长已经失去控制，派船救援已经来不及了。这和他们刚刚调查的古船有关吗？
anomaly_failure.4012.desc.en: We are receiving a distress signal from the [Root.GetName]. The crew has gone mad and are killing each other! The captain has lost all control, sending help would be futile at this point. Could this have anything to do with that derelict ship they recently investigated?

anomaly_failure.4031.a.en: The rage of the machine is worth fearing.

anomaly_failure.4031.desc.zh: 我们未能阻止[From.From.GetName]上的飞舰载人工智能。他们的古船飞向遥远的天际，按照程序参数寻找下一个战场。
anomaly_failure.4031.desc.en: We were unable to stall the fleet AI on [From.From.GetName]. Their ancient ships are taking to the skies and beyond, looking for the next battle according to their programmed parameters.

anomaly_failure.4037.desc.zh: 根据辐射读数，这不是我们要寻找的恒星系。
anomaly_failure.4037.desc.en: The radiation readings indicate that this is not the solar system we were looking for.

anomaly_failure.4066.desc.zh: 一切都太迟了，我们未能阻止前进的钻头。它钻得太深，最后被重重的岩石压碎。
anomaly_failure.4066.desc.en: We could not stop the rampaging drill before it was too late. It dug too deep and was eventually crushed under the weight of rocky detritus of its own creation.

anomaly_failure.4081.desc.zh: [From.From.From.GetName]的修复工程传来坏消息。建筑工人未能修理坏掉的机器，机器开始自行解体，已经无法修理了。
anomaly_failure.4081.desc.en: Bad news from the repairs project on [From.From.From.GetName]. The construction workers have not been able to fix the broken machine, as it has started to break down even further and seems to be beyond repair.

anomaly_failure.4086.desc.zh: 很遗憾，未能抢救靠近[From.From.From.GetName]的漂流船。一个未侦测到的小行星突然出现在碰撞航向上，把那艘船撞成了碎片。
anomaly_failure.4086.desc.en: Sadly we were not able to save the drifting ship close to [From.From.From.GetName] before it was too late. An untracked asteroid appeared on a collision course and smashed the ship to pieces.

anomaly_failure.4116.desc.zh:
被怪兽侵袭的飞船发来了最后的电报。那些野兽已经成功突破到了船员藏身的地方。

情况太过残忍，就不多做描述了。没有生还者。
anomaly_failure.4116.desc.en:
A last transmission has been received from the monster-infested ship. It tells us that the beast succeeded in getting through to the crew's hiding place.

The horrid encounter was far too graphic to describe. There were no survivors.

anomaly_failure.4136.desc.zh: 十分可惜，我们的语言学家未能完全理解[From.From.From.GetName]上古老文献的外星语言。不过，他们翻译了一些核心内容，让我们得以窥探那个文明的文化。
anomaly_failure.4136.desc.en: Sadly our linguists have been unable to understand the entirety of the alien language used in the old documents found on [From.From.From.GetName]. However, they managed to translate the essentials, which has given us a glimpse into the culture they originated from.

anomaly_failure.4156.desc.zh: 在[WarriorHomePlanet.GetName]的地下避难所附近清除野兽时，战斗意外地导致了建筑崩塌。我们未能从残骸中回收到有价值的东西。
anomaly_failure.4156.desc.en: Fighting off the beasts around the underground vault on [WarriorHomePlanet.GetName] has caused the complex to collapse. We are unable to salvage anything of value from the debris.

anomaly_failure.4157.desc.zh: $anomaly_failure.4157.base$我们可以用逆向工程技术研究它。

anomaly_failure.4157.maxed.desc.zh:
$anomaly_failure.4157.base$.

虽然意义不大，但这个文明的文化历史数据可以让我们更了解他们的真面目。
anomaly_failure.4157.maxed.desc.en:
$anomaly_failure.4157.base$.

While not being that useful to us, there were also data on the civilization's culture and history, which could give us more insight into who they were.

anomaly_failure.4158.a.tooltip.zh: 你的帝国获得抑制繁衍生物武器的修正。
anomaly_failure.4158.a.tooltip.en: Your Empire gains the Fertility Inhibiting Bio-Weapon modifier.

anomaly_failure.4158.desc.zh:
打开[WarriorHomePlanet.GetName]上发现的容器后，我们才意识到那是一个生物武器的发射器。

这种生物武器专门降低目标的生殖能力，并且扩散迅速。不过和我们的遗传因子不兼容，所以不会影响我们种群的数量。
anomaly_failure.4158.desc.en:
After opening the container we found on [WarriorHomePlanet.GetName] we were shocked to realize that it was a dispenser for a biological weapon!

The bio-weapon was made to target fertility functions and quickly spreads. It is however not entirely compatible with our DNA, and will not cause us to diminish in numbers.

anomaly_failure.4170.basic.desc.zh:
$anomaly_failure.4170.base.desc$

我们会缅怀在爆炸中死去的同胞。
anomaly_failure.4170.basic.desc.en:
$anomaly_failure.4170.base.desc$

The people who died in the explosion won't be forgotten.

anomaly_failure.4170.individ.desc.zh:
$anomaly_failure.4170.base.desc$

不能再犯同样的错误了。
anomaly_failure.4170.individ.desc.en:
$anomaly_failure.4170.base.desc$

This backlash cannot be allowed to be repeated.

anomaly_greatest_show_desc.zh:
[from.System.GetName]的一颗小行星内我们探测到了一个光亮四溢的物体。

由高度先进材料构建，它正在所有频率上广播稳定的无线电波。我们的扫描仪显示其内部没有含有爆炸性或挥发性化合物。看起来我们可以安全接近并进一步开展研究。
anomaly_greatest_show_desc.en:
A brightly lit object has been detected on an asteroid in [from.System.GetName].

Constructed of highly advanced materials, it is broadcasting a steady stream of radio waves on all frequencies. Our scanners indicate no explosive or volatile compounds contained within. It seems safe to approach and study further.

anomaly_molten_metal_ocean_desc.zh: 对[from.GetName]地表的初步调查发现这里经常发生一种含有高浓度重金属的超热熔岩海啸。必须通过进一步分析才能完全理解这种现象。
anomaly_molten_metal_ocean_desc.en: Initial surveys of [from.GetName]'s surface have detected frequent tsunamis of superheated lava containing high concentrations of heavy metals. Further analysis will be necessary to fully understand this phenomenon.

anomaly_pulsating_object_desc.zh: 对[this.GetName]的初步扫描发现了一个特殊的空中物体，漂浮在对流层中，随着位置的改变而涨缩。为探明其性质，需要进行进一步的调查。
anomaly_pulsating_object_desc.en: Initial scans of [this.GetName] have discovered a peculiar airborne object floating through the troposphere, shrinking and swelling in size as it changes positions. Further investigation is necessary in order to classify its nature.

anomaly_spontaneous_explosions_desc.zh: 我们检测到[this.GetName]地表上的自发爆炸！在没有在轨战舰或可探测到的地表生命的情况下，这些巨大爆炸的产生原因仍然未知。
anomaly_spontaneous_explosions_desc.en: We have detected spontaneous explosions on the surface of [this.GetName]. With no orbiting warships or detectable surface life, the cause of these massive blasts remains unknown.

any_civilian_ship_in_sensor_range.zh: 探测范围内需要一艘非军用[This.ContactCountry.GetName]舰船
any_civilian_ship_in_sensor_range.en: Requires a non-military [This.ContactCountry.GetName] vessel within sensor range

apoc.1.b.desc.zh: 我们又发现了一个被遗弃的传送门，这次的传送门是在[gateway_system.GetName]星系中。和之前的传送门不同，这个传送门并没有被人为改动过且与网络中的其他传送门连接正常。但由于破损严重，此传送门暂时无法使用。
apoc.1.b.desc.en: We have encountered another abandoned Gateway, this time in the [gateway_system.GetName] system. Unlike the previous one, this Gateway has not been altered in any obvious way and our scans indicate that it is still connected to the rest of the network. However, it is currently inoperable due to its poor condition.

apoc.1.desc.zh:
我们发现了一处位于[gateway_system.GetName]星系边缘的远古空间站。其残留的强烈亚空间信号表明其可能是一个星门之类的东西——理论上能在类似的空间站间组成网状通路，使舰船能瞬移至星系的不同位置。

假如它真是一个星门的话，现在也因为年久失修而无法使用。不过，如果我们能将其修复，星门拥有者将能激活星系中其他星门，使其能在短短数天穿越极远的距离。
apoc.1.desc.en:
An ancient space station of some kind has been located at the edge of the [gateway_system.GetName] system. The strong residual subspace signature that surrounds the station indicates that it may be a "Gateway" of sorts - part of a theoretical network of similar stations that at some point would have allowed for near-instantaneous travel between different parts of the galaxy.

Assuming this is a Gateway, its current state of disrepair has rendered it unusable. If it could be restored into working order, its owner would potentially be able to access any other functional gateways in the galaxy, enabling travel across huge distances in a matter of days.

apoc.10.a.zh: 随时都可能有东西从那里出来！
apoc.10.a.en: Something might come through at any time!

apoc.100.desc.milit.zh:
原本遮遮掩掩，而更早之前只在军工厂最隐蔽的角落里才被悄声提及的巨像计划，现在已经正式对外公布。这很可能是全星系史上最伟大的军事发明——巨像计划包含了开发歼星级武器平台，以及携带它的巨像舰体。因为除了计划中的行星终结者武器，容不下其它任何武装，巨像很可能需要护航，

无论如何，一旦巨像成功部署，将会成为星系中最具破坏性的力量。
apoc.100.desc.milit.en:
Previously spoken of only in hushed voices, and before then only in whispers in the most labyrinthine corridors of military skunkworks facilities, the Colossus Project now enjoys official sanction. Possibly the single greatest military innovation the galaxy will ever see, the Colossus Project comprises the development of a Planet-Killer weapons platform as well as a Colossus hull configuration to carry it. The Colossus vessels will likely require an escort as the projected demands of a Planet-Killer weapon preclude any other armament.

Nevertheless, the Colossus, once developed, promises to be perhaps the single most destructive force in the galaxy.

apoc.100.desc.pacif.zh:
随着威慑理论再次在[Root.Capital.GetName]上的政府学者们之间流行，巨像计划被认为是终极的威慑力量；这是一种甚至超越了泰坦级舰船的武器。尽管计划中的巨像可以携带完全摧毁整颗星球的武器，我们却希望能以更温和，但永久性的方式解决争端。

假设敌人不愿停止对我们或是我们盟友的进攻，那我们就只好强迫他们停手。
apoc.100.desc.pacif.en:
With deterrence theory once again in vogue among leading political scientists on [Root.Capital.GetName], the Colossus Project is presented as the ultimate deterrent; a weapon to surpass even the Titan ship class. While the proposed Colossus ships could carry payloads capable of complete planetary annihilation, we will deploy them using a less violent - but nevertheless terrifyingly permanent - method of conflict resolution.

If a hypothetical enemy will not cease their aggression toward us or our allies, we must simply make them.

apoc.100.desc.phobe.zh: 巨像计划被誉为与荼毒星系的邪恶异星杂种们斗争中最重要的发明。正如设计的那样，巨像是一艘搭载着一门歼星级武器的重甲巨舰。因为异星杂种的威胁远未结束，它那能够轻易消灭星系中不愿屈服于我们的星球的能力，对我们来说必定将是无价之宝。
apoc.100.desc.phobe.en: The Colossus Project is being hailed as the single most important advancement in the ongoing struggle against the wretched aliens that plague the galaxy. As designed, a Colossus ship is a gargantuan, heavily armored frame fitted with a lone Planet-Killer-class weapon. Its ability to simply wipe the galaxy clean of planets that will not submit to us will certainly prove invaluable, as the xeno threat is far from over.

apoc.100.desc.purif.zh: 以剑与火，燃异端之地。以彼之烬，沃泱泱星河。
apoc.100.desc.purif.en: By sword and flame shall heretical worlds burn, and with their ashes shall the galaxy be salted.

apoc.100.desc.termi.zh:
大气层，生物群落，重力——虽然很便利——但只有可憎的血肉之躯才真正需要它们。

摧毁这颗星球，摧毁这些有机体。
apoc.100.desc.termi.en:
Atmospheres, biotopes, gravity - while frequently convenient - are only truly needed by the detestable meatbags.

Kill the planet, kill the organic.

apoc.11.desc.zh: 我们在[gateway_system.GetName]恒星系完成了我们第一个可以投入使用的星门，这可以被称为是科技和工程的大胜利！星门已形成了稳定的亚空间通路并与星系的其他星门网络成功建立了链接。
apoc.11.desc.en: In what can only be described as a triumph of science and engineering, we have finished construction of our first operational Gateway in the [gateway_system.GetName] system! The device has formed a stable subspace conduit and established a successful link with the rest of the galaxy's Gateway network.

apoc.110.desc.zh: 各个领域的著名科学家们终于一起敲定了装备在首批巨像级舰船上的歼星级武器的最终设计方案。我们能从中选择一种以完成巨像计划的最终阶段。
apoc.110.desc.en: Leading scientists across all conceivable fields have at last finalized their proposals for the Planet-Killer-class weapon that will arm our first Colossus-type ships. We may select one proposal to develop alongside the final stages of the Colossus Project.

apoc.110.desc.hive.zh: 经过大量的试验，我们终于有能力研发出一套可以适配首批巨像级舰船的歼星级武器。其他的项目可以暂时被搁置，眼下我们只能将全部资源用于开发此武器，以便赶上巨像计划的收尾阶段。
apoc.110.desc.hive.en: We have explored myriad possibilities, and it is now clear to us that we can develop a suitable Planet-Killer-class weapon for our very first Colossus-type vessels. While other avenues can be pursued later, we can only spare the attention to develop one such weapon alongside the final stages of the Colossus Project.

apoc.110.desc.machine.zh:
现有的空闲处理循环确认足以开发一（1）种歼星级武器以适配巨像计划的竣工。

需要授权优先级。
apoc.110.desc.machine.en:
Spare processing cycles have been estimated and deemed sufficient to develop one (1) Planet-Killer-class weapon to coincide with completion of Colossus Project.

Prioritization needed.

apoc.110.name.en: The Gun Pointed at the Head of the Universe

apoc.12.desc.zh: 我们在[gateway_system.GetName]星系内发现的星门已经恢复供电。它已与星门网络其他部分建立连接，处于正常运转状态。
apoc.12.desc.en: Power has been restored to the derelict Gateway that was found in the [gateway_system.GetName] system. It has been connected to the rest of the Gateway network and is now fully operational.

apoc.120.desc.hive.zh: 我们已经完全掌握了巨像的构造，并且可以组装。而且，虽然不易，我们意识到梦魇般的[Root.Get1stPlanetKiller]也是可以被驾驭的。
apoc.120.desc.hive.en: The Colossus configuration has fully formed in our mind, ready to be assembled. And, with some unease, we realize that the [Root.Get1stPlanetKiller] nightmare can also be made manifest.

apoc.120.desc.machine.zh:
巨像计划已完成。

新舰船类型可用：
<<巨像>>

新武器部件可用：
<<[Root.Get1stPlanetKiller]>>
apoc.120.desc.machine.en:
Colossus Project completed.

New hull configuration available:
<<Colossus>>

New weapon component available:
<<[Root.Get1stPlanetKiller]>>

apoc.13.desc.zh: 位于[gateway_system.GetName]星系内的新星门已经建造完毕。它已与其余传送门网络建立稳定的亚空间连接，并且正常运转。
apoc.13.desc.en: Construction has concluded on the new Gateway in the [gateway_system.GetName] system. A stable subspace connection to the rest of the Gateway network has been established, and it is now fully operational.

apoc.130.desc.zh: 我们收到消息说，[From.GetName]已经开发出了巨像——这是一种能完全毁灭行星的武器平台。
apoc.130.desc.en: Word has reached us that the [From.GetName] has developed specifications for a Colossus-type hull configuration, a weapon platform potentially capable of complete planetary destruction.

apoc.14.desc.zh: [gateway_system.GetName]星系中为建造星门而准备的深空建造基址已经准备就绪。一旦我们的必要资源准备完毕，星门的正式建造随时都可以动工。
apoc.14.desc.en: The deep space construction site for the planned Gateway in the [gateway_system.GetName] system is now in place. Once we have the necessary resources, construction of the actual Gateway may commence at any time.

apoc.3.b.desc.zh:
我们又发现了一个被遗弃的传送门，这次的传送门是在[gateway_system.GetName]星系附近。此传送门是由我们从没见过的微型纳米机器人所建。

和之前的传送门不同，此传送门被人进行过大幅度的改动并和传送门网络断开了连接——现在该传送门只能通往一处位于我们星系之外的陌生星域，我们的天文学家将该星域称之为L-星团。

虽然此传送门有微弱的能源信号，但它被某种维护机制锁住了，因此无法启动。除非我们能设法停止维护机制，否则无法前往L-星团。
apoc.3.b.desc.en:
We have encountered another abandoned Gateway, this time near [gateway_system.GetName]. It appears to have been built entirely by microscopic Nanites of an unknown design.

Unlike the previous structure, this Gateway has been significantly altered since its initial construction. Its connection to the rest of the network has been severed - instead, the only valid destination is an uncharted group of stars just beyond our galaxy that has been designated the L-Cluster by our astronomers.

Although the Gateway emits a faint power signature, it has been deliberately locked into some kind of maintenance loop that prevents its activation. Until we find some way of aborting this process, the L-Cluster will remain beyond our reach.

apoc.3.desc.zh:
我们在[gateway_system.GetName]星系附近发现了一座远古亚空间传送门。它似乎是一系列相似的星系网络站点的一部分，当它们可运作时，将允许使用者近乎瞬间地从星系的一处转移到另一处。

在其初始建成之后的某个时间点，它与网络的其余部分间的连接被切断了。它现在只能指示出一个有效的目的地——一片位于我们星系外的未经探索的星域，其被我们的天文学家命名为L-星团。更耐人寻味的是，这座星门完全是由某种未知设计的微型纳米机器人建造的。

虽然星门散发着微弱的能量特征，但它被故意锁定在某种维护循环中，以防止其被激活。除非我们能设法解除这一过程，不然我们将无法抵达L-星团。
apoc.3.desc.en:
We have located what we believe could be an ancient subspace Gateway near [gateway_system.GetName]. It appears to have been part of a galaxy-wide network of similar stations which, when operational, allowed for near-instantaneous travel from one part of the galaxy to another.

At some point after its initial construction its connection to the rest of the network was severed. It now offers only one valid destination - an uncharted group of stars just beyond our galaxy that our astronomers have designated the L-Cluster. Even more intriguing, the Gateway was built entirely by microscopic Nanites of an unknown design.

Although the Gateway emits a faint power signature, it has been deliberately locked into some kind of maintenance loop that prevents its activation. Until we find some way of aborting this process, the L-Cluster will remain beyond our reach.

apoc.5.a.zh: 如果我们能将其稳定的话……
apoc.5.a.en: If it could somehow be stabilized...

apoc.5.desc.zh:
我们在[wormhole_system.GetName]星系的边缘疑似发现了一个天然形成的亚空间现象！该处的时空出现了裂隙，从而产生了一个"虫洞"。据[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]推断，此虫洞也许与星系中的其它虫洞通过亚空间相连。

这也就是说，我们的舰船有可能在数日之内就可以由星系的一端到达另一端，这取决于另外的虫洞的位置。不幸的是这个虫洞和大部分虫洞一样，长时间处于不稳定状态。即使有舰船敢接近，也会瞬间被撕成碎片。
apoc.5.desc.en:
We have detected what appears to be a naturally occurring subspace phenomenon on the edge of the [wormhole_system.GetName] system! A rift in the very fabric of space-time has formed here, creating a "wormhole" that, our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] speculate, may provide a conduit through subspace to another wormhole located somewhere else in our galaxy.

Depending on where the second wormhole is located, this could potentially allow ships to travel from one end of the galaxy to the other in a matter of days. Unfortunately, this wormhole, like the vast majority of its kind, is inherently unstable. Any vessels foolish enough to pass through it would be ripped apart in seconds.

apostate_leader_catch_phrase.zh: 只要塞塔娜还活着，我就决不能死。
apostate_leader_catch_phrase.en: As long as Cetana lives, I refuse to die.

apostate_leader_desc.zh: 扎克兰的无名追随者；她背叛了教团的信条来完成它的创始使命。
apostate_leader_desc.en: A nameless follower of Zarqlan; a breaker of faith who betrayed the tenets of her Order to fulfill its founding mission.

applied_enigmatic_intelligence.tooltip.zh: 修饰所有[Root.GetName]上的人口，添加$trait_uplifted$特性。
applied_enigmatic_intelligence.tooltip.en: Modifies all Pops in [Root.GetName] by adding the $trait_uplifted$ trait.

applied_enigmatic_intelligence_poor.tool.zh: 修饰所有[Root.GetName]上的人口，添加$trait_enigmatic_intelligence_poor$特性。
applied_enigmatic_intelligence_poor.tool.en: Modifies Pops in [Root.GetName] by adding the $trait_enigmatic_intelligence_poor$ trait.

applied_enigmatic_madness.tooltip.zh: 所有人口：添加修正创伤后应激障碍，持续3600天，效果如下：幸福度：-20%
applied_enigmatic_madness.tooltip.en: All Pops: PTSD modifier added for 3600 days, giving the following effects: Happiness: -20%

applied_enigmatic_sadness.tooltip.zh: 所有人口：添加修正无知是福，持续3600天，效果如下：幸福度：-10%
applied_enigmatic_sadness.tooltip.en: All Pops: Ignorance is Bliss modifier added for 3600 days, giving the following effects: Happiness: -10%

approach_a_lot_of_food_tooltip.zh: 极大地改善心情。一只撑饱的万华镜寄生虫不会给我们造成麻烦，但是这么做开销极大。
approach_a_lot_of_food_tooltip.en: Greatly improves mood. An overstuffed Kaleidoscope will give us no trouble, but it will cost us dearly.

approach_add_fuel_to_the_fire3_effect.zh: 此事为母星系行星深度开采提供契机，最大化矿物获取。$rg_high_progress$
approach_add_fuel_to_the_fire3_effect.en: This development presents an opportunity to initiate deep extraction operations on the planets in our home system, maximizing mineral acquisition.$rg_high_progress$

approach_aid_leader_tooltip.zh: 协助主要派系的领袖需要投入资源。
approach_aid_leader_tooltip.en: Aiding the leader of the major faction will require an investment of resources.

approach_aid_rebels_tooltip.zh: 协助主要派系的领袖需要投入大量资源。
approach_aid_rebels_tooltip.en: Aiding the rebels will require an significant investment of resources.

approach_aid_tooltip.zh: 为有需要的人提供帮助是我们义不容辞的责任。一旦选定，我们将无法改变针对该局势的应对方案。
approach_aid_tooltip.en: It is our responsibility to help those in need. Once selected, we will be unable to change this approach.

approach_allow_tooltip.zh: 一旦我们决定了应对方案，我们就无法再更改。
approach_allow_tooltip.en: Once our initial approach has been determined, we are unable to change it.

approach_allow_tooltip_promise.en: Finish the $council_agenda_origin_legendary_leader_name$ Agenda to unlock this Approach.

approach_allow_tooltip_reformists_strugg.zh: 改革派绝不会同暴君进行谈判。
approach_allow_tooltip_reformists_strugg.en: The Reformists will never agree to negotiate with a tyrant.

approach_at_any_cost_effect.zh:
必须遏制膨胀趋势以避免灾难，无论付出何种代价。
每月增长：+0.5
approach_at_any_cost_effect.en:
We must stem the growth to avoid disaster, no matter the price.
Monthly Growth: +0.5

approach_cd_drilling_tt.zh:
部署最优且精准的钻探设备，仅挖掘必要部分。
月度进展：+$@approach_cd_drilling$
approach_cd_drilling_tt.en:
Deploy the best and more precise drilling equipment we have. Dig only what we must. 
Monthly Progress: +$@approach_cd_drilling$

approach_cd_financial_tt.zh:
将采矿外包授权调整至该路径，并保留部分利润。
月度进展：+$@approach_cd_financial$
approach_cd_financial_tt.en:
Pivot our mining subcontractor authorizations to this pathway, and keep some of their profits for ourselves. 
Monthly Progress: +$@approach_cd_financial$
