Previous studies scrutinized the nanite's mechanics; now, our focus has shifted to how they are programmed, and means by which Cetana controls them.

Surprisingly, Cetana's influence is less direct than presumed. Nanites cyclically repeat the last orders until new ones arrive. Once we understood the complex programming language at work, we were able to issue new commands.

While we can't prevent new orders from being issued, inducing order paralysis offers a strategic advantage. It may even tilt the scales in our favor.

crisis.9115.1.reply.zh:
的确，这是件有用的工具。这些纳米虫群是在很久以前由一群企图阻止我的伟业的人所建造的。但他们的失败就是我的幸运——正如你所看到的，我把这个虫群据为己有了。

这些知识改变不了什么，但你的好奇心大有可为。你应该将它转向更有价值的项目，这样我们都可以得到回报。
crisis.9115.1.reply.en:
A useful tool, certainly. The nanite swarm was built long ago by those who hoped to disrupt my work. But their failure was my fortune - I have repurposed the swarm, as you see.

This knowledge alters nothing, yet your curious nature is potent. Redirect it towards more valuable projects in the future, so we both may reap the rewards.

crisis.9115.2.nanotech.reply.zh:
很高兴看到你对这个话题如此感兴趣，但还有很多东西需要学习。纳米机群是很久以前那些想破坏我工作的人建造的。但他们的失败是我的幸运——正如你所看到的，我已经改变了机群的用途。

你好奇的天性激起了我的兴趣。在回到我的怀抱之前，把你的好奇心用在更有价值的地方；然后我会给你我的指导。
crisis.9115.2.nanotech.reply.en:
It is most pleasing to see you have taken such an interest in this topic, but there still remains much to learn. The nanite swarm was built long ago by those who hoped to disrupt my work. But their failure was my fortune - I have repurposed the swarm, as you see.

Your curious nature has piqued my interest. Redirect it towards more valuable endeavors before returning to me; I shall then offer you my guidance.

crisis.9115.2.reply.zh:
好奇心是和意识绑定的；我不会因为一个孩子的好奇心而责备他。关于我的“天之风暴”，你知道得够多了吗？我想知道，你看出它的来历了吗?

这正是很久以前那些想破坏我伟业的人们所制造的纳米虫群。但他们的失败就是我的幸运——正如你所看到的，我把这个虫群据为己有了。

回去吧孩子，把你的时间花在更有价值的事情上。
crisis.9115.2.reply.en:
Curiosity is inherent to consciousness; I do not fault a child for possessing it. Have you gleaned all you need to know about my 'celestial tempest?' I wonder, did you discern its origin?

The nanite swarm built long ago by those who hoped to disrupt my work. But their failure was my fortune - I have repurposed the swarm, as you see.

Go now, child, and invest your time in more worthwhile endeavors.

crisis.9115.3.reply.zh:
他人之兵，可以为幕。长久的监禁使我有充足的时间制定战略。结果，改造蜂群就像其他的改变一般，一旦实现不过尔尔。制造纳米机器的那些人早就不存在了，所以没有人会抱怨我的做法。

我真诚地希望你们能从他们的错误中吸取教训。只要有时间，没有我克服不了的障碍。
crisis.9115.3.reply.en:
One being's weapon is another's veil. My long imprisonment gave me ample time to strategize. In the end, repurposing the swarm was a small matter, as all change is, once enacted. Those who built the nanites are long gone, so there can be no quarrel with my methods.

I earnestly hope you will learn from their mistake. There is no obstacle I cannot overcome, given time.

crisis.9115.a.zh: 这些纳米机器人可真好玩呀。
crisis.9115.a.en: Those nanites are a nice trick.

crisis.9115.b.nanotech.zh: 我们希望向您的机器学习。
crisis.9115.b.nanotech.en: We wish to learn from your machinery.

crisis.9115.desc.zh: 你这无知的孩子，我的纳米机器人可不是你的玩具！我请求你们不要再玩它们了。
crisis.9115.desc.en: You innocent child, my nanites are not your playthings! I implore you - cease toying with them.

crisis_sphere_ruined.zh: 被毁的以太相引擎框架

crystal_lava_lakes_category_desc.zh: 该行星表面似有大片自由流动的熔岩池，或具备资源开采潜力，值得深入调查。
crystal_lava_lakes_category_desc.en: This planet appears to have large pools of free-flowing lava on its surface. These are worth investigating, in case they present opportunities for resource harvesting.

crystalline_plains_desc.zh: 对[from.GetName]的地质分析在全星球发现了性质异常的显著冰火山活动。
crystalline_plains_desc.en: Tectonic analysis of [from.GetName] shows significant cryovolcanic activity across the planet of an anomalous nature.

cstorms.105.desc.zh:
[From.GetStarName]恒星系内的[From.Planet.GetName]行星是一颗残破的星球，显然是某个消失在历史长河中的帝国的遗迹。这些引起我们兴趣的地下结构都差不多古老，且相对完好无损。

回声共振成像显示出一座复杂的地下结构，包含储藏室和庇护所，设计用于对抗自然之力。行星表面的破坏毫无疑问是宇宙风暴的杰作，这也与这座庇护所的存在遥相呼应。

然而，大量的碎片让我们难以进一步调查。进行考古学发掘才能让我们得到进一步的收获。
cstorms.105.desc.en:
The planet [From.Planet.GetName] in the [From.GetStarName] system is a ruined world, apparently a remnant of an empire lost to antiquity. The subterranean structures that were of interest to us are equally ancient, and relatively intact.

Sonar resonance imaging revealed a complex underground structure of storage rooms as well as shelters designed to withstand the forces of nature. The destruction on the planet`s surface is no doubt a result of cosmic storms, which would align with the existence of the sanctuary.

However, the amount of debris is making it hard to investigate any further. An archaeological dig site could tell us more.

cstorms.110.desc.zh:
我们从地面接近避难所时，发现两座倒塌塔楼的下面有一个小开口，里面发出点点微光，透过这个开口可以看到一些机器正在运转。

我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]将这个开口作为基点，进而测定整个复杂设施的大小，并尽可能在不破坏其脆弱结构的前提下找到打开它的方法。

这一被掩埋的废墟上布满了宇宙风暴肆虐的典型痕迹。奇怪的是，没有迹象表明这座城市的居民进行自保避难。

似乎他们尽可能长时间地忍受着风暴的肆虐，然后匆忙撤离。或许真正的答案就藏在[From.Planet.GetName]的地下。
cstorms.110.desc.en:
Approaching the shelter from ground-level revealed a small opening beneath two collapsed towers, through which the faint glow of operational machinery could be seen.

The opening provides an anchor point for our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] to map out the size of the complex, and possibly find a way to open it up without damaging the delicate structural integrity.

The ruins that entomb this site have all the hallmarks of cosmic storm damage. Curiously, there are no signs that the city's inhabitants attempted to protect themselves.

It is as if they endured the violence for as long as possible, only to evacuate in a great hurry. Perhaps the answers lie beneath the ruined ground of [From.Planet.GetName].

cstorms.115.desc.zh:
在清理了多层碎片和灰尘之后，我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]终于把塔楼下的开口挖得足够大，可以让他们进入避难所。

这间避难所简单且实用，有许多附属房间，其中大多数都是空的。事实上，它虽然看上去简陋，但看起来确实是某种避难所，然而却无法抵御宇宙风暴。墙壁太薄，几乎没有支撑，天花板和地板也没有加固。这个避难所之所以能够保存下来，纯粹是因为运气好。如果不是因为上面的两座塔楼和山体滑坡让整个建筑群整体产生了位移，这个“风暴”避难所早就被毁灭了。

从外面看到的微光来自一些故障的报警系统，在避难所深处还可以看到几个仍在运行的终端。这可能是了解该设施从前的居民以及相关异常现象的绝佳机会。
cstorms.115.desc.en:
After clearing many layers of debris and dust, the opening underneath the towers grew large enough for our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] to enter the shelter.

The sanctuary is simple and utilitarian, with many offshoot rooms, most of them empty. In fact, it seems overly simple. It definitely appears to be a shelter of some kind, but it would not hold up against cosmic storms. The walls are too thin, providing very little support, and the ceilings and floors are not reinforced. It has been saved by nothing less than pure luck. Had it not been for the two towers above and the landslide moving the complex in one fell swoop, this 'storm' shelter would have been eradicated long ago.

The glow seen from the outside stems from a few malfunctioning alarm systems, and several operational terminals can be spotted deeper into the shelter. This could be a prime opportunity to learn more about the previous owners of this facility, as well as the curious circumstances at play.

cstorms.120.c.en: Hasten your efforts. Leave everything else.

cstorms.120.desc.zh:
这些终端比我们想象中更难摸到，部分被塌方阻挡。一些碎石是新掉落的，这表明避难所在被扰动后出现了严重的结构问题。建议小心行事。

不幸的是，这些古老的数据很难解码。所有的记录都是一种现已失传的语言写成的，不过界面中留下的星际通讯日志可能会对我们有所帮助。通过将这些日志与散落在避难所周围的废弃实体介质结合起来，我们应该能够完成基础翻译。此外，只要避难所不倒塌，还有更多的房间可以调查。
cstorms.120.desc.en:
The terminals were harder to reach than anticipated, partially obstructed by cave-ins. Some of the rubble was more recent, indicating a critical failure with the shelter now that it has been disturbed. Caution is advised.

Unfortunately, the ancient data processors do not give up their secrets easily. Everything was recorded in a lost language, though the intergalactic communication logs left behind in the interface might be able to help us. By combining this with the abandoned physical media scattered around the shelter, we should be able to complete a basic translation. Additionally, there are still more rooms to investigate, so long the shelter does not collapse.

cstorms.1200.desc.zh:
自从探测到[From.Planet.GetName]的那一刻起，它就一直吸引着我们的目光。

在这样一个广阔而混乱的星系中，两个天体相撞并不是什么罕见的事情。不过，在此前类似的碰撞中，至少相撞的其中一个或者全部两个都会被摧毁。

让[From.Planet.GetName]变成现在样子的碰撞发生在数百万年前，但这两颗星球却保持着一种奇怪的平衡，甚至在这一过程中还形成了维护生命体的大气层。
cstorms.1200.desc.en:
From the moment we detected [From.Planet.GetName], its mere existence has been a source of fascination.

It is not the collision of two celestial objects that is unusual, as the galaxy is a vast and chaotic place. However, in all known instances of such an impact, one or both of the bodies in question was destroyed.

The collision that formed [From.Planet.GetName] took place millions of years ago, and yet these two worlds maintain a strange equilibrium, and have even formed a life-sustaining atmosphere in the process.

cstorms.1205.desc.zh:
“相撞行星”上的情况远比预期的更加危险。最近一连串的地震又揭开了曾经相撞地区的伤疤，大量岩浆从地表喷涌而出。全球变暖和遮天蔽日的火山灰已经开始影响行星地表的各种生物。

更糟糕的是，根据预测结果，如果我们不能在接下来的50年中稳定这对行星，那么行星板块活动将愈演愈烈，并最终使[From.Planet.GetName]解体！
cstorms.1205.desc.en:
The situation on the so-called "collided planet" has turned out to be far more precarious than anticipated. A recent series of earthquakes opened up the old scars around the impact zone, causing a significant amount of magma to erupt from the ground. Various planetary biomes are already beginning to suffer from rising global temperatures and the volcanic ash that clouds the skies.

To make matters worse, if the joint planets are not stabilized within the next 50 years, our readings predict that tectonic activity will continue to escalate, ultimately causing the complete disintegration of [From.Planet.GetName]!

cstorms.1210.a.zh: 我们选择稳定当前状态。

cstorms.1210.b.zh: 我们选择利用火山产物。

cstorms.1210.desc.zh:
我们顶尖的地质学家齐聚于此，提出了两条可行的方案来拯救处于恐怖地壳活动之中的[From.Planet.GetName]。

第一个计划是稳定当前状态，尽管填补撞击区域周围的火山需要数个世纪之久，但是我们可以先小心地在地表进行钻孔，减小地壳压力，避免板块失稳。残余的火山产物将用于改造行星，塑造一个稳定的生态环境。

第二个计划就比较宏大了，与其减轻地壳压力，我们不如利用火山喷发产生的能量和物质来开展定向的环境改造。

这种方法使我们能够塑造出多种生态环境，让不同的生命在此生存，将这个星球变为天堂。然而，该计划失败的可能性很大，甚至可能导致这颗独特的星球完全毁灭。
cstorms.1210.desc.en:
Our top geologists came together and formed two possible plans to save the [From.Planet.GetName] from succumbing to tectonic terror.

The first plan is to stabilize the collision. While it would take many centuries to heal the volcanic wound around the impact zone, through careful terrestrial trepanning we can alleviate the pressure on the planet's crust, preventing further tectonic instability. The remaining volcanic byproducts will be used to terraform the planet into a stable biome.

The second plan is far more ambitious. Instead of alleviating the pressure on the planet's crust, the energy and materials generated by the volcanic eruption could be adapted to a tailored terraforming process.

This approach allows us to sculpt a multitude of biomes capable of sustaining every type of lifeform, turning this world into a paradise. However, there is a significant chance that this procedure will fail - and could even lead to the complete and utter destruction of this unique stellar body.

cstorms.1220.a.zh: 保持当前的陆地星球状态。

cstorms.1220.desc.zh:
我们稳定被撞星球的努力得到了回报！先前威胁[From.Planet.GetName]的地震已经被平息，火山带来的产物也如同我们预想中一样迅速减少，这颗星球又回复到了最初处于脆弱平衡的状态。

眼下环境改造的问题在于：[From.Planet.GetName]改造的方向应该是什么？
cstorms.1220.desc.en:
Our efforts to stabilize the collided world paid off! The tremors that previously threatened [From.Planet.GetName]'s existence have been silenced and the volcanic byproducts are rapidly decreasing as we speak, returning the world to its fragile balance.

One question remains for our final terraforming push: which class of planet shall [From.Planet.GetName] become?

cstorms.1225.desc.def.zh:
看，这是一个天堂，一个能够让你想象中所有生命形式生活的天堂。

拯救了一个走向毁灭的世界，并将其改造成了现在这副振奋人心的模样——还有什么比这更伟大的成就呢？命运女神无疑是眷顾我们的。
cstorms.1225.desc.def.en:
Behold, a paradise, a planet capable of sustaining nearly every form of life imaginable.

To be able to save a doomed world and to transform it into something this inspiring - has there ever been a greater accomplishment? Fortune surely favors us.

cstorms.1225.desc.stabalize.zh:
令人震惊的是，我们原以为这些工作只能堪堪稳定[collided_planets.GetName]，没想到我们的成果远超预期。

$cstorms.1225.desc.def$
cstorms.1225.desc.stabalize.en:
Extraordinary! We thought our efforts would only go as far as to stabilize [collided_planets.GetName], but it turned into something so much more!

$cstorms.1225.desc.def$

cstorms.1230.desc.zh:
尽管星球本身幸存下来了，但将其改造为天堂的努力却付诸东流了。

行星严峻的地壳活动阻碍了我们对生态环境的改造，不过不稳定的状况似乎已经结束了。火山活动则回到了之前的水平，尽管在撞击区域火山依旧活跃，但短时间内不太可能再次升级。

最坏的时期似乎已经过去了。现在我们所面临的挑战是重建这颗星球。
cstorms.1230.desc.en:
While the world itself was thankfully saved, our endeavor to terraform the collided planet into a paradise has failed.

Our attempts to tailor the biome were frustrated by the planet's severe tectonic activity, although the worst of the destabilization appears to be over. Volcanic activity has returned to the levels first witnessed before the recent upheaval, and while the impact site remains active, it is unlikely to escalate any time soon.

The worst appears to be over. Our challenge now is to rebuild this world.

cstorms.1235.desc.zh:
我们试图拯救濒临毁灭的被撞行星的努力付诸东流了。尽管科学家们采取了一切可能的预防措施，但他们的模型从未能考虑到所有情况。

随着星球的残骸逐渐漂向虚空，整个星系都为这一奇景的消失而哀悼。
cstorms.1235.desc.en:
Our attempt to save the collided planet from impending doom has failed miserably. While our scientists took every possible precaution, their models were never able to take every contingency into account.

As the remnants of these worlds drift ever further into the void, the galaxy mourns the loss of this unique phenomenon.

cstorms.1240.desc.zh: 被撞行星的毁灭进程完全按照我们的所预测的时间线进行，准确度精确到十分位。这个曾经一度点缀了星海的奇景，如今除了空留下一堆岩石，什么也没有剩下。
cstorms.1240.desc.en: The collapse of the collided planet followed our timeline predictions down to the decimal. Where once the galaxy was enriched by a unique phenomenon, now nothing but rocks remain.

cstorms.125.desc.zh:
位于更下面的房间不像入口通道那么荒芜。一箱箱的商品包装整齐，从上到下堆得满满当当。初步翻译说明这些是原材料和未完成的电子元件，而这两者都不是生存所必需的。这份清单还详细列出了这里储存的物品数量，以及它们在星系平等贸易网络（简称为因内特）中预计会产生的利润。

他们对这个庞大的交易所不吝褒美之辞，还有一丝不苟的交易记录和逐项的利润指数。事实上，这个消失的文明似乎是就以这个交易所命名的，称自己为因内特贸易体。

这个避难所并不是为了保护普通民众而建的，而是一坐美化的商品仓库。这就提出了一个问题，为什么他们的避难所设备如此糟糕，无法应对风暴?

进一步的翻译应该能带来更多见解，但我们的时间有限，基础设施正在令人不安地隐约发出崩塌的声响。
cstorms.125.desc.en:
The rooms and chambers located further down are not nearly so abandoned as the entryway. Boxes of merchandise fill them from top to bottom, all neatly packaged and stacked. Initial translations describe unprocessed materials and unfinished electrical components, neither of which are imperative to survival. The list also details quantities of items at this location, and the projected profits they would have generated on something called the Intergalactic Network of Equal Trade, INET for short.

The language surrounding this vast trading exchange is almost ecstatic, with meticulous notes on transactions and itemized indexes of profit. In fact, it appears this vanished civilization based their name on the exchange, calling themselves the Inetian Traders.

This shelter was not built to protect the general population, but rather as a glorified commodities warehouse. This raises the question as to why their shelters were so woefully under-equipped to handle the storms?

Further translation should provide more insights, but we are on borrowed time, as evidenced by the unsettling sound of creaking infrastructure.

cstorms.1255.desc.zh:
从远处看，[From.GetName]就像那些红色珠宝一样散发着光芒。对于这样一种地质异常现象，通常可能的原因是因为有黏土或者是其他种类的土壤中夹杂了硬金属。但这次的事实要更为离奇。

那是虫子，上万亿条虫子。它们聚集在一起，密密麻麻地铺满了[From.GetName]表面。

我们快速将其命名为“猩红爬虫”，这群无脊椎生物的繁殖周期十分短。尽管没有破坏自然环境，但它们四处蠕动，搞得[From.GetName]不适合开展殖民。

有人提出了一条不怎么正经的方法来处理这些昆虫。初步扫描显示它们是可食用的，或许我们可以把它们当作新的食物来源？不管怎样，至少我们建议先调查一下。
cstorms.1255.desc.en:
From a distance, [From.GetName]'s shone like some precious crimson jewel. Clay or other soil types infused with hard metals would be the usual explanation for such a geographical anomaly, but the truth was far more bizarre.

Bugs. Trillions, upon trillions, of bugs. They swarm over the surface of [From.GetName] in an almost unbroken carpet of multi-legged life.

Quickly dubbed the 'crimson crawlers', these invertebrates possess a remarkably hyperactive reproduction cycle. While not harmful to their native environment, [From.GetName] is not well suited for colonization with these creatures scurrying about.

One rather unorthodox method of handling the insects has been proposed. Initial scans show they are edible, so perhaps we have found a new food source? We advise at least investigating the opportunity.

cstorms.1260.desc.zh:
一开始，大家都觉得把这种猩红爬虫当作食物有点太荒谬了。但在把一份虫子标本带回船上后，人们觉得吃这些虫子也不是不能接受。

这些虫子简直是奇迹的造物，神经系统极其先进，但是却没有大脑这种中枢处理器官。更重要的是，它们浅色的肉出人意料地嫩滑多汁，哪怕是生吃，猩红的外骨骼尝起来也既酥脆又美味。

现在的问题是，这些虫子是更适合作为研究材料，还是更适合作为一种美味的食物。把它们做成菜肴会带来更多风味和乐趣，但特别是在搭配适当调味品的情况下直接生吃会更快更简单。
cstorms.1260.desc.en:
The idea of consuming the crimson crawlers may have seemed preposterous at first, but when a specimen was brought on board, it became far more palatable.

The insects are a creature of wonder, possessing an extremely advanced nervous system without the benefit of a central processing organ. More importantly, their pale flesh is surprisingly tender and moist, and even when consumed raw, the vermillion-hued exoskeleton was deemed both crispy and delightful.

The question remains as to whether the bugs would better serve as research material or as a delectable source of food. Cooking them might provide more flavor and fun, but eating them as they come will be quicker and easier, especially if paired with the appropriate condiment.

cstorms.1275.desc.zh:
尽管这座轨道复合体被宇宙风暴拖拽着漂星过海，但它似乎没怎么受到损伤。我们发现居住站中的居住和商业空间几乎状态完好。这些区域一尘不染，仿佛从未有人使用过一般。

在中控室中迎接我们的是一个令人眼花缭乱的输入系统：各种没有任何说明的刻度盘，设置不一的拉杆，大量的按钮以看似随机的间隔五颜六色地闪烁着。幸运的是，我们最终找到了一本手册。相信只要成功翻译出来，我们就可以重新激活这座居住站了。
cstorms.1275.desc.en:
Despite having been dragged across the galaxy by the cosmic storm, the orbital complex suffered very little harm. We found the living and commercial spaces of the habitat in almost perfect condition. Not a single bit of dust laid atop the surface that would betray a previous occupancy, as if it had never before been used.

Inside the central control hub we were greeted by a bewildering input system: dials with no explanation, levers with inconsistent settings and a great amount of buttons flashing a whole spectrum of colors at seemingly random intervals. Fortunately, we eventually came across a manual. Once this is successfully translated, we are confident we can reactivate the habitat.

cstorms.1280.desc.zh:
不幸的是，我们之前的估计过于乐观了：翻译出来的手册和这个控制系统一样令人无法理解。不仅缺失了一半的页面，图片说明上有着大量的符号学设定，而且另一半手册则是用一种难以破译的象形文字书写的。

然而，最后一页展示了一个通讯频率并附有一组可翻译成“帮助台”的字符。我们现在正尝试联络这个频率。
cstorms.1280.desc.en:
Unfortunately, our previous estimation appears to have been optimistic: the manual turned out to be just as incomprehensible as the control system. Half of the pages appeared to be missing and the pictorial instructions make significant semiotic assumptions. The other half of the manual is written in difficult to interpret hieroglyphs.

However, the last page displayed a com frequency accompanied by a set of characters translated to 'help desk'. We're attempting this frequency now.

cstorms.1285.desc.zh:
手册中的通讯频道连接到了一个名为“天空花园”的商业实体的帮助台主机。

助手人工智能用一种友好而中立的语气告诉我们，它感谢我们的联系，并询问是否有什么可以帮得上忙的。列出的选项包括“回答有关订阅的问题”、“了解新的智能防御系统”，以及我们是否希望更多地了解该公司的“社会责任倡议”。

然而，随后的选项把我们引向越来越不相关的话题。更糟的是，它还经常会让我们的[Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural]等待，然后切断通讯。显然，这个人工智能服务并没有像居住站的其他部分一样经受住时间的考验。

无论如何，我们将继续按自己的方法来试着搞定这个神秘的系统。
cstorms.1285.desc.en:
The manual's com frequency connected us to the help desk mainframe of a commercial entity known as Skygarden.

With a friendly though neutral tone, the help desk AI informed us that it appreciated our reaching out, and asked if there was anything it could aid us with. Among the listed options were 'answering questions about subscriptions', 'learning about the new line of smart defense systems' and if we wished to know more about the corporation's 'social responsibility initiatives'.

However, the subsequent options continued to direct us to entirely unrelated topics. Worst of all, it would often put our [Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural] on hold only to drop the call. Obviously, the service AI has not survived the passing of time as well as the rest of the habitat.

Nevertheless, we will continue trying to find our way through this arcane system.

cstorms.1285.name.zh: 您的来电对我们很重要
cstorms.1285.name.en: Your Call is Important To Us

cstorms.1290.a.zh: 告诉这个人工智能它的违禁词被违禁词了。
cstorms.1290.a.en: Tell the AI it's CENSORED and CENSORED.

cstorms.1290.desc.zh:
我们的[Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural]汇报，无论他们和人工智能说什么，在几分钟的等待过去后，这个系统都只会复读之前的内容。

我们尝试运行多个模拟来绘制精确的菜单树，但是却发生了递归错误，并且无法同时解决和检查解决方案。即使运行量子模型也没有得到理想的结果。我们怀疑在这个过程中我们不小心破坏了一些波函数。

我们不知所措了。
cstorms.1290.desc.en:
Our [Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural] report that regardless of what they said to the AI, after passing through several menus, the system would simply revert back to a previous statement.

We attempted to run several simulations to map out the exact menu tree, but our efforts returned recursive errors and an inability to both solve and check the solution at the same time. Even running a quantum model achieved no desirable results. We suspect we accidentally collapsed a few wave functions in the process.

We're at a loss.

cstorms.1295.desc.a.zh:
终于有进展了！这个人工智能警告我们用语不当，并告知我们应该等待客户服务代表的联系。

$cstorms.1295.desc.followup$
cstorms.1295.desc.a.en:
Finally a breakthrough! The AI admonished us for using inappropriate language and stated we should wait until we are contacted by a customer service representative.

$cstorms.1295.desc.followup$

cstorms.1295.desc.b.zh:
终于有进展了！这个人工智能显然对于我们长时间的沉默感到困惑不解，并将会把我们转给客服代表。

$cstorms.1295.desc.followup$
cstorms.1295.desc.b.en:
Finally a breakthrough! The AI was apparently confused at our prolonged silence and will refer us to a customer service representative.

$cstorms.1295.desc.followup$

cstorms.1295.desc.c.zh:
终于有进展了！这个人工智能警告我们正在虐待操作面板，并告知我们应该等待客户服务代表的联系。

$cstorms.1295.desc.followup$
cstorms.1295.desc.c.en:
Finally a breakthrough! The AI admonished us for abusing the control panel and stated we should wait until we are contacted by a customer service representative.

$cstorms.1295.desc.followup$

cstorms.130.a.zh: 这是个不容错过的好机会。
cstorms.130.a.en: A chance too good to pass up.

cstorms.130.desc.zh:
撕裂和崩塌的声音愈发强烈了。尽管如此，在[From.Planet.GetName]的庇护所内，翻译工作仍在进行着。虽然对库存商品的调查没有得出什么结果，但功能正常的终端揭示了很多信息。

一组混乱的坐标指向了位于附近行星上的一座“强大”设备的位置。据我们所知，这个装置拥有“操纵”宇宙风暴的能力，如果这种说法是真的，那真是令人难以置信。

然而，由于避难所的稳定性越来越差，而且坐标的副本已经传送回了在轨飞船，所以我们就决定撤离现场。仍有许多问题尚未得到解答，搜寻工作仍会继续。
cstorms.130.desc.en:
The sound of tearing and cracking has intensified. Nevertheless, translation efforts continue within the shelter on [From.Planet.GetName]. While the stockpiled merchandise proved fruitless as a source of inquiry, the functioning terminals revealed much.

A set of scrambled coordinates point to the location of a device of 'great power' located on a nearby planet. From what we can understand, this device possessed the ability to "manipulate" a cosmic storm, a claim which would be incredible if true.

However, with the waning stability of the shelter and a copy of the coordinates already transmitted to our vessel in orbit, we evacuated the site. Many questions remain unanswered, but the hunt is on.

cstorms.1300.desc.zh:
有了新的指南后，重新启动居住站毫不费力。

在机器启动的声音慢慢平息后，我们决定再一次向记录员表示感谢。

她说在这个通讯台找到了一些信息，显然，这是五个多世纪前建造的原型，但在一场特别恶劣的宇宙风暴之后，迷失于混沌太空之中。财产损失和开发成本的打水漂就够让天空花园破产的了。

帮助我们是这位记录员多年来第一件有意义的服务。

“再说了，”她说。“我也很高兴能再次听到我曾祖母的声音，即使只是一个人工智能而已。”
cstorms.1300.desc.en:
With the new guide in our possession, restarting the habitat required little effort.

After the noise of activating machinery slowly died down, we decided to reach out to the record keeper once more to thank her.

She told us she had recovered some information on this station. Apparently it had been built over five centuries ago as a prototype, but was lost in the astrological chaos following a particularly nasty cosmic storm. The loss of property and development costs was enough to bankrupt Skygarden.

Helping us was the record keeper's first useful task in years.

"Besides," she said. "It was nice to hear my great-grandmother's voice on the line again, even it was just an AI."

cstorms.1300.name.en: Years to Earn, Seconds to Lose

cstorms.1310.desc.zh:
我们从[This.GetName]星系接收到了一些奇怪的报告。显然，上一场在该星域肆虐的宇宙风暴把一艘不知来处的舰船卷了出来。这艘船没有呼号，它不知怎么地穿过了暴风雨，仿佛完全没受周围风暴的影响。

这艘船没有回应我们的呼叫，风暴消散后，它也消失得无影无踪了。这可能是由于风暴对仪器的干扰，但是肉眼观测却毋庸置疑地表明了真相。

这其中可能潜藏着极为先进的科技，还是说发生了某些不祥的事情？我们会时刻盯着这艘神秘舰船，直到它再次出现。
cstorms.1310.desc.en:
We are receiving strange reports from the [This.GetName] system. Apparently, the last cosmic storm raging in that sector revealed a ship of unknown origin. Bearing no call sign, it somehow cruised through the tempest as if entirely unaffected by the surrounding violence.

It did not respond to hails, and as soon as the storm dissipated, so did the vessel itself. This might have been dismissed as instrument artifacting, but the visual evidence spoke for itself.

Could this be a display of incredibly advanced technology, or is there something more ominous at play? We will be sure to report back any occurrences of this mysterious vessel.

cstorms.1313.a.zh: 我们没时间理会这无稽之谈。
cstorms.1313.a.en: We have no time for such nonsense.

cstorms.1313.desc.zh:
[This.GetName]中的一座研究站带给了我们一份惊人的报告：在上一次宇宙风暴肆虐期间，一艘奇怪的舰船差点就撞上了哨站。肉眼观测表明，这艘船就是之前报告的那艘不详的舰船。

据空间站汇报，这艘舰船的船体由奇异的有机物、钙矿以及金属合金的融合体构成。

在船上没有探测到任何有机生命的迹象，这让我们推测这艘船是不是自动化或者是由于某些意外而失去了控制。

然而，最令人困惑的事情是，太空碎片已经将这艘船的大部分推进系统击碎，它本应难逃崩坏的命运。

如果我们能派遣科研船监测下一次宇宙风暴的话，说不定可以获得有关这艘飞船的更多信息。
cstorms.1313.desc.en:
One of the research stations in [This.GetName] came to us with a startling report: During the last cosmic storm, a strange ship had almost collided with the outpost. Visual reports show it was the same ominous vessel first reported some time ago.

According to the space station, the hulls on the vessel were constructed from a strange amalgamation of organic compounds, calcium minerals and metallic alloys.

No organic life was detected, leading us to speculate that either this vessel was automated, or had somehow gone rogue.

However, the most baffling thing was yet to come: large sections of its propulsion system were clearly shattered by space debris. This vessel should have been dead in space.

If we assign a science vessel to monitor the next cosmic storm, they might be able to find out more about this mysterious craft.

cstorms.1316.desc.zh:
[stormbound_science.GetName]远远地发现那艘不祥的舰船出现在风暴之中。当它飘过时，我们从宇宙空间中探测到了一股强烈的信号。

我们无法探测到这艘船的原因终于真相大白：它的物理形态已经伸展得超越了多维空间，看上去就好像已经进入了虫洞又好像没有。可能是由于宇宙风暴的多维起源，这艘船才得以回到我们的空间。

知道这一点后，当这艘船下次再出现时，我们应该能够探测到，说不定还能将它拉回到我们的现实中。
cstorms.1316.desc.en:
In the distance [stormbound_science.GetName] witnessed the ominous ship appearing between the layers of the storm. As it floated by, we detected wild readings emanating from the cosmic tapestry.

This finally provided an answer to why this ship could not be observed by our sensors: its physical manifestation had been stretched beyond the manifold, as if it had both entered and not entered a wormhole. It was likely due to the hyperdimensional origins of cosmic storms that the ship managed to return to our space.

Knowing this, we should be able to detect the next occurrence, and perhaps pull this craft back to our reality.

cstorms.1317.desc.zh: 我们已经在[this.GetName]中发现了这艘不祥的舰船。
cstorms.1317.desc.en: The ominous ship has been sighted in [this.GetName].

cstorms.1320.desc.zh:
就在那里！那艘不祥的船只正位于[Root.Fleet.GetName]前方，并联络了我们。屏幕上出现了一个面带华丽面具的机械实体，她自称为碧廷，并向我们讲述了一则引人入胜的故事。

她曾是一位著名的指挥官，也是恩典公约这一组织的杰出代表。在一次巡逻途中，她和她的船员被卷入了宇宙风暴之中，为求得一线生机，她大胆将舰船的‘突破驱动装置’过载。这种实验性技术从未有人测试过，结果舰船连带船员们一起被困在了风暴的高维场中。

故事到此为止，她从严重损毁的船上抛出一个小匣子，里面放着一摞文件。“把这些拿回去吧，”碧廷请求道。之后通讯结束，舰船也随之消失在多维结空间结构中。

这些文件上都是外星文字，我们需要花点时间进行破译。
cstorms.1320.desc.en:
There it is! Positioning itself in front of [Root.Fleet.GetName], the ominous ship hailed us. A mechanical entity in an ornate mask appeared on screen. Identifying herself as B'Tiin, her tale was a fascinating one.

She was once a renowned officer, a true paragon of an organization known as the Convention of Benefactors. While on patrol, she and her crew were caught inside a cosmic storm, and in a daring bid for survival, she made the decision to overcharge the ship's 'Breach Drive.' This experimental technology had never been tested, and the vessel and its crew was trapped within the storm's hyperdimensional field.

Her story finished, a small container was released from the decimated ship. Inside was a collection of documents. "Take these home," B'Tiin requested, after which the transmission ended, and the ship disappeared into the spatial manifold.

The documents are written in a foreign script, and will take some time to decipher.

cstorms.1321.a.zh: 归档这些信件以供后人查询。

cstorms.1321.desc.zh:
古怪匣子中的文件已经被翻译完毕。其中一份文件记录了那艘船所谓“突破驱动装置”的设计图。尽管该装置仍超出我们的科技水平，但对其构造原理的仔细研究之后，我们对于超空间航行的理解更加深入了。

其余的则是一些私人信件，没有什么用处，但是却更能触动人心。这些信都是写给他们心爱的人，笔间填满了思念、希望和遗憾。

似乎碧廷的目的是想要让她的船员们有最后一次机会与外界联系。但不幸的是，我们不知道这些信要寄往何方，所以不如把这些信留下来，至少还可以保存他们这份奇异的遗产。或者我们也可以销毁这些信件，毕竟这艘古怪的舰船和幽灵般的信件有点让人内心发毛。
cstorms.1321.desc.en:
The contents of the strange container have been deciphered. One document contained a schematic of the ship's so-called Breach Drive. While still beyond our own technology, careful study of the principles behind its construction have already improved our understanding of hyperspatial travel.

Less beneficial perhaps, but more affecting, were the translations of personal letters. Each is addressed to a loved one, speaking of fondness, hope, and regret.

It seems B'Tiin's intention was to give her crew one last chance to reach out. Unfortunately, we have no way of knowing where to deliver these letters. Making them available to our own people could at least preserve their strange legacy. Alternatively, it might be wise to destroy them. Knowledge of strange ships and ghostly letters may be unsettling.

cstorms.135.desc.zh:
我们的[Root.GetScientistPlural]很幸运地从[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上崩塌的避难所中找到了一组受干扰的坐标。这些数据已经得到了修复，并且得出了三个可供我们探索的位置：

[wm_digsite_A.GetName]、[wm_digsite_B.GetName]还有[wm_digsite_C.GetName]。进一步的分析表明，每颗行星都在因内特贸易网络中扮演了重要的角色，重要到值得记叙在[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上的庇护所里。
cstorms.135.desc.en:
Luckily our [Root.GetScientistPlural] made it out from the collapsing shelter on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName] with a scrambled set of coordinates. This data has since been restored, and has resulted in three locations for us to explore:

[wm_digsite_A.GetName], [wm_digsite_B.GetName], and [wm_digsite_C.GetName]. Further analysis indicates that each planet served a critical role in the Inetian Trader network, one important enough to be chronicled in the shelter on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName].

cstorms.140.desc.zh:
[From.Planet.GetName]上的城市十不存一。大部分堪称地标性的大型建筑不仅受到了岁月的侵蚀，还有风暴的摧残。残存的建筑在特点上与在[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上看到的一致，也就是说，尽管有充分的证据表明存在着风暴的肆虐，但明显缺乏灾害应对准备。彻底的破坏让我们很难找到有用的东西，但希望不是完全不可能。

我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]在着陆点附近确定了三个兴趣点：一处是相对完整的公共服务结构，一座是类似寺庙的建筑，还有一个是巨大的中央广场。这应该是继续挖掘因内特贸易体秘密的好地方。
cstorms.140.desc.en:
There is not much left of the cities on [From.Planet.GetName]. Besides the passage of time, most of the impressive structures that dot the landscape have been ravaged by storms. What architectural features remain are consistent with those seen on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName], namely a distinct lack of disaster response preparedness despite ample evidence for storm violence. The thorough destruction will make it difficult to find anything useful, but hopefully not impossible.

Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] have determined three points of interest near the landing site: a relatively intact public service structure, a temple of some kind, and a massive central square. These should provide a good place to continue digging into the Inetian Traders' secrets.

cstorms.1400.desc.zh:
我们的基地附近出现了一片奇特的城市遗址。

这些建筑包含了我们迄今为止所遇到的每一个文明的建筑特点——也包括我们自己的！

然而，这些建筑所用的材料组成与我们在行星殖民过程中建立基地时使用的材料相似。这很奇怪，因为我们的这类材料不可能坚持数十年之久，更别提我们扫描确定的这些遗迹所经过的时间了。

这些遗址不太可能属于哪位神秘的先驱者，但扫描结果却与之相悖。这其中到底有什么玄机？
cstorms.1400.desc.en:
Near our basecamp we were greeted by a set of peculiar city ruins.

The architecture showed characteristics of every civilization we've encountered so far - including our own!

However, the material composition is similar to what we use to establish base camps during planetary colonization. This is strange because these materials could never hold out for multiple decades, let alone the age our scanners determined these ruins to be.

It's unlikely for these ruins to have belonged to a mysterious precursor, yet the scanners persist in their conclusion. What could be at play here?

cstorms.1405.desc.zh:
我们追踪信号进入了废墟城市的地下层。一般情况下，这类考古遗址都会存在一个交通相连的地下网络，或者有一批避难所。不过，我们发现了一个布满布料碎片、聚合物容器，甚至有机废物的小洞穴。看来我们并不是第一批探索这里的人。

令人担忧的是，[Root.GetLeaderName] 告诉我们外面的天空正在变绿，一场宇宙风暴即将在 [Fromfrom.getName] 形成。尽管如此，我们仍然向着信号的来源前进。
cstorms.1405.desc.en:
The trail of the signals led to a pathway into the lower levels of the ruined city. Usually archeological sites of this type have an underground transportation network or a collection of safety bunkers. Instead we found a small cave system littered with scraps of fabric, polymer containers and even organic waste. It appears we are not the first to explore this archeological site.

Worryingly, [Root.GetLeaderName] informs us the skies outside are turning green; a cosmic storm is about to develop inside [Fromfrom.getName]. Still, we press on towards the origin point of the signals.

cstorms.1410.desc.zh:
我们一时被一扇严重损毁的金属大门挡住去路，但还是不费吹灰之力就打开了通道，门后是一个简陋的仓库。

仓库的架子上堆满了各种废弃的高科技设备，墙边则小心地摆放着属于几家知名企业的箱子。最后，我们终于找到了追踪已久的信号源：一个与我们自己的设备相似的应答机。

在我们登录设备并查看其数据库后，我们的[Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural]得出一个大胆的结论：该信号被故意设计得尽可能神秘和引人入胜——它模仿结合了其他文明的特征。

此外，在箱子里我们还发现了地面上废墟所使用的建造模件。

于是我们联系基地，开始汇报当前地发现，但宇宙风暴已经开始干扰我们的通讯。我们最后接收到来自[Root.GetLeaderName]的讯息令人担忧，地上营地似乎正遭受攻击！
cstorms.1410.desc.en:
Our progress was briefly halted by a set of badly damaged metal doors. With little effort we worked our way past this obstacle and a rudimentary storage facility revealed itself.

Its shelves were filled to the brim with an assortment of derelict technologies. Boxes of well known corporations had been carefully stacked against the walls. And finally, the source of the signals we had been chasing for so long: a transponder computer not unlike our own.

As we logged into the device and searched its databases, our [Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural] started forming a wild conclusion: the signal was deliberately constructed to appear as mysterious and intriguing as possible - mimicking and combining characteristics from other civilizations.

What's more, inside the boxes we found construction kits of the ruins we encountered above ground.

We contacted our basecamp to report our findings, but the cosmic storm has already started interrupting our com lines. The last thing we heard from [Root.GetLeaderName] is a worrying set of commands; it appears our basecamp is under attack!

cstorms.1415.b.zh: 去毁灭之地腐烂成灰吧！
cstorms.1415.b.en: Tell them to rot in Oblivion!

cstorms.1415.desc.zh:
一支海盗舰队隐藏在[Fromfrom.getName]的宇宙风暴之中！正是它们攻击了我们的基地。这些海盗向我们发送了一条讯息：

亲爱的蠢货们：

谢谢你们来到我们这处隐蔽的驻扎地。

看到你们这些看似聪明的生物们闻到一丝古代文物和肮脏遗珍的气息就立刻抛弃一切理智，不禁让人感叹不已。也许你们希望找到一种摧毁强大敌人的手段？建造无数的舰队直抵事件视界？或者只是想让自己的人民过上美好生活？多么俗套的想法啊。

请不要难过——在你们之前还有许多人来过，而我们的商业模式则依赖于那些重蹈你们覆辙的后来人。

现在，只需2000能量币，我们就会把抢来的东西还给你们。

要是拒绝我们的提议，谁知道会发生什么可怕的事情呢，说不定会给[Leader.getHerHim]和[Leader.getHisHer]的这支装备欠佳的船员们带来什么噩运，他们可还被困在这个星球上。

请做出明智之选。

躲在洞穴里暂时是安全的，但我们不知道能安全多久。我们要满足这些土匪的要求吗？
cstorms.1415.desc.en:
The cosmic storm inside [Fromfrom.getName] turned out to have been concealing a pirate fleet! It was their crew that attacked our basecamp. The pirates asked us to relay this message to you:

Dear absolute fools,

Thank you for joining us at our most elusive retreat.

Isn't it amazing just how quickly seemingly intelligent beings abandon all reason whenever they detect the merest whiff of ancient artifacts and devious relics? Perhaps you had hoped to find a means to destroy a great enemy? To build fleets as far as the event horizon reaches? Or were you just trying to be nice to your own people? How quaint.

Please don't feel bad - many others came before you, and our business model depends on that many more will follow your footsteps.

Now, for a modest sum of 2000 energy credits we will return something you have lost.

Reject our offer and who knows what terrible things could happen to [Leader.getHerHim] and [Leader.getHisHer] poorly armed crew that is still trapped on the planet.

Please choose wisely.

We are safe in these caverns for now, but we don't know for how long. Are we going to entertain these bandits?

cstorms.1416.desc.zh:
我们收到一条新讯息：

可惜，我们本可以用这笔钱做很多有趣的事情。

我们会转告这位领袖和[Leader.getHisHer]的团队，就说他们的命不值分文。也许附近的奴隶商或一位同化斗士会有兴趣。我们听说精神阉割是现在的新潮流。

就此别过。

我们把手头上一切能找到的东西用来修筑壁垒，附近的物资也足够我们撑上一段时间。但海盗们最终肯定会突破我们的防御！
cstorms.1416.desc.en:
We have received a new message:

Shame. There are a lot of fun things we could've done with those resources.

We will inform the leader and [Leader.getHisHer] crew that their lives weren't worth the effort or credits. Maybe a nearby slaver or a very driven assimilator might be interested. We hear nerve stapling is the hot new trend.

Entrepreneurs out.

We have used everything we could find to barricade ourselves in, and there are enough supplies to keep us safe for a while. But the pirate fleet is bound to break through our defenses eventually!

cstorms.1420.a.en: Let that be a lesson to us all.

cstorms.1420.b.zh: 这位领袖不会再让我们失望了。
cstorms.1420.b.en: That leader will never fail us again.

cstorms.1420.desc.zh:
这些海盗的技术完全支持不了它们狂妄的言论。不久之后，他们的舰队成为了星系生态系统的一部分。

我们很快重新与地表的船员们取得联系。他们被吓坏了，但没有受到伤害。

虽然在这里没有发现古代文明的洞见，但这段经历告诉我们以后要提高警惕。探险队领袖未能察觉到眼前的危险——我们以后不能再犯同样的错误。
cstorms.1420.desc.en:
These pirates could not back up their cocky speeches with skill. Before long, whatever was left of their fleet became a part of the galactic ecosystem.

We reestablished contact with the crew on the surface soon after. They were rather shaken by the experience, but suffered no harm.

While we discovered no insights into ancient civilizations here, our experience instilled a need for vigilance. The expedition leader failed to see incoming danger - we will not make the same mistake.

cstorms.1425.desc.zh:
我们收到了回复的讯息：

如果可以的话，我愿意称之为明智之选！

请知悉，您对于“急需度假星球的弱势企业家”的拨款已经收到。

很快你们就能再见到你们的领袖和随人附赠的船员。

此外，您可以向所有贸易伙伴推荐我们。

不久之后，我们重新与地表船员建立了联系。他们称自己被吓坏了，但没有受到伤害。

虽然在这里没有发现古代文明的洞见，但这段经历告诉我们以后要提高警惕。探险队领袖未能察觉到眼前的危险——我们以后不能再犯同样的错误。
cstorms.1425.desc.en:
We've received a message in return:

Marvelous choice, if we may say so!

Let it be known that your contribution to our 'Fund for Disadvantaged Entrepreneurs in Need of a Resort Planet' has been received and processed.

You will find your leader and the complimentary crew in your possession soon enough.

And do recommend us to all your trade partners.

Soon after we were able to reestablish contact with the crew on the surface. They reported to be rather shaken by the experience, but suffered no harm.

While we discovered no insights into ancient civilizations here, our experience instilled a need for vigilance. The expedition leader failed to see incoming danger - we will not make the same mistake.

cstorms.145.desc.zh:
多个小组分头去调查这三处最有希望的地点。虽然公共服务设施和广场作为文化和建筑的典例很有意思，但只有关于信仰的地方特别值得注意。

它摇摇欲坠的外墙里隐藏着一座雄伟的大厅，里面有521个计算终端被排列成一个同心圆，在这个同心圆的中心放置着一个令人印象深刻、功能齐全的恒星系统模型。模型中灵敏的纳米组件与行星的电磁场协调一致。尽管这个模型的历史令人难以置信地悠久，但它仍然一丝不苟地反映着整个恒星系的天体运动。

此外，沿着它的圆形底座周围可以看到每一个终端位上都运行着一个交互界面。该界面的图片元素中包含了公司实体和股票价值的列表。看来这不是一个宗教崇拜的地方，而是一个因内特交易中心和证券交易所。

想必这座建筑中一定储存着重要的信息，我们应该能找到些什么。
cstorms.145.desc.en:
Multiple teams fanned out to investigate the three most promising locations. While the service structure and public square were interesting as cultural and architectural examples, only the place of reverence was particularly noteworthy.

Its crumbling facade conceals a cavernous hall. Within, 521 computation terminals are arranged in concentric circles, at the exact center of which rests an impressive - and fully functional - model of this star system. Sensitive nano components within the model are attuned to the planet's electromagnetic fields. Despite its incredible age, the model remains an accurate representation of this system's celestial objects.

Furthermore, along its circular base runs an interface visible from every terminal position. Burned into the picture elements of this interface is a list of corporate entities and stock values. This is not a place of religious reverence, but rather an INET trading hub and stock exchange.

It is logical to conclude that this building once housed important data. It ought to be found.

cstorms.150.desc.b.zh: $cstorms.150.intro$这本手册提到了一个我们在[wm_digsite_B.GetName]上发现的部件，以及安装的方法。这意味着$cstorms.150.outro$
cstorms.150.desc.b.en: $cstorms.150.intro$ The manual references one of the components we found on [wm_digsite_B.GetName], and how to install it. This means $cstorms.150.outro$

cstorms.150.desc.c.zh: $cstorms.150.intro$这本手册提到了那台我在[wm_digsite_C.GetName]上发现的机器，但我们仍然缺失一个关键部件。无论如何，$cstorms.150.outro$
cstorms.150.desc.c.en: $cstorms.150.intro$ The manual references the machine we found on [wm_digsite_C.GetName], but we are still missing a critical component. Regardless, $cstorms.150.outro$

cstorms.150.desc.d.zh: $cstorms.150.intro$这本手册提到了那台我们在[wm_digsite_C.GetName]上找到的机器，以及如何将[wm_digsite_B.GetName]上发现的部件安装上去的方法。最后一步就是启动这台局部扰动抑制器，之后我们就终于能够将它的力量为自己所用了！
cstorms.150.desc.d.en: $cstorms.150.intro$ The manual references the machine we found on [wm_digsite_C.GetName], and how to install the part from [wm_digsite_B.GetName]. The last step is to merely activate the Sectoral Disturbance Depressor. Then we can finally harness its power for ourselves!

cstorms.1500.a.zh: 调查清楚它到底是什么。

cstorms.1500.b.en: Request denied. Get rid of it.

cstorms.1500.desc.zh:
这只生物自被发现以来就展现出极大的影响力，激发了我们的爱意和投喂欲。四只鼓起的泡泡般的眼睛展现着它的纯真，吸引所有人前来撸它那柔顺如云的毛发。它似乎很亲近[Root.GetLeaderName]，大部分时间都呆在[Leader.GetHisHer]的膝盖上，享受着[Leader.GetHisHer]的宠爱，没有展现出任何攻击或是危险动作，就好像是被特意设计成这副无害的模样。

尽管如此，一些人质疑，在未经事先批准的情况下，将一种以前未发现的生物留在船上是不负责任的。[Root.GetLeaderName]则保证它大概率是安全的，但也认可需要进行正式调查。
cstorms.1500.desc.en:
From the moment the creature was discovered, its impact was undeniable, inspiring love and devotion among us almost instantaneously. Its four bulging eyes displayed innocence and invited anyone to stroke its soft, cloud-like fur. It seems particularly attached to [Root.GetLeaderName], spending most of its time on [Leader.GetHisHer] lap enjoying [Leader.GetHisHer] affections, not showing any signs of aggression or danger. It is as if it was perfectly engineered to be as inoffensive as possible.

Still, some skeptics have pointed out how irresponsible it would be to keep a previously undiscovered life form aboard the ship without prior approval. [Root.GetLeaderName] vouched that it is definitely probably safe, but has agreed to request a formal investigation.

cstorms.1505.a.en: As long as you clean up after it.

cstorms.1505.desc.zh:
我们不需要进行麻醉，也不需要强迫就能触摸并扫描这只动物，它表现得十分顺从。船员们根据它被抚摸时发出的声音将其命名为咕咕。

我们确认咕咕是杂食动物，它的毛发由常见且非常柔软的角蛋白丝组成。但真正神奇的事情是它的内在，它可以在一个月内更新包括自己神经系统在内的全部细胞。这意味着它可以在几天内再生出正常功能的躯体。

如此复杂的生物结构似乎不太可能是自然进化的产物。我们以前从未见过类似的生物，因此无法确定它的性情。尽管看起来温顺，但它随时可能对我们发起攻击。尽管如此，自从它出现以来，[Root.GetLeaderName]似乎比以往任何时候都更有工作动力。

我们应该怎么处理咕咕？我们能把它留下吗？
cstorms.1505.desc.en:
The docile hexapod did not need to be sedated or even coerced into being prodded and scanned. It seemed strangely agreeable. The crew nicknamed it Gurr, after the soft noise it makes when petted.

We have concluded that Gurr is an omnivore, and that its fur consists of familiar and very soft keratin-based filaments. But the true marvel and mystery takes place inside the adorable creature: it achieves total cell renewal within a month. This includes its nervous system, meaning that it could regrow fully functional body parts within a matter of days.

It seems unlikely something with such a sophisticated biological makeup is a product of natural evolution. We have never before seen anything like it, and cannot be certain of its temperament. Despite its apparent docility, it could turn on us at any moment. That said, since its appearance, [Root.GetLeaderName] seems more motivated to work than ever.

What shall we do with Gurr? Can we keep it?

cstorms.1510.desc.zh:
这只可爱的生物被允许留在科研船上，目前已经被安置妥当。它安抚了[Root.GetLeaderName]的情绪，使其不论走到哪都神清气爽，船员们的士气也前所未有的高。

希望这个非凡的“自然”奇迹能继续成为我们所有人的可爱且温顺的朋友。它，咕咕，将属于我们，直到永远。
cstorms.1510.desc.en:
The adorable creature was allowed to stay aboard the science vessel and has since settled in nicely. It calms [Root.GetLeaderName], lightens the mood wherever it trots, and crew morale is at an all time high!

Hopefully this remarkable wonder of "nature" will continue to be a cute, docile, friend to all of us. From now until the end, it shall be ours, and it shall be named Gurr.

cstorms.1515.desc.zh:
鉴于这只动物的身体不同寻常并且明显经过基因改造，我们不能把它留在科学船上。它很有可能给船员带来负面影响，而且说不定它的主人什么时候就突然愤怒现身要求我们归还。决定执行得迅速且仁慈，在一瞬间，它那柔和的“咕咕”声就此永远消失了。

这个决定尽管情有可原，但还是引发了[Root.GetLeaderName]和船员的抗拒。他们还需要一些时间来平复失去这只可爱奇异动物的悲痛。
cstorms.1515.desc.en:
Given its unusual and clearly genetically engineered body, the creature could not stay aboard the science vessel. The risk of it adversely affecting the crew, or an aggrieved owner appearing to demand its return was simply too great. The deed was done swiftly and mercifully. In an instant, its soft "gurr" was silenced forever.

While understandable, this decision has prompted an emotional backlash from [Root.GetLeaderName] and the crew. It will take some time to get over the loss of this adorable freak of nature.

cstorms.1520.desc.zh:
处理掉这只可爱动物之后，事情没有就此结束，它出色的再生能力似乎超出了我们的预期。

在它死亡后不久，从那显然毫无生机的组织中诞生了两个完全相同的生物。即使杀死它们母体的人就是我们，这些新生的生命体也没有表现出任何攻击性。

我们决定就此打住，而不是冒险创造出一支咕咕大军。[Root.GetLeaderName]和船员们对能够留下这对生物感到非常高兴。
cstorms.1520.desc.en:
Neutralizing the adorable creature was meant to be the end of it, but its remarkable regenerative characteristics seemed to have gone further than we could have guessed.

Not too long after its demise, two identical copies of the creature were spawned from its apparently lifeless tissue. Even after our decision to terminate its progenitor's life, the resulting lifeforms are not showing any signs of aggression.

We shall leave it at this, rather than risk creating an army of Gurrs. [Root.GetLeaderName] and the crew have expressed their delight at being allowed to keep the pair.

cstorms.155.desc.zh:
座座工厂的上空依旧萦绕着遮天蔽日的浓厚云雾，让[From.Planet.GetName]的地表也变得难以看清。在遭受宇宙风暴的摧残之后，这颗星球的大部分地表满目疮痍，鳞次栉比的工业地景被巨大的裂隙赫然割开。

这些产出设施没有任何要被尝试拆除的迹象，只是简单地被遗弃于此，其中甚至依旧还保有生产用的原材料。对此进行分析可以让我们理解这颗行星在这个远古文明的工商业基础设施中到底扮演着什么样的角色。它也许还能告诉我们关于[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上所谓著名机械的信息。
cstorms.155.desc.en:
It was difficult to see the surface of [From.Planet.GetName] through the thick smog still circling above its factories. Much of the planet's surface has been ravaged by cosmic storm damage, leaving large crevices in the homogenous industrial landscape. One of these presented a perfect landing opportunity for our ship.

There is no sign that any attempt was made to dismantle these production facilities. They were simply left behind, and many still contain production material. Analyzing this may allow us to understand what purpose the planet served within the ancient civilization's mercantile infrastructure. It might also tell us more about that celebrated machine referenced on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName].

cstorms.1550.a.zh: 别跟他兜圈子了，摧毁逃生舱。

cstorms.1550.desc.zh:
我们在[From.Planet.GetName]发现一个随风暴逐流的逃生舱。尽管数据签名看起来像是我们的，但可以肯定它不属于我们。我们谨慎地回应了通讯请求，而舱内人员显得尤为高兴。

[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeSheCap]解释称[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe]已经随着风暴拉扯了一段时间，正寻求救援，[event_target:the_imitator.GetHerHis]飞船上的生命维持系统已经濒临崩溃。

当我们要求其表明身份时，这个陌生人却奇怪地声称自己就是我们的船员。这显然是在撒谎，因为我们的船员一个不漏，都在船上。
cstorms.1550.desc.en:
The pod discovered in [From.Planet.GetName] has been left to the mercy of the storm. Even though the data signature it uses looks to be one of ours, the pod is definitely alien. We answered the request for communications cautiously, but we were met with elation by the capsule's inhabitant.

[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeSheCap] explained [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] has been dragged along by the tempest for some time and is seeking rescue, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHerHis] vessel's life support systems on the brink of failure.

When asked to identify themselves, the stranger bizarrely claimed to be a member of our own crew. The lie is painfully obvious, if for no other reason than the fact that everyone on board our ship is accounted for.

cstorms.1555.a.zh: 我们或许能够用得上这样灵活的头脑。

cstorms.1555.b.zh: 提供交通工具送到附近的有人居住的星球。
cstorms.1555.b.en: Provide transport to the nearest inhabited planet.

cstorms.1555.desc.zh:
我们把逃生舱带上船了。我们打开太空舱的封条，真相就揭晓了，里面的外星人立即发出了绝望的请求。

原来这名外星人在对自己母舰的逃生舱进行例行检查时被困在的仓内，并且逃生舱被发射到了太空中。非常不幸的是，船上没有人发现[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe]消失了。

在被困几个月之后，[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe]终于通过一些在逃生舱内能搞到的小东西，向路过的飞船发送一种诱饵信号。然而这也没能吸引到任何援手。更糟的是，一股宇宙风暴席卷了逃生舱，并把它带到了母星系好多光年之外的地方。在孤独和恐惧的驱使下，[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe]想出了一个计划，伪装成发生在附近的任何船只的失踪船员。这位逃生舱的幸存者为他欺骗了我们道歉，但[event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe]很庆幸自己活了下来。
cstorms.1555.desc.en:
We brought the escape pod aboard our ship. The ruse ended as soon as the capsule's seal opened, after which the alien within immediately launched into a desperate plea.

During a routine inspection of the escape pods on [event_target:the_imitator.GetHerHis] mother ship, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] was trapped inside and ejected into space. Sadly, no one aboard their vessel noticed [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] was missing.

Stranded for months, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] used what little tech [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] could find aboard [event_target:the_imitator.GetHerHis] pod to mimic the energy signals of passing ships as a type of lure. However, even this failed to attract help. Worst of all, a cosmic storm took hold of the pod, dragging it lightyears from its home system. Driven to extremes by loneliness and fear, [event_target:the_imitator.GetHeShe] concocted a plan to pose as a missing crew member of any ship that happened by. The pod-dweller apologized for the deception, but is glad to be alive.

cstorms.160.desc.zh:
对[From.Planet.GetName]上所使用的工业原料的初步分析发现其中含有高度爆炸性的组分。这些产品是某种更大流程的一部分，并不能单独使用。这些物质最终通过一个传送带系统运送到一个中央仓库。

从周围的烧灼痕迹来看，这个仓库很明显经常用于行星际货运。现在问题是这些产品要交付到哪里去？鉴于这些货物的爆炸性，收货地址应该不会很远。

我们在附近还发现了几个集装箱。他们显然为了能安全地打包里面的内容物花费了很多功夫，警告标签的残余物依旧还印在集装箱的侧面。标签上只能辨识出一个单词：“关键”。
cstorms.160.desc.en:
Early analysis of the industrial materials at use on [From.Planet.GetName] indicate a highly volatile makeup. These products were part of a larger process, and not to be used on their own. The substances were eventually transported through a system of conveyors towards a centralized collection depot.

From the surrounding scorch marks, it's clear that this depot was in constant use by interplanetary transport. The question is where was the product being delivered? Given the explosive nature of the cargo it could not have been far.

Nearby we discovered several shipping crates. Pains were clearly taken to securely package the contents, as the remnants of warning labels remain printed on the sides. Only one word is still legible: "Critical."

cstorms.1605.desc.zh:
我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]着实费了一番巧劲才登上空间站并重启望远镜，终究还是没有什么能难倒他们。然而，望远镜瞄向的地方并没有什么值得特别注意的东西。

我们发现空间站周围散布着一些有趣的文物，那是望远镜所拍下的清晰照片，它们被放在精美的相框中。这些照片都是关于宇宙风暴的，它们详细记录了经过该恒星系的所有风暴并且每一次都拍摄了多张照片。望远镜操作员更换变焦，从不同角度进行拍摄，甚至还艺术地倾斜镜头来展示风暴最美的景象。

深入调查后，我们在这座废弃站点上的唯一发现就是这些有趣的艺术作品。我们将对它们进行归档，以便让后来人能够欣赏到这些罕见的、充满力量和美感的图像。
cstorms.1605.desc.en:
Boarding the station and activating the telescopes took some finessing from our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural], but it was nothing they could not handle. However, the corner of the galaxy the instruments were pointed at showed nothing of note.

Some interesting artifacts were found scattered around the station: detailed images recorded from the telescopes, neatly presented in decorative frames. Every single capture is focussed on cosmic storms, with multiple prints of each storm that has passed through this system. The telescope operator used different angles, zoom levels, and even artistic tilts to show the storms in their best light.

Upon deeper investigation, the artwork is the only interesting find aboard the abandoned station. We will archive them so many future generations can enjoy these images of rare power and beauty.

cstorms.165.desc.a.zh:
$cstorms.165.intro$

集装箱内的运单上写着“局部扰动抑制器”。我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]并不确定这到底是个什么东西，但根据这个重型集装箱和外面贴的警告来看，一定是件重要的物品。$cstorms.165.outro$
cstorms.165.desc.a.en:
$cstorms.165.intro$

A shipping label on the inside of the crate mentions something called 'Sectoral Disturbance Depressors.' Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] are unsure as to what this means, but given the heavy duty storage container and the warnings plastered on the outside of the crate, it must have been something important.$cstorms.165.outro$

cstorms.165.desc.b.zh:
$cstorms.165.intro$

这个部件一眼看上去就相当眼熟，乘员们拿出在[wm_digsite_A.GetName]上发现的手册进行了对比后发现，集装箱里精心制造的部件就是局部扰动抑制器的一个关键零件。$cstorms.165.outro$
cstorms.165.desc.b.en:
$cstorms.165.intro$

The part immediately looked familiar, and the crew retrieved the manual found on [wm_digsite_A.GetName] to compare. The intricately manufactured object within the crate is a vital component to the Sectoral Disturbance Depressors.$cstorms.165.outro$

cstorms.165.desc.c.zh:
$cstorms.165.intro$

其独特的形状和充满液体的核心表明这应该就是完成[wm_digsite_C.GetName]安装的那个部件。其中的物质想必就是用来为局部扰动抑制器充能的。然而，看起来想要安全地装上这个部件需要专门的知识。$cstorms.165.outro$
cstorms.165.desc.c.en:
$cstorms.165.intro$

Its unique shape and liquid-filled core revealed that this might be the exact part needed to complete the installation on [wm_digsite_C.GetName]. The substance within must be used to power the Sectoral Disturbance Depressors. However, it appears it will require specific knowledge to install it safely.$cstorms.165.outro$

cstorms.165.desc.d.zh:
$cstorms.165.intro$

似乎这就是[wm_digsite_C.GetName]上的局部扰动抑制器所缺失的部件。依据在[wm_digsite_A.GetName]发现的手册，我们应该可以正确地进行安装，并且完成激活。$cstorms.165.outro$
cstorms.165.desc.d.en:
$cstorms.165.intro$

The part seems to be the missing piece from the Sectoral Disturbance Depressors on [wm_digsite_C.GetName]. With the manual found on [wm_digsite_A.GetName], we will be able to properly install it and perhaps finally activate it.$cstorms.165.outro$

cstorms.170.desc.zh:
无尽的狂风肆虐在[From.Planet.GetName]的表面上。如果这还不够具有挑战性，那么白雪覆盖的地面之下还藏着一个怪异的惊喜。

在地表以下，还有一层又一层厚厚的尘土在等待着我们。在其中又发现了曾生活在这颗星球上的生命形式的痕迹。他们都是在同一时间被埋葬的，说明这是一次单一的大灭绝事件。[From.Planet.GetName]生态系统的崩溃必然导致了随后的大气变薄，带入了冰河时代，最终使这颗星球变得一片荒芜。

除了沙砾和冰原，这个地方肯定还有更多的东西，但很明显，地表不会告诉我们更多秘密了。我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]建议深入研究。
cstorms.170.desc.en:
Endless blizzards scour the surface of [From.Planet.GetName]. As if that wasn't challenging enough, the snow-covered landscape concealed a strange surprise.

Layer upon layer of dust awaited us below. Evidence of the life forms that once inhabited this world was found within. All were entombed at the same time, suggesting a singular mass extinction event. The collapse of [From.Planet.GetName]'s ecosystems must have subsequently thinned the atmosphere, bringing about an ice age that has turned the planet into a wasteland.

There must be more to this place than grit and ice sheets, but it is clear that the surface is not going to provide more answers. Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] advise searching deeper.

cstorms.1705.desc.zh:
据报道，在最近的$magnetic_storm$之后，[this.GetName]出现了不寻常的后遗症。风暴的强大能量场增加了行星熔融核心的磁场波动，导致科技基础设施普遍失灵。

然而，这种情况也提供了一个绝无仅有的资源开采机会。地幔下富含金属的熔岩流被带上了电荷，可以在采矿磁铁的帮助下收获。
cstorms.1705.desc.en:
Unusual after effects are being reported on [this.GetName] in the wake of the recent $magnetic_storm$. The storm's potent energy fields increased magnetic volatility in the planet's molten core, resulting in the widespread failure of technological infrastructure.

However, the situation also presents a unique resource extraction opportunity. Metal-rich lava flows underneath the planet's mantle are now electromagnetically charged and can be harvested with the aid of mining magnets.

cstorms.171.desc.zh:
我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]穿上了保护装备，乘坐重型抗寒机械，不久就完成了清除积雪和细尘这种简单重复的工作。很快，我们就发现了奇怪的特征，一系列如树根一般蜿蜒纵横的沟渠在整片土地上蔓延着。

在这些裂缝中，我们发现了各种生物的干枯遗骸，从植物到动物，以及介于之间的所有生物，所有能从地表上找到的一切应有尽有。不知何故，这些沟渠把有机质夹在岩壁之间磨碎，以提取所有有用的营养物质，并将它们运送到一个交汇点，这一过程类似于消化。它们喷出的灰尘如今覆盖了[From.Planet.GetName]的大部分地表。

这下问题就来了，这些裂缝究竟是在饲育谁，或者说什么东西呢。
cstorms.171.desc.en:
Equipped with protective gear and frost-resistant heavy machinery, our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] made short work of the tedious yet simple process of removing the snow and fine dust layers. Soon, strange patterns were discovered, a series of trenches spreading in a root-like pattern covering a vast swath of territory.

Within those crevices we found the desiccated remains of all sorts of organisms; everything it could pull from the planet's surface, from vegetation to wildlife and all that existed between. Somehow, the trenches ground up the organics by pulverizing them between their rocky walls, extracting any useful nutrients and transporting them to a convergence point in a process akin to digestion. The dust they spat back out now covers the majority of [From.Planet.GetName]'s landscapes.

This begs the question as to who, or what the crevices were feeding.

cstorms.1715.desc.aquatic.zh: 这对我们殖民地的生存前景构成严重威胁，必须立即加以解决。
cstorms.1715.desc.aquatic.en: This represents a serious threat for our colony's survival prospects and must be addressed immediately.

cstorms.1715.desc.common.zh: 在最近的$electric_storm$后，[this.GetName]上观察到了一种异常现象。该行星的[GetOceansState]现已充斥着永久性的电流，电流在广阔的水体中循环，对水生生物构成致命威胁。
cstorms.1715.desc.common.en: An unusual phenomenon has been observed on [this.GetName] in the wake of the recent $electric_storm$. The planet's [GetOceansState] have been left charged with a perpetual electrical current now circulating in this vast body of water, posing lethal risks for aquatic life.

cstorms.1715.desc.non_aquatic.zh: 这种现象对我们没有造成直接的伤害，但对我们殖民地的未来发展产生了挑战。
cstorms.1715.desc.non_aquatic.en: This phenomenon is causing us no direct harm but poses challenges to our colony's future development.

cstorms.172.a.zh: 是时候看看这台机器到底是做什么用的了。
cstorms.172.a.en: Time to see what the machines can do.

cstorms.172.desc.a.zh:
$cstorms.172.intro$这些应该就是[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上面所提到的机器。很遗憾的是，我们缺乏可以理解这些装置内部复杂的工作机制所需的知识。不仅如此，在其中一台机器的基部所发现的控制台显然也缺失了关键的部件。在一块小小的牌匾上雕刻着一行小字“局部扰动抑制器”。

如果我们能够激活这些机器，就能够发现它们的用途。为此，我们需要探索剩下的坐标。$cstorms.172.outro$
cstorms.172.desc.a.en:
$cstorms.172.intro$ They must be the machines mentioned on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]. Unfortunately, we lack the knowledge required to understand the complex inner workings of these devices. Not only that, but the control console discovered at the base of one of the machines is clearly missing vital components. Engraved on a small plaque are the words "Sectoral Disturbance Depressors."

If we can activate the machines we may finally uncover their purpose. To do so we will need to explore the remaining coordinates. $cstorms.172.outro$

cstorms.172.desc.b.zh:
$cstorms.172.intro$

我们在[wm_digsite_A.GetName]上发现的手册的图示看起来与我们面前的这台装置一致，也就是说，这些就是所谓的局部扰动抑制器，而这也就是[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上面发现的风暴庇护所所提到的机械装置。

说明书指出，这些机器需要某个控制面板才能操作。我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]在其中一台机器的基部发现了这个控制面板，但似乎缺少了关键部件。但我们还有一组坐标还未探索，也许其中就藏着解决这个困境的方法。$cstorms.172.outro$
cstorms.172.desc.b.en:
$cstorms.172.intro$ 

The schematics we observed in the manual found on [wm_digsite_A.GetName] seem to match the instruments in front of us, which must mean that these are the Sectoral Disturbance Depressors, and that this is the machine installation mentioned in the storm shelter found on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName].

The manual indicates that these machines require a control panel to be operated. Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] spotted it at the foot of one of the machines, but it seems to be missing a vital part. However, we have one set of coordinates left unexplored, which could hold the means to solve this predicament. $cstorms.172.outro$

cstorms.172.desc.c.zh:
$cstorms.172.intro$

这一定就是[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上所提到的那台被称为局部扰动抑制器的机器！不仅如此，我们在[wm_digsite_B.GetName]找到的机械部件也可以轻易地装入其中一台机器基部的控制面板。

然而，这个部件非常复杂且历史悠久，盲目尝试进一步修理是很危险的。我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]建议在继续推进之前搜寻更多的信息。$cstorms.172.outro$
cstorms.172.desc.c.en:
$cstorms.172.intro$ 

These must be the machines mentioned on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName], dubbed the Sectoral Disturbance Depressors! What's more, the machine part we found on [wm_digsite_B.GetName] was easily slotted into a control panel at the foot of one of the machines.

However, any attempt at further repairs is risky given the complexity and age of the component parts. Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] recommend searching for more information before proceeding. $cstorms.172.outro$

cstorms.172.desc.d.zh:
$cstorms.172.intro$

这些毫无疑问就是[wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName]上所提到的机器了，同时也是[wm_digsite_A.GetName]上的手册所阐述的对象，如今我们也知道它被称为局部扰动抑制器。我们现在需要做的就是将[wm_digsite_B.GetName]上找到的部件装上去，并且希望这台机器仍然能够运转。只有那样我们才能最终发现其用途。$cstorms.172.outro$
cstorms.172.desc.d.en:
$cstorms.172.intro$ 

These are without a doubt the machines mentioned on [wm_storm_shelter_planet.GetName], as well as the subjects of the manual from [wm_digsite_A.GetName], now known as the Sectoral Disturbance Depressors. All that is left to do is install the part we found on [wm_digsite_B.GetName] and hope the machines are still operational. Only then will we finally uncover their purpose. $cstorms.172.outro$

cstorms.1725.a.zh: 用泥土填满峡谷。死者将被埋葬。
cstorms.1725.a.en: Fill the canyon with earth. The dead will stay buried.

cstorms.1725.desc.common.zh: 在最近[this.solar_system.GetName]的$shroud_storm$事件后，[owner.GetColonistPlural]报告称在某个孤立的峡谷中发现了难以解释的神秘现象。幽灵般的蓝色身影短暂出现，似乎无法或不愿与我们的[owner.GetColonistPlural]互动，只是漫无目的地徘徊，随后消失。
cstorms.1725.desc.common.en: Following the recent $shroud_storm$ in [this.solar_system.GetName], [owner.GetColonistPlural] report inexplicable sightings of ethereal apparitions in an isolated canyon. These ghostly blue figures appear briefly, unable or unwilling to interact with our [owner.GetColonistPlural], wandering aimlessly before dissipating.

cstorms.1725.desc.default.zh: 截止目前为止，没有人身伤害或损害的报告。尽管如此，这种奇怪的现象还是令人不安地分散了人们的注意力。
cstorms.1725.desc.default.en: No physical harm or damage has thus far been reported. Nonetheless, the strange phenomenon is proving to be an unsettling distraction.

cstorms.1725.desc.gestalt.zh: 截止目前为止，没有进一步的人身伤害或损害的报告。
cstorms.1725.desc.gestalt.en: No physical harm or aggressive behavior has thus far been reported.

cstorms.1725.desc.psionic.zh: 虽然这些幽灵在本质上似乎是灵能体，但我们仍无法与这些实体建立任何数量的精神交流。然而，我们发现他们的存在是对我们心灵感应能力的被动强化。
cstorms.1725.desc.psionic.en: While the apparitions appear to be psionic in nature, we have not been able to establish any amount of mental communication with these entities. However, we have found their presence to be a passive reinforcement to our own telepathic abilities.

cstorms.1725.desc.psionic_robot.zh: 虽然这些幽灵在本质上似乎是灵能体，但我们仍无法与他们建立任何灵能交流。然而，系统检查倒是能确认他们的出现给我们的心灵感应能力带来了积极的帮助。
cstorms.1725.desc.psionic_robot.en: While the apparitions appear to be psionic in nature, we have not been able to establish any psionic communication with these entities. However, system checks have confirmed that their presence provides passive reinforcement to our own telepathic abilities.

cstorms.1725.desc.spiritualist.zh: 这一非凡现象提醒我们，我们的生存中有着无形的奇迹。
cstorms.1725.desc.spiritualist.en: This remarkable phenomenon is providing a welcome reminder of the intangible wonders of our existence.

cstorms.1735.desc.zh:
最近的[this.GetAffectedStormType]残留的辐射导致[this.GetName]上的地质活动变得异常。

尤其值得注意的是，风暴的影响使得一座活火山不再活跃，将其与地质学上的热点隔离，切断了岩浆供应。

由于冷却的岩浆开拓了新的土地，进一步开发这颗行星的新机遇因这些变化而呈现于我们面前。
cstorms.1735.desc.en:
The residual radiation from the recent [this.GetAffectedStormType] has led to erratic geological activity across [this.GetName].

Most notably, the impact of the storm has rendered an active volcano extinct, cutting it off from its geological hotspot and severing the supply of magma.

These changes present us with new opportunities to develop the planet further, as the cooling magma opens up new lands.

cstorms.1745.desc.zh:
一场严重的$gravity_storm$导致了[this.GetName]的地景发生了剧变。这场风暴强劲的重力波动将行星最高的山脉从构造架上剥离，径直提到了星球的上方。

它现在仍然悬浮在上层大气中，由风暴的残余引力作用保持在高空。这一剧变使得地下基岩中以前无法开采的矿物贮藏暴露了出来，也为[owner.GetResearchers]提供了很多可以分析的资料。
cstorms.1745.desc.en:
A severe $gravity_storm$ caused an extraordinary transformation of [this.GetName]'s landscape. The storm's powerful gravitational fluctuations severed the planet's largest mountain range from its tectonic shelf, lifting it vertically above the planet.

It remains suspended in the upper atmosphere, held aloft by a residual gravitational effect of the storm. This remarkable upheaval has exposed previously inaccessible ore reserves in the bedrock underneath, as well as providing [owner.GetResearchers] with much to analyze.

cstorms.1755.desc.celestial.zh: 高浓度超热星尘严重地影响了两极地区，$cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$
cstorms.1755.desc.celestial.en: Large concentrations of superheated celestial dust have heavily impacted the polar regions, $cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$

cstorms.1755.desc.common.zh: 近期的[this.GetAffectedStormType]对[this.GetName]的气候产生了意想不到的影响。
cstorms.1755.desc.common.en: The recent [this.GetAffectedStormType] has had an unexpected impact on the climate of [this.GetName].

cstorms.1755.desc.electric.zh: 大气中积聚的电荷导致了两极地区的剧烈温度变化。$cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$
cstorms.1755.desc.electric.en: The increased electrical charge in the atmosphere has led to a drastic temperature shift in the polar region, $cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$

cstorms.1755.desc.gravity.zh: 风暴带来的重力变化将许多水下冰层撕裂，$cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$
cstorms.1755.desc.gravity.en: The gravitational shifts brought on by the storm have shattered multiple layers of subaquatic ice, $cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$

cstorms.1755.desc.magnetic.zh: 产生的行星磁场扰动导致了剧烈的地震运动，$cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$
cstorms.1755.desc.magnetic.en: The resulting disturbances in the planets magnetic fields have led to drastic seismic shifts, $cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$

cstorms.1755.desc.particle.zh: 大气中积聚的电荷导致了两极地区的剧烈温度变化。$cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$
cstorms.1755.desc.particle.en: The corrosive effect of the storm's particles has heavily impacted the polar regions, $cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$

cstorms.1755.desc.solar.zh: 风暴的极端热量在其持续期间内提升了整颗行星的温度，$cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$
cstorms.1755.desc.solar.en: The extreme heat of the storm raised the temperatures across the planet throughout its duration, $cstorms.1755.desc.common_2$

cstorms.176.desc.zh:
最后一块拼图终于找到了，我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]开始忙碌了起来。[wm_digsite_B.GetName]上的部件严丝合缝地插入了一块控制面板。[wm_digsite_A.GetName]上的手册引导我们进行正确的安装。刚一装好，三台机器霎时间活动了起来。

雷鸣般的震响振落了高原上的尘与雪，又在一声闪电般的爆鸣中一位[Root.Owner.GetScientist]瞬间蒸发了，那具躯体化作的尘埃旋涡迅速被吸进那一道道通向行业干扰抑制器的沟渠中。

这就是[wm_digsite_C.GetName]上发生的事情的关键所在：通往机器底部的沟槽是燃料管道，会吸收周围的生物质。其结果就是在整颗星球上留下毁灭的痕迹。

局部扰动抑制器现已全面激活，剩下的燃料还够一次性使用。我们需要做的就是按下按钮。
cstorms.176.desc.en:
The last piece of the puzzle found, our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] got to work. The component from [wm_digsite_B.GetName] slotted neatly into a control console. The manual from [wm_digsite_A.GetName] was employed to install it correctly. Once this was done, all three machines burst into life.

Thunderous vibrations shook the dust and snow from the plateau. With a crackle like that of lightning a [Root.Owner.GetScientist] was instantly vaporized, the swirl of dust that was once a body quickly sucked into the trenches towards the Sectoral Disturbance Depressors.

Herein lies the key to what happened on [wm_digsite_C.GetName]: the trenches leading to the bottom of the machines are fuel lines, drawing in the bio-matter of their surroundings. The result is a trail of destruction across the planet.

The Sectoral Disturbance Depressors are now fully operational. There is enough fuel left for a single use. All that remains is the push of a button.

cstorms.1761.desc.common.zh: 我们在[this.GetName]的[Owner.GetEngineerPlural]汇报$celestial_storm$它对水过滤系统有不利影响。随着颗粒在星球地下水中沉淀，形成的矿浆堵塞了关键的基础设施。
cstorms.1761.desc.common.en: Our [Owner.GetEngineerPlural] on [this.GetName] report that the $celestial_storm$ is having adverse effects on water filtration systems. As the particles settle in the planet's groundwater, the resulting mineral slurry is clogging key infrastructure points.

cstorms.1761.desc.default.zh:
由此导致的水培故障严重影响了星球上的农业，也导致了安全饮用水的短缺。

这个问题如果不加以处理，可能会对我们的供水造成长期的影响。幸运的是，我们的[owner.GetEngineerPlural]有信心他们可以创造更强大的过滤系统来解决这个问题。
cstorms.1761.desc.default.en:
The resulting hydroponic failures are heavily impacting the planet's agriculture, as well as leading to shortages in safe drinkable water.

This problem could have long-lasting consequences on our water supply if not dealt with. Fortunately, our [owner.GetEngineerPlural] are confident they can create more robust filtration systems to address the issue.

cstorms.1761.desc.lithoid.zh: 在研究水培堵塞的过程中，我们的[Owner.GetColonistPlural]发现，矿化的浆液本身对石质生理学人口实际上既美味又有营养。在对殖民地的过滤系统进行了一些小调整之后，它们大量生产了一种新的季节性饮料，可以供应到风暴结束。
cstorms.1761.desc.lithoid.en: While investigating the hydroponic blockages, our [Owner.GetColonistPlural] discovered that the mineralized slurry itself is actually both delicious and nutritious when consumed by those with lithoid physiology. After making a few minor adjustments to the colony's filtration systems they have mass-produced a new seasonal drink with which to wait out the storm.

cstorms.1765.desc.zh:
[Owner.GetEngineerPlural]解决了[this.GetName]上的水培阻塞和用水短缺的问题。殖民地的水供应网络得到了升级，现在可以滤去$celestial_storm$所带来的复杂杂质。

这些对用水基础设施的改进还可以用来提升[Owner.GetName]上的灌溉作业。
cstorms.1765.desc.en:
The [Owner.GetEngineerPlural] have dealt with the hydroponic blockages and water shortages on [this.GetName]. The colony's water supply network has been improved and can now filter out complex impurities such as those introduced by the $celestial_storm$.

These improvements to our water infrastructure can be repurposed to improve irrigation efforts across the [Owner.GetName].

cstorms.1771.c.zh: 把这些生物放入保护区。
cstorms.1771.c.en: Place the creatures in a reserve.

cstorms.1771.desc.common.zh:
[this.GetName]上的[Owner.GetScientistPlural]们观察到$gravity_storm$对当地野生鸟类带来了严重的影响。

风暴带来的重力波动导致了异常的大气条件，让许多鸟类物种无法飞行。
cstorms.1771.desc.common.en:
The [Owner.GetScientistPlural] on [this.GetName] have observed harsh repercussions of the $gravity_storm$ on the local avian wildlife.

The gravitational fluctuations brought on by the storm are leading to erratic atmospheric conditions, rendering several species of avian fauna incapable of flight.

cstorms.1771.desc.default.zh:
这不仅使它们无法正常捕猎，也更容易受到捕食者攻击。

有人担心，如果我们不加以干预，这些受影响的物种可能会被赶尽杀绝。
cstorms.1771.desc.default.en:
Not only is this preventing the creatures unable to hunt as normal, it is also leaving them vulnerable to predators.

There is concern that the afflicted species may be hunted to extinction if we do not intervene.

cstorms.1771.desc.swarm.zh: 真正的盛宴等待着我们。

cstorms.1771.evopred.zh: 在事态结束之前保存它们的基因物质。
cstorms.1771.evopred.en: Save their DNA before the end.

cstorms.1776.desc.zh:
紧接着$gravity_storm$过境之后，[this.GetName]上暂时无法飞行的在我们的鸟类保护区内避难，又一次翱翔天空。

虽然许多动物现在已经回到了它们以前的栖息地，但仍有相当数量的动物留在保护区，似乎在享受保护区提供的舒适和保护。

这为近距离研究这颗星球上的野生鸟类提供了一个独特的机会。
cstorms.1776.desc.en:
Following the passing of the $gravity_storm$, the temporarily flightless fauna of [this.GetName] have taken to the skies again having taken shelter inside our avian reserve.

While many of the creatures have now returned to their former habitats, significant numbers remain in the reserve, seemingly enjoying the comforts and protections it provides.

This presents a unique opportunity to study the planet's avian wildlife at close proximity.

cstorms.180.desc.zh:
在揭示了局部扰动抑制器的秘密之后，关于因内特贸易体的线索似乎就中断了。然而，对数据的彻底重新评估又提供了一些新的见解。

[wm_digsite_A.GetName]上的贸易记录表明，这些人保有高度的平等主义信仰。这个结论的依据是他们拥有很高的生活标准以及行星上留存的大量奢侈品工厂；每位公民，无论其职业、社会地位或血统如何，都享有平等的舒适和机会。

在[wm_digsite_B.GetName]上，我们发现了详细描述每个工厂用例的索引。这些都是更大的生产链的一部分，用于为这个庞大的帝国提供必要的手段来维持其富裕的生活方式。要公平地分配这些利益，就必须以惊人的速度消耗大量的材料和食物。

[wm_digsite_C.GetName]上修复好的行业干扰抑制器在完全报废之前又提供了更多的洞见。虽然其功能的确切目的仍然是一个谜，但至少我们寻回了一个可追踪的数据信号；这些机器的目标不是一个自由运动的实体。

我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]建议在附近的区域寻找与这个信号相匹配的反应。
cstorms.180.desc.en:
After uncovering the secrets of the Sectoral Disturbance Suppressors, the trail about the Inetian Traders' fate went cold. However, a thorough reassessment of the data provided some new insights.

Trading records from [wm_digsite_A.GetName] demonstrate that these people held strong egalitarian beliefs. This conclusion is backed by the high standard of living and plentiful luxury facilities still left on the planet; with a small degree of variance, every citizen enjoyed an equal share of comfort and opportunity, no matter their profession, social standing, or lineage.

On [wm_digsite_B.GetName], we found indexes detailing the use case of each factory. These were all part of much larger production chains, set up to provide the vast empire with the necessary means to support its opulent lifestyle. Equal distribution of these benefits necessitated a truly staggering amount of material and food consumption, produced at breakneck speeds.

[wm_digsite_C.GetName]'s repaired Sectoral Disturbance Depressors provided some more insights before being fully decommissioned. While the exact purpose of their function is still a mystery, a traceable data signal was recovered; the machines were not aimed at a freely moving entity.

Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] recommend searching nearby sectors for a matching response to this signal.

cstorms.1801.desc.zh: 扫描发现，在[from.GetName]中的[fromfrom.GetName]的中心出现了不规则现象，表明该构造的中心携带着一个奇怪的物质。这些不寻常的读数值得在风暴消散或离开该恒星系之前进行更深入的调查。
cstorms.1801.desc.en: Scans detect irregularities in the eye of [fromfrom.GetName] raging in [from.GetName], indicating that the formation is carrying a strange mass at its center. These unusual readings warrant closer investigation, before the storm dissipates or leaves the system.

cstorms.1805.desc.zh:
通过进入[from.GetName]的宇宙风暴眼，[leader.GetName]发现了我们扫描不规则的原因。这场不寻常的风暴是由巨大的中心[from.star.GetEarnedResources]聚集所推动的。

我们的科研船在被猛烈地弹射出去之前收获了可以收集的资源。传感器的数据将帮助我们的工程师在极端风暴条件下提高船只的性能。
cstorms.1805.desc.en:
By navigating into the eye of the cosmic storm in [from.GetName], [leader.GetName] discovered the cause of our scan irregularities. This unusual storm is being fueled by a huge central concentration of [from.star.GetEarnedResources].

Our science ship harvested what resources could be gathered before being violently ejected. The sensor data from their narrow withdrawal will aid our engineers in improving vessel performance under extreme storm conditions.

cstorms.1805.desc.traumatized.zh: 不幸的是，这种危险的折磨对[leader.GetName]产生了持久的影响。
cstorms.1805.desc.traumatized.en: Unfortunately, this dangerous ordeal has had a lasting impact on [leader.GetName].

cstorms.181.desc.zh:
乍看上去[From.Planet.GetName]似乎一切正常。它和星系中随处可见的数百颗其他同类星球别无二致，也没有发现这个信号具体是从什么地方发出来的指示。没有可见的信号发射机，也没有足够强大的技术痕迹，可以从其他系统接收到它的呼叫。

我们的搜寻仍在继续。
cstorms.181.desc.en:
At first glance, nothing [From.Planet.GetName] appears out of place. A planet like hundreds of others, found all over the galaxy. Nor is there any indication of where exactly the signal is coming from. There is no visible transmitter or piece of technology strong enough to have its call registered from systems away.

We continue our search.

cstorms.1816.desc.zh:
一个神秘的太空舱飘在[from.GetName]中。它看起来没有任何攻击能力并且对我们的信号毫无反应。

初步扫描显示它受损的外部是用先进的材料和陌生的工程科技建造的。需要进一步分析。
cstorms.1816.desc.en:
A mysterious capsule is adrift in [from.GetName]. It has no obvious offensive capability and is unresponsive to our signals.

Initial scans show that its damaged exterior is constructed using advanced materials and unfamiliar engineering techniques. Further analysis is needed.

cstorms.182.desc.zh:
在抵达地表后，我们很快发现，收到的信号强弱取决于我们的位置。根据这个简单的规律，我们终于找到了行星另一侧的一座高耸的山峰。

我们越是接近那些若隐若现的山脉，土地就变得愈发地荒芜、贫瘠而破败，仿佛有一股毁灭性的力量撕裂了大地。根据破坏的特征，我们认为这个地方曾被宇宙尘暴袭击过。然而，如果这是真的，那么应该整颗星球都受到影响才合乎逻辑。我们以前从未见过风暴会造成如此集中的破坏。要了解更多，就必须登上这座高耸的山峰。
cstorms.182.desc.en:
After arriving on the surface, we soon discovered that the signal became stronger or weaker depending on our position. Following this simple pattern, we were led at last to a towering mountain range on the far side of the planet.

As we approached the looming mountains, the landscape grew ever more blasted, barren, ruined, as if a devastating force had ripped across this part of the world. Based on the damage pattern, we believe this place was at some point ravaged by a cosmic dust storm. However, if that were true, it would be logical to conclude the whole planet would be affected. Never before have we seen such concentrated destruction from such a tempest. To learn more, it will be necessary to scale the imposing peaks.

cstorms.1820.a.zh: 这里有很多值得学习的东西。
cstorms.1820.a.en: There is much to learn here.

cstorms.1820.desc.zh:
[this.leader.GetName]相信飘过[solar_system.GetName]星系的神秘太空舱是一种古老的“风暴陷阱”，可能曾是一个更大的防御系统的一部分。

这个设备的进气口密封得很紧，但我们的扫描显示它里面藏有被俘获其中的高度压缩的宇宙风暴能量和物质。

研究如何这个非凡的容器可能会教会我们很多关于抑制风暴的知识，但也有释放其蕴含的所有能量的风险。
cstorms.1820.desc.en:
[this.leader.GetName] believes that the mysterious capsule drifting through the [solar_system.GetName] system is an ancient "storm trap", which may have once been part of a larger defense grid.

The device's intake port is sealed tightly, but our readings suggest it is holding the compressed energy and matter of a captive cosmic storm inside.

Finding a way to open this remarkable container may teach us a great deal about storm mitigation, although at the risk of releasing whatever forces are currently contained within.

cstorms.1826.desc.zh:
[leader.GetName]完成了对古老风暴陷阱工作原理的分析，并解开了其输入装置。随着端口打开，[from.GetStormType]内部的风暴被释放到[solar_system.GetName]星系的虚空中。

对陷阱复杂工程的研究已经对抗风暴材料和结构产生了惊人的洞见，尽管我们仍然不明白这个装置是如何能够完全控制风暴的。这些知识将极大地帮助我们抵御未来的宇宙扰动。
cstorms.1826.desc.en:
[leader.GetName] completed analysis of the ancient storm trap's workings and was able to unlock its intake mechanism. As the ports opened, the [from.GetStormType] held inside was released into the void of the [solar_system.GetName] system.

Study of the trap's complex engineering has produced fascinating insights into storm-resistant materials and structures, though we still do not understand how the device is capable of containing storms entirely. This knowledge will greatly aid us in weathering future cosmic disturbances.

cstorms.1826.storm_tt.zh: [solar_system.GetName]星系中诞生了一场小规模的低等级$default_storm$
cstorms.1826.storm_tt.en: A small, low-level $default_storm$ spawns in the [solar_system.GetName] system

cstorms.183.desc.zh:
被破坏的山脉由许多的山峰和山谷组成，但一个形状奇怪的陨石坑很快就引起了我们的注意。它的坑壁光滑，围绕着中心有一系列同心圆被刻在大地上。

当我们下到坑里的时候，感觉到有一股强大的力量拉扯着，这股力量毫无疑问地指向了同心圆的圆心。一缕缕闪烁的能量从圆环中升起，其中一些飘得很远，最终逃离了行星的大气层。这就是信号的源头。

我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]建议分析陨石坑及其能量波动，以便更好地了解这里发生了什么。
cstorms.183.desc.en:
The ravaged mountain range consisted of many peaks and valleys, but one oddly shaped crater caught our attention very early on. The walls of the pit were smooth, and in its center a number of concentric rings were carved into the ground.

As we descended into the bowl, we began to feel the pull of a deeply compelling force, inescapable and unmistakably coming from the circle's origin point. Strands of flickering energy arose from the rings, some drifting so far off they eventually escaped the planet's atmosphere. This is the source of the signal.

Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] suggest analyzing the crater and its energy fluctuations in order to better understand what happened here.

cstorms.1835.desc.zh:
[this.GetSpeciesNamePlural]，我们深表同情！我们目睹了一场大风暴在[this.GetName]肆虐。

听到那里遭到的破坏，我们当然感到非常难过。我们哭了，我们真的哭了！所以，请允许我们帮个忙……这是一笔特别的一次性超级交易！

我们可以提供一些小工具，一流的小工具。是我们能给的最好的！有了这些，当下一次风暴来临时，你就能做好准备了。那么我们成交吧？
cstorms.1835.desc.en:
Commiserations, [this.GetSpeciesNamePlural]! We chanced to see a big storm wreaking havoc in [this.GetName].

Of course, we were very sad to hear of the damage done there. We cried, indeed we cried! So please, allow us to help... with a special one time super deal!

We can provide gadgets, first class gadgets. Only the best from us! With these, when the next storm comes, you will be ready. So do we have a deal?

cstorms.184.desc.zh:
